SUTRA (50) WHAT IS SUBSERVIENT TO THE PURPOSES OF THE SACRIFICE SHOULD BE DONE, BECAUSE IT IS A SUBORDINATE FACTOR Bhāsya The Hypothetical Inquiry continues |– In connection with the same Bone-sacrifice’ the following question 18 going to be considered-At the Archetypal sacrifice the Udumbara Post Is as tall as the sacrificer’ and ’the sacrificer touches the Shukra-vessel’ at the Bono-sacrifice (assuming that it is performed by the Bones] should such acts as these be performed–or not ? L The Purvapakṣa view is that the Bones being inanimate things, they cannot, by themselves, do any act at all, and hence in the measuring of the Post’ and ’the touching of the Shukra’ they cannot be the per- formers.” In answer to this, we have the following–Siddhania–What is sub- servient to the purposes of the sacrifice should be done, because it is a sub- ordinate factor, acts like those in question, which subserve the purposes of the sacrifice, should be done, because in this case the Sacrificer’ 18 & subordinate factor, what is needed at the sacrifice is (a) the Udumbara- Post measured to be as tall as the sacrificer, and (b) the Shukra that has been touched by the Sacrificer, and (a) the measuring can be done with the inanimate bonos also, (b) so also can the touching of the Shukra Hence it follows that acts like these should be doue+ 4 ADHIKARANA (20): At the Bone-sacrifice’, Prospective acts’ shall not be performed-(Hypothetical Discussion). C SUTRA (51).

THE PROSPECTIVE ACTS ARE NOT TO BE PERFORMED BECAUSE THERE CAN BE NO KNOWLEDGE OF THE DESIRE (FOR RESULTS), JI’ST AS THERE IS NO KNOWLEDGE OF THE DESIRE OF OTHER PERFORMERS ALSO UNTIL THEY ARE MENTIONED Bhāsya There is the Jyotųętoma acrifice. in connection with which, we read- - ‘If one desire that the Rain-god should ram, he should measure out the assembly-room (Sadas) on a low level’, etc, ete

The question that arises is At the Bone-sacrifice, which has the Jyotiatoma for its Archetype, and which therefore takes in the details of the latter, according to the General Law should, or should not, such prospec - tive acts (acts performed with a definite resuh in view), be performed ’ The Pūrvapaksa view is as follows In accordance with the General Law, it should be done -Objection But the Bones cannot desure any thing, while all such acts are performed by reason of the sacrificer entertaining the desire for definite results —Answer-In such cases, it is not necessary that the Sacrificer should have the desire for the results, the meaning of the text in *If the assemble-rooni is measured out at a low level, there is rain’, so that whenever rain is needed (by anyone) the Assembly Room should be measured out at a low level, and the much-needed rain will follow ·

In answer to this, we have the following Siddhånta • Prospective acts like those in question shall not be performed. Why?* What meant is that if the sacrificer desires rain, rain comes if the Assembly Room 18 measured out at a low level’, on account of the Atman pada ending (in ‘kāmayēta”) the unplication is that the main act along with all its subsidiary details is conducive to bringing rewards to the Sacrificer; and it cannot bring it to others desiring it. In the case in question, it cannot be known that the Sacrifice (who has been assumed to be the Skeleton) desires the rain as his reward; even in the case of living sacrificers, when the desire us there, it is not known until he mentions it,–what to say of the Bones (which are inanimate)? And when the desire itself is absent in them, the acts prompted by that desire cannot be performed. ADHIKARANA (21): At the ‘Bone-sacrifice’, there shall be no ‘invoking of blessings’ along with the ‘Suktavāka (Hypothetical Discussion). SUTRA (52) THE INVOKING ALSO OF DESIRED BLESSINGS AS CONTAINED IN

  • SUKTAVĀKA SHALL NOT BE DONE BECAUSE OF • ABSENCE Bhās a

7 In connection with the Bone-sacrifice there are certain acts performed, like the Prāyaṇiya, which have the Darsha-Pūrnamisa for their Archetype, and which come into the Bone sacrifice by the General Law At these acts, the reciting of the Nüktarūka also comes in by virtue of the General Law; tlas Sūktavāka contains the following words Ayam yajamāna āyurāshastë, suprajāstvamāshāstē, vishvam priyamūshūstē yadanēna kavrši ūshūstē tada- skyät tad dadhyûl tadasmai dēvūrūsattām` |‘This sacrificer destres longevity, ho desires excellent progeny, etc. etc ‘] The question that arises IN Should, or should not, thus ‘invoking of blessing” be done at the Bone-sacrifice ? The most reasonable answer that presents itself is as follows · The blessings that are invoked in course of the Sûktarāka should not be invoked. **Why * Because of absence of the desiring person, the Bones do not demure anything, as has been already pointed out hence the invokings should not be done.

Instead of reading Süktāraki”, the Sutra has read Süktavākarat”. Why do you explain it like that * The answer is that the invoking of the blessings is that which finds place in the Sūktavāka, hence the affix ‘razhi’ is taken as signifying this `finding place : that such interpretation is permissible has been shown under Sũ 10 5 88 below, hence it means no attack on the Sutra, SUTRA (53) [Pūrvapakṣin’s objection |- * THE INVOKINGS SHOULD BE DONE. BECAUSE " THE STATEMENT IS PURELY DECLAMATORY Bhāṣya “It is not as you say that in the case of the Bones (performing the sacrifice) the invoking of the blesangs should not be done; as a matter of fart, the invokings should be done, because the statement is purely declamatory: that is, the invoking of the blessings must be done why 1-because the statement is purely declamatory: the whole of the passage- ‘He desires longevity, etc. is purely declamatory; there are no injunctions here, they 1718 9HABARA BHIİŞYA: are only declamations; and because they are declamations, the fact of their coming in at the performance is indicated by the General Law. Hence if this invoking 18 done, the General Law becomes obeyed. Hence we ‘conclude that the mvoking of the blessings should be done.” SUTRA (54). [Answer]-NOT SO; BECAUSE THEY SIGNIFY DESIRE, AND THERE IS NO SUCH DESIRE (IN THE BONEs) as THERE IS IN OTHERS. Bhāsya. It is not as you say–that the invoking of blessings should be done’. Why “–Because they signify desire, L.e. the invocations in question speak of desire, the words ’the sacrificer dares longevity, etc., etc ‘-are used only when the desire has netually appeared, in the caso in question however, there is no such sacrificer as would entertain the desire for the blessings spoken of, the Bones are inanimate things, and Bones can have no desire. this is what is meant by the phrase there is no such desire”,— 1e there is no such desire in the Bones, - as there in others, 1e in living persons, thusse desires do appear: never in the Bones Hence we conclude that in the case of the Bones (being the sacriticers), there should be no invoking of the blessings *L But we have said that these assertions are declamatory ** The answer to that 18 that they are not declamatory, these are injunc» tive. hence the objection urged becomes refuted; so that what you have said that for the Bones, the in:oking of the blessings should be done, is not right; as a matter of fact, it should not be done, thus 15 what is meant by the Sutra-Not so, because they signify desire and there is no auch desire in the Bones as there is in others. ADHIKARANA (22): At the Bone-sacrifice, there should be no performance of the • Hotṛ-Kāmas’ (acts con- tingent upon the Hotr’s desire)—— (Hypothetical Discussion). SUTRA (55). [PORYAPAKSA - THE HOT-KIMA’ ACTS SHOULD BE DONE Rhāṣya The Drūdashāha’ and other Sattras form the subject matter of this Adhikarina, in reference to these, we read Tatah samvatsari asthān yā jauēt” | Thin at the end of the year, one should make the Bones perform the sacrifice . under the General Law, Initiation and other rites also become admissible at these Sattras –and further, at the Archetype, ther Po certain Hotrkāma” gets, laid down in the text Yam kāmayēta apashu- man ayādīti parichīm tasyēdāmupakviyēt, apashumānēva bharatı, yam kāma- yeta pramāyukah syādīti tasyochchavstarām vasat kuryāt, etc etc : Where certain acts are laid down as to be done by the Hoir-priest, in the event of ls desiring certain results to befall the Sacrificer, hence these acts are called Hot kāma ‘| In regard to these, there arises the question Should these Hotr-Kāma sets be done or not in the ease of Bones (performing the sacrifice) " Objection It has been settled that the sacrifice can be performed only by the living persons (Vide above Sũ 47 et seq)” Answer We start this enquiry on the assumption (taking it for grantedi that the sacrifice may be performed by the Bones. The How- On this question, the Pürvupaksa starts with the Sutra Kāma acts should be done in the case of the Bones Why? Because thes General Law makes them admissible, hence their performance would mean obedience to the tieneral Law, hence we conclude that the Hotr-Kāma nets should be done SCTRA (36). NOT SO BECAUSE THEY INVOLVE THE INVOKING OF BLESSINGS UPON HIN Bhasya. This not right: you have said that the Hotr-Kāma acts should be done, as a matter of fact, they should not be done.-Why? BecauRS they involve the invoking of blessings upon him, it 18 an invocation of blessings upon the sacrificer; as it has been declared that- Whatever blessings the Priests invoke at a sacrifice, they all pertain to the sacrificer’, which shows that the blessings in question also should pertain to the 1720 SHABARA-BHĀṆYA: Sacrificer. In the case in question however, there is no ‘sacrificer’; the Bones (that are supposed to be the performers of the sacrifice) are inanimate things; and hence the Bones have not the capacity to desire anything It has been established under Su. 6. 1. 5 that a person to be entitled to perform an act should be desirous of something and should be capable of performing that act -From all these we conclude that in the case of the Bone-sacrifice the Hotṛ-Kāma’ acts should not be performed.

All the hypothetical discussions (Adhikaranas 18-22) have been finished. Their purpose need not be explained All that is necessary to do is to reiterate that the acts in question should not be performed, as it involves the inporing of blessings upon the sacrificer. C ADHIKARAŅA (23): The Sarvasvāra Sacrifice’ should be completed, even after the death of the sacrificer, SUTRA (37). [PURVAPAKYA]—” WHEN THE SACRIFICER HAS DIED, THE ‘SARVASVĀBA * SHOULD NOT BE COMPLETED, AS EVERY ACT IS RELATED TO A LIVING PERSON Bhānya. ** There is the Sarvasvāra suerifice, known as the * Shunahkarna Agnıştoma”. laid down in the text Desiring one’s own death, one should perform tlas sacritice, if he wishes that he should reach the Heavenly Region, without any disease * [At the Third Extraction of this serifer, the sacrificer throws himself into the Fire after having requested the priests to complete the performance of the sacrifice | In regard to this, there arises the question When the Sacrificer has ded, should the performance be left off at that point? Or should it be carried on to its completion?

At the Sarvasvāra, after the The Pūrvpaket view is as follows sacrificer has diod, the performance should be left off at that point, because the act in related to a living person, Le, an act can be performed only by a living person, not by a dead one and this implies that when one performs the Sarvasvāru, one should perform it only to the point of the sacrificer’s death “. " SUTRA (58) IN REALITY, THERE MUST BE [COMPLETION] BECAUSE BOTH HAVE BEEN DIRECTLY ENJOINED Bhasya

There musl b it completion, because both " have been directly eagoined the Sacrifice as well as its completion.-m the following text Dearing death, one should perform this sacrifice where the verb clearly means that having begun the performance of the Sacrifice, one should complete it ; hence the completion also is denoted by the verb itself Then Agam, there the text · Arbhavi prastûyamāni audumbarim parito’ dushēna vākamā par vēstya brühmanāk parisamāpayata më yazñamıtı samprƐ- pyágnum vishati’ [ When the Arbhava has begun, the Sacrificer, having covered the Udumbara post with a borderless piece of cloth, saya-() Bák- maņas, please complete this Sacrifice for me, and enters the Fire’) -If this were meant to be a mere verbal direction (not meant to be acted upon), then it would have to be taken as serving only a transcendental purpose; hence on the basis of the indications of this Direction, it must be taken 20 1722 SHABARA-BHÂṆYA: as actually enjoining the completion of the Sacrifice just as, in the case of the text’ If they take away the Soma, one should say—Run away, seek for it’. away and It has been argued that " it is the living, not the dead, man that can be the performer of a Sacrifice”. -This does not affect the case in question " It is the hiring man that says Please complete what has been begun ‘; so that what is done (in obedience to this direction) is really done by a living man. Says the Opponent At the time that the man addressed this direction, the completion was not done; at the time that the completing is done, the man is not alive, who then would be the performer 1” The answer to this is as follows-This is similar to that case where you, without any uncertainty, regard the performer to be a living man, when a man directs some one else to complate a piece of work and is alive at the tune of completion, the fact of his being so alive is munaterial so for He his being the performer is concerned.–he being regarded as the performer by virtue of the direction given by him; and so far as the giving of this previous direction is concerned, it is equally present in both cases,—that of the man alive at the time of completion as also the man that is not so alive. So that the man who has died after giving the direction as much the performer as one who is alive at the time of completion It might bo argued that- Inasmuch as the living man is present at the time of the completion. It is possible for hun to be regarded as the performer (10 the man who has died]”. This also is equally applicable to both cases: in the case of the living man also it is the Personality, not the Body, that is the performer, and the Personality is present also when the body has fallen off; so that the same Personality is the performer at the completion. —It might he urged that after the death of the Sacrificer, as it would not be possible for the Sacrificer’s functions to be performed, the rest of the procedure cannot be carried out, and hence the General Law cannot uidicate the admission of that part of the procedure That not so, the Genersi Law would certainly bring in all the rest of the details save those reinted directly to the Sacrificer, hence the argument does not affect the case at all. Or, we may rely upon the direct assertion in the text itself— ‘() Brahmanas, please complete this sacrifice of mine, which clearly indie stem that the sacrifice has to be completed,] and on the strength of thes, the details relating to the Sacrificer also may be performed. 5 ADHIKARANA (24): After the Sacrificer’s death the ‘Touching of the Shukra’ and such other acts as are capable of being done by him shall be done. SUTRA (59). ON HIS DEATH, THE PERFORMANCE SHALL PROCEED AS IN THE CASE OF THE BONE-SACRIFICE ’ 1 Bhāṣya. . There the Sarvanira acritice, also known as Shunahkarna Aquştomia, Inid down in the text Desiring lug own death, one should perform this sacrifice, if he wishes to go to the Heavenly regions, free from discuso - After the Sacrificer has died what is it that should be done?— - That is the question - We start off with the question itself, without setting forth the two views (Pūrvapakṣa and Saldhinta), even when the two views are set forth, the doubt remains there, as also when all the details bearing on the matter are not already known, as we find in the case of such questions. as-what is the name of this hull What is this river called” What frut tlus ? " The answer to this question is as follow. On his death, the performance shall proveel as in the case of the Bone acrstiere when the Sacrificer has gone the way of destiny the performance shall proceed as it does in the case of the Bone sterifice, that is, just as at the Bonesneriler only those details are performed by the Bones that are necessary for the accomplishment of the sacrifice, and the other details are omitted, sumilarly in the case in question when the Sacrineer has died, only that much shall be made to be done by the dead body HS IN Try for the accomplishment of the Sacriticer, such, for instance, as the Sacrifice touches the Shukra’, ’the Udumbara post is of the same height as the Sacrificer” ADHIKARAŅA (25): At the Sarvasvāra, before the Sacrificer’s death, the invoking of the blessings of longevity’ shall be done. SUTRA (60). E [PURVAPAKṢA]—“ EVEN WHILE HE IS ALIVE, THE WORDS INVOKING THE BLESSINGS OF LONGEVITY SHALL NOT BE PRONOUNCED ; AS IT IS FOR HIS SAKE 11 Bhārya. TA In connection with the Sarrasvara, while the Sacrificer is still alive, there arises the question–Should the words invoking the blessings of langevity— Ayuräshästë yajamānah ‘—be pronounced? or not? The Purvapakea view is as follows:- “Even while he is alive, the words invoking the blessings of longevity shall not be pronounced,-why ?- because it is for his sake. When the Sacrificer invokes the blessings of longevity, It implies that he desires longevity, -just as when one says “give me the bedding, it is implied that one desires to have the bedding, but in the case in question, how is the Sacrificer going to secure the longevity asked for ? In fact, here what the Bacrificer desires is something quite the contrary (of longevity), as he is going to immolate himself From thus it follows that the words invoking the blessings of longevity shall not be pronounced.” SUTRA (61) [SIDDHANTA IN FACT, THEY SHOULD BE PRONOUNCED, AS IT IS QUITE COMPATIBLE, PRIOR TO THE SAID OCCASION. Bhāṣya The answer to the above is as follows. The words invoking tla blessings of longevity should be pronounced; because much invoking is quite compatible; it is after the Arbhava has begun that the death of the Sacrificer comes to be sought for by him; while it is prior to the occasion of the Arbhava that the Sacrificer invokes the blessings of longevity; and the meaning of this would be ‘may I live till the time of the Arbhara’; in this manner the General Law would be obeyed. Hence it follows that in thas case also the words invoking the blessings of longevity should be pronounced. ADHIKARANA (26): At the ‘Dvādashāha’, details like the

Rtuyājyā’ should be performed. SUTRA (62). THERE SHOULD BE PERFORMANCE OF WHAT ARE SIMPLY MERITORIOUS ACTS. Bhasya. There is the Doddashāha sacrifice, laid down in the text― Dewiring prosperity, they should have recourse to the Drādashāha’, there are certain purely meritorious acta (having no bearing on the Sacrificial Ritual) which are indicated by the General Law as admissible at it, such acts, for instance us, Bluyāyā. [PURVAPAKṢA]—” EVEN WHILE HE IS ALIVE, THE WORDS INVOKING THE BLESSINGS OF LONGEVITY SHALL NOT BE PRONOUNCED ; AS IT IS FOR HIS SAKE Bhāsya. "” In connection with the Sarvasvara, while the Sacrificer is still alive, there arises the question–Should the words invoking the blessings of longevity- Ayuräshästē yajamānah-be pronounced ?-or not? The Purvapakṣa view is as follows :— Even while he is alive, the words invoking the blessings of longevity shall not be pronounced ;-why ?-because it is for his sake. When the Sacrificer invokes the blessings of longevity, it implies that he desires longevity,–just as when one says ‘give me the bedding’, it is implied that one desires to have the bedding, but in the case in question, how is the Sacrificer going to secure the longevity asked for? In fact, here what the Sacrificer desires is something quite the contrary (of longevity); as he is going to immolate himself From this it follows that the words invoking the blessings of longevity shall not be pronounced.” SUTRA (61) [SIDDHANTA-IN FACT, THEY SHOULD BE PRONOUNCED, AS IT IS QUITE COMPATIBLE, PRIOR TO THE SAID OCCASION. Bhāṣya The answer to the above is as follows.-The words invoking the blessings of longevity should be pronounced; because such invoking is quite compatible; it is after the Arbhava has begun that the death of the Sacrificer comes to be sought for by him; while it is prior to the occasion of the Arbhava that the Sacrificer invokes the blessings of longevity; and the meaning of this would be ‘may I live till the time of the Arbhava’; in this manner the General Law would be obeyed. Hence it follows that in this case also the words invoking the blessings of longevity should be pronounced. C ADHIKARANA (26): At the Dvadashaha’, details like the ‘Rtuyājyā’ should be performed. IN THE ABSENCE OF THE SUBORDINATE FACTOR, THE PRINCIPAL FACTOR (SHOULD BE CARRIED OUT) Bhāṣya. In connection with the Fire-installation Rite’, the Pavamāna-Iṣṭis are performed, as laid down in the text-Yo’gnaye pavamānāya purodāsha- maṣṭākapālannirvapēt, agnayē pāvakāya, agnaye shuchaye’; at these tie the General Law renders admissible the act of Cooking with the Agnihotra- havani’.-Now the time at which the Pavamana-Istis are performed is not the time of the Agnihotra ; so that at that time, the Agnihotrahavani s Got available. Thus then, there arises the question-As the Agnihotrahavani 18 not there, should the said Cooking’ be done (without it)? Or should st not be done? 4 The Purvapakça is as follows.“The Cooking cannot be done in the prescribed manner [as the Agnihotrahavani is not there]; and no useful purpose can be served by doing an act in a manner not prescribed; -hence it follows that as the act would be defective, it should not be done at all.” C In answer to this, we have the following Siddhanta:-In the absence of the subordinate factor,” the principal factor should be carried out.-tho Agnihotrahavani is a subordinate factor, and the act of Cooking’ is the principal factor. If the Cooking’ were not possible, then there would be no need for the Agnihotrahavani, which, therefore, would be excluded; but even in the absence of the subordinate factor, the principal factor is not impossible; hence it follows that the Cooking’ (which is the principal factor) should be done; it is only the fact of its being done with the Agma- hotrahavani which, being impossible, becomes excluded. • C •ADHIKABANA (28): At the Vājapēya’, the ‘Musti’ (Handful) becomes excluded. SUTRA (64). [PURVAPAKṆA]—“THE EXCLUSION OF THE NUMBER FOLLOWS FROM THE EXCLUSION OF THE ‘HANDFUL; BECAUSE IT IS SUBSERVIENT TO THAT.” Bhāṣya. There is the l’ajapaya sacrifice, laid down in the text-Desiring self-sovereignty, one should perform the Vajapeya sacrifice during the autumn’ :-in connection with that, we read- Naivärah saptadasha- sharāvaḥ kṣīrē charurbhavati’ [The Nivara-corn cooked in milk in seventeen saucers constitutes the Charu’],-now in connection with the Archetypal Sacrifice, a definite number and the measure of ‘handful’ have been laid down. in the sentence - Chaturo muştirnırvapatı’ [‘He cooks four hawlfuls’), —and both of these become admissible at the l’ajapēya, accord- ing to the General Law • There arises the following question in this connection- [At the l’‘ājapēya] (7) Should the number be adunitted and the ‘handful’ excluded “–ar (b) the Handful’ admitted and the number excluded?-or (c) the number excluded ? or (d) the number and handful both excluded 1-or (0) either one excluded? L On this question, the Purvapakea view (A) is as follows.” (A) Either one of the two may be excluded, 1e either the number or the ‘Handful may be excluded.-Why so 1-Because there being no word indicating the exclusion of any one in particular, there can be no restriction as to this or that alone being excluded 17 In answer to this we have the following view, which is Pūrvapakṣa (B) :~~ “There should be exclusion of the Handful and inclusion of the number. –Why? Because the number is the predominant factor in the text quoted, the number comes first, and it, therefore, becomes apprehended first; at the time of its comprehension there is nothing to obstruct the idea of the number; it is only after this unobstructed idea of the number hang appeared that the idea of the Handful comes in (as expressed by the second word in the sentence);—this latter therefore cannot get over the obstruction caused by the presence of the idea of the number ;—hence, as coming later, the Handful becomes excluded, and the number becomes admitted, this latter1728 SHABARA-BHĀṆYA : being the predominant factor; this is what is going to be explained under 12. 2. 23.” In answer to the above we have the following, [which is Pūrvapakṣa (C)]:–“The exclusion of the Handful should lead to the exclusion of the Number.-Why i-Because it is subservient to that; in the phrase “four handfuls’, the number is spoken of as subordinate to (1.8. qualifying) the Handful; the number four’ being mentioned simply with the view that the Handful may be qualified by the number Four,–and it is not mentioned for its own sake Hence, even though the number 18 mentioned first (in the phrase), it is as good, as not so mentioned; it is mentioned only for qualifying the other factor (Handful); consequently, no special regard should be shown to it; and if the Handful becomes excluded, the number subsisting in that Handful also becomes excluded, by reason of its substratum having disappeared, if the number were admitted as subsisting in another sub- stratum, then it would not be admitted in the form in which it has appeared at the Archetype On the other hand, if the number were excluded (and not the Handful), then the Handfuls which subsist in the ‘Cooking’ would not become excluded, for the simple reason that their substratum (Cooking) will not have been excluded. Hence, inasmuch as the number is subservient to (quality of) the Handful, it is the number that becomes excluded, not the Handfuls, according to the principle going to be explained under Sutra 12 2 25 SÜTRA (65) [Argument against Pūrvapaksa (C)—IT CANNOT BE SO BECAUSE IT IS AUXILIARY TO THE COOKING ‘. Bhasya. C It is not as has been explained above, as a matter of fact, the number is not mentioned as subsisting in the Handfuls; if it had been mentioned as subsisting in the Handfuls, then, being subservient, it could be excluded (on the exclusion of the Handfuls).” What then is it mentioned as sub- susting in “–In the Cooking’ How BO The construction is, not as ‘four handfuls’ (’ Chaturo muştih), but as ‘he cooks four’ (‘Chaturo nirva- pati’); in fact, it is the Cooking that is spoken of as qualified by the handful, as also by the number: it is only when a thing is connected with an action that the word expressing it takes the Accusative Ending (as we have in the words ‘chaturah’ and ‘muştih’)—“Why -Because it is a case- ending, an ending denoting a verbal relationship of something brought about; and what is brought about in an action, not a substance (which is an already accomplished entity) Hence Direct Assertion connects the number four’ with the action of Cooking’, while it is only Syntactical Connection that connects it with the ‘handfuls’,—and Direct Assertion is more authorita- tive than Syntactical Connection. Hence we conclude that in consideration of the principal factor, there should be exclusion of the Handful. 4 19 ADHYİYA X, PÅDA II, ADHIKARANA (28). SUTRA (66). 1720 [Final Përvapakṣa] “IN REALITY, ON ACCOUNT OF SIMILARITY IN REGARD TO THE INJUNCTION, THE NUMBER SHOULD BE REGARDED AS THE MODIFICATION OF THE ORIGINAL NUMBER, AND THE OTHER THING SHOULD BE TAKEN AS EXCLUDING THE HANDFUL’, BECAI SE 4 OF THE CONNECTION’.” Bhāṣya. The term ’tu’ (in reality’) implies the rejection of the view set forth above. " 1

1 It is not right that the Number is to be retained and the Handful excluded; what really happens is that the Number (seventeen) excludes the Number (Four), and the Saucers’ exclude the Handfuls ‘.-How NO — Because of similarity;—At the Archetype the ‘Handful is the substance leading to the act of Cooking’, and the Number four’ is a qualification of these Handfuls -n the case in question (of l’ajapeya) what is asserted is that the Charu’ consists of the Saucers’ as its substance and is qualified by the number seventeen -now here the substance Handful’ which serves the purpose of measuring (at the Archetype) becomes excluded (and replaced by the substance Saucers’, which also serve the same purpose of measuring,–and the number four, which qualified the Handful’, 18 excluded (and replaced) by the number seventeen’, which qualifies the ‘Saucers’ ;-just as in the case of the expression- This is curd, this 18 clarified butter, this is the vegetable, these the paddy-grams.-Dēvadatta should be fed; like Devadatta, Yajñadatta also should be fed, with oil ̊,– the purpose that is served in the food by the Clarified Butter is in the latter case understood to be served by oil; hence, even though it is not asserted in so many words that the food should be lubricated with oil’, yet the oil serves to exclude the Clarified Butter (and no other substance),—and that for the only reason that both of these serve the same purpose (of lubricating the food). Similarly in the case in question, the number that qualifies a substance can exclude only the number that serves the same purpose of qualifying a substance The other thing,-.e. the substance. Saucers should be taken as excluding the Handful, because of the connection.–From all this we conclude that the Number as well as the Substance connected with the Archetype becomes excluded (at the l’ājapēya).” " SUTRA (67) [SIDDHANTA]-NOT SO, BECAUSE OF THE CONNECTION OF THE SACRIFICER; SPECIALLY AS AT THE ARCHETYPE, THERE IS CONNECTION OF AN EMBELLISHMENT It is not as set forth above. explain as sacrifice; the number Bhāṣya.
