SUTRA (55). C [PURVAPAKŞA]” THE SENTENCE CHATURTHE CHATURTHEʼHANI AHI- NASTA GRHYATË SHOULD BE UNDERSTOOD TO MEAN THAT

THERE SHOULD BE REPETITION, AS IN THE CASE OF ‘EATING Bhasya In reference to the Sodashin, it has been declared- Chaturthê chaturthë ahani ahinasya grhyate’ [‘The Sodashin is taken up on the fourth day and the fourth day ‘1 In regard to this, there arises the question-Does this mean that at one and the same Ahina sacrifice, the Sodashin should be repeated (on the fourth day) ? Or, that it should be repeated in the sense that it should be taken up at the fourth day of each of the several Ahina-sacrifices? " The Purvapakṣa is as follows:—’ “It should be repeated at one and the same Ahina.-Why Because the text contains the word ’ ahinasya’ which means of one Ahina’; if it were taken as standing for several Ahinas, this could be only by Indirect Indication, while under our view it 18 Direct Denotation. Further, if several Ahinas had been meant, then the repetition (of the word ‘Chaturthō’) would have been entirely superfluous; and the required idea would have been obtained by the simple expression ‘Chaturthe ahanı ahinasya’ (‘on the fourth day of the Ahina’) If, on the other hand, it refers to a single Ahina, then the repetition serves a useful purpose. Hence the Sodashin should be repeated at one and the same Ahina;-like eating; just as in the case of the expression Chaturthe chaturthē ahani devadatto bhunktē’, it is understood to mean that having eaten on the fourth day, he eats again on another fourth day during the same fortnight’, sumilarly should it be in the case in question also-From all this it follows that there should be repetition at the same Ahina " SUTRA (56). [SIDDHANTA-IN FACT, IT SHOULD BE TAKEN UP AT SEVERAL ARĪNAS ; BECAUSE OF THE MENTION OF THE NUMBER, AS IN THE CASE OF THE FORTNIGHT; AS IT IS ONLY THUS THAT THE NUMBER SERVES A USEFUL PURPOSE. Bhāṣya. In fact, the Sodashin is taken up on the fourth day of several Ahina sacrifices; as it is only in this way that there would be a number of ’taking ADHYAYA X, PĀDA V, ADHIKARAṆA (14). · 4 1889 up’. Ja one Ahina, there can be only one fourth day, the other would be the eighth day’.-It has been argued that “under the Purvapakea view, the term ‘ahina would be taken in its direct denotation “.-It is true that there would be direct denotation; but mere direct denotation cannot do anything; as the character of ‘fourth’ would not be there. In our view, there is Indirect Indication, and this does serve a useful purpose.- Further, under our view, there need be no indirect indication either; as the singular number (in ‘ahani ‘) may be taken as standing for the generio entity-It has been argued that “repetation would be superfluous” ;- but that is not right, merely because a certam term would be superfluous, ther an be no justification for assuming a meaning of words which the words do not express at all-From all this it follows that the Sodashan in to be taken up at the several Ahinas,—as in the case of the fortnight’ ; in the case of the expression ‘pañchamyām pañchamyām bhunktë’, it 19 understood to mean the fifth day of two distinct fortnights; the same should be the case in the present instance also-We conclude therofore that the Sodushin should be taken up at several Ahinas ( SUTRA (57) IN THE CASE OF EATING, THE NUMBER CAN BE APPLICABLE. L 4 Bhāsya. It has been argued that “it should be as in the case of Eating”,-but in the case of Eating, it is by implication that the other day also is regarded as the fourth, that is, the second occasion of eating would be the fourth’ day only when it is counted from the first occasion of Eating, which alone is really the fourth day’ -in the case of the Ahina, that occasion would be the eighth day In the case of an act (like sacrifice) which is governed entirely by Verbal authority, we can understand only that much as is actually expressed by the word, and not on the basis of secular practice. Thus then, it 18 only right that in the case of Eating (which is a secular act), the ordinary secular practice should be followed, in the case of the Ahina however (which is a Vedic act), that alone can be admitted which is expressed by the word. ADHIKARAṆA (15): It is at the Ectype that the ‘Grahas’ should be led by ‘Āgrayaṇa”. SUTRA (58). IN THE CASE OF THE TERM JAGATSAMAN’,-INASMUCH AS THERE IS NO SUCH SAMAN,-THE SAMAN WOULD TAKE THAT NAME THROUGH THE VERSE. Bhasya. In connection with the Jyotışłoma, we read—’ Yadı rathantarasāmā Yadi jagateämä ägrayumägrän’ [‘If the Soma-sacrifice should be one at which the Rathantara-Sāman is chanted, then the grahas should be led by those dedicated to Indra-Vāyu If it is one at which the Jagat-Saman 14 sung, the grahas should be led by the Agrayana’.] This second sentence is the subject-matter for consideration

In regard to this, the question that arises is-Does this character of being led by the Agrayana find place in the Archetype? Or in the Ectype? The Purvapakea is as follows “In accordance with the Context, it should find place in the Archetype As a matter of fact, the sacrifice referred to in the expression if the Soma-sacrifice be one at which the Jagat- Saman is chanted’ is the Jyotistoma itself (which is the Archetype),-the name ‘Jagat-sāmā’ being applied to it by some sort of relationship-of quality or of action.” In answer to this, we have the following Siddhanta —Even though we And the term ‘Jagatsāman’ actually used, yet it is through the verse alone that the Săman could take that name.-Why so 1-Because there is no such Söman; in the whole of the Sāmavēda, there is no such Sāman as ‘Jagat- sama’; hence that sacrifice alone can be called ‘Jayatsāmā’ at which the Säman is chanted over a verse in the Jagati metre (as the basic verse);-and such a sacrifice is the Visuvat (an Ectypal sacrifice).” But the Visuvat has been spoken of as being one at which the grahas are led by Shukra”. That does not affect the case; this latter may be taken as pertaining to cases where the Visuvat is performed with a view to a particular reward.—From all this it follows that the character in question is to find place in the Ectypal Sacrifice, Visuvat. This same Sutra (58) may be explained differently as embodying the following Adhikaraṇa. ADHYAYA X, PĀDA V, ADHIKARAṆa (10). Lear ADHIKARAṆA (16): The name ‘Jagatsāmā’ applies to the 6 Visuvat’ sacrifice. SUTRA (58). IN THE CASE OF THE TERM JAGATSMAN’,-INASMUCH AS THERE IS NO SUCH SIMAN, THE SAMA WOULD TAKE THAT NAME THROUGH THE VERSE. Bhāsya. The text for consideration is the same as above-’ Yadı jagatsāmā ägrayanägrän grahän grhnätı’. 1 In regard to this there arises the question- What is it that is meant by ‘Jagatsām (a) Is it one that has either of the two Samans-Rathan- ‘ara or Brhat (b) Or that which has both these Samans (c) Or is it that which has the Rathantara only ? (d) Or is it that wherein the Saman Is chanted over a basic verse in the Jagati-metre ? The Purvapaksa is as follows “(a) It is that at wluch the Saman 18 either Rathantara or Brhat-Why ?-Because there is no reason for dis- criminating between the two That it is so 19 indicated by the fact that the Jyotistoma is the sacrifice dealt with in the Context, and at this sacrifice either of the two Sāmans may be chanted (b) Or, that sacrifice may be regarded as ‘Jagatsāmā’ at which both the said Samans are chanted; the terin ‘Jagat’ denotes whole, and the Jyotiatoma could be spoken of as having the whole Säman’ only if it had both the Samans; if only one of the two alone were used, then the term ‘jagat’ could not be taken as a qualifying terin, and it would have to be regarded as being of no signi- ficance at all Hence it follows that it must be a sacrifice having both the Sāmans.—(c) Or, that may be regarded as ‘Jagatsāmā’ which has the Rathantara only; as the basic verse of the Rathantara Ishānamasya jagatah evardrsham-contains the term ‘Jagat’ If the Jagatsāmā” were that at which both (Rathantara and Brhat) are chanted, then the Injunction in question would be doing what is already done, and as such it would be superfluous. Hence there can be no combination of those two at the Archetype, so that that alone can be regarded as ‘Jagatsāmā’ at which the Rathantara alone is chanted "” In answer to the above, we have the following Siddhanta :-That is called ‘Jagatsāmā’ at which the Saman is chanted over a basic verse in the Jagati metre. This is the view that is supported by the direct denotation of the term. Otherwise, if the term were taken as standing for the Rathantara- Săman, the verae would indicate the word and the word would indicate the Sāman; so that there would be indicative indication. For this reason the name ‘Jagatsāmā’ should be taken as standing for that at which this Säman is chanted over a basic verse in the Jagati-metre Thus then, it is through verse (in the Jagati metre) that the Sāman named ‘Jagat’ would be taken as occurring at the Vauvat sacrifice.” But the Visuvat has been 1892 SHABARA-BHĀṆYA : declared to be Shukrägra (whereas the Jagatedma is spoken of as ‘Agra- yanāgra ‘)".—That does not affect our position; as that would be taken as referring to that case of Vauvat where it is performed with a view to a definite reward. From all this it follows that the character in question should find place at the Fasuvat; which is an ectypal sacrifice C ADHIKARANA (17): At the Samsava’ sacrifice, neither the ‘Agriyavati’ nor the Upavati’ verse is to be used. SUTRA (59). [PURVAPAKŅA (A)]—“AT A SACRIFICE WHERE BOTH SIMANS ARE CHANTED, THAT WHICH IS CONTINGENT SHOULD BE USED OPTIONALLY, BECAUSE BOTH ARE EQUAL.” Bhāsya. Ubhayasāman’ (where both There are certa a sacrifices called Samans are chanted ‘), such as ‘Both should be chanted at the Samsara’; —again in einection with Ekaha sacrifice called Apachiti we read-’ Both, the Rathantara and the Brhat, should be chanted’,-now contingent upon the adoption of the Rathantara or of the Brhat, we have the rule that’ in connection with the Rathantara, one should adopt the verse containing the term ‘upa’, and in connection with the Brhat, one should adopt the verse containing the term ‘agriya” C Now thore arises the following question (a) Should the verse adopted be either the one contingent upon the Rathantara-Säman (1.e the verse with ‘Upa’), or that contingent upon the Brhat-Saman (10 the verse with agriya ‘), and there should be option —Or (b) Should that alone be adopted which is contingent upon the Rathantara Saman ! Or (c) Should that be adopted which is contingent upon something totally differont (from both Rathantara and Brhat) ? The Purtapaksa is as follows “One should adopt that contingent upon either the one or the other, there being option -Why ?–Because the admissibility of both is equal, and combination of both is impossible, -nor is there any reason for selecting either one of the two to the exclusion of the other, justifying the adopting of that contingent upon one, and not that contingent upon the other, nor is it possible to adopt both the verses. Hence there must be option.” SỮTRA (60) [PURVAPAKSA (B)]” OR, PREDOMINANCE SHOULD BE THE DETERMINING FACTOR Bhāṣya. * “It has been argued that the admissibility of both is equal and there is no reason for selecting either one of the two, but we say that there is such a reason, in the shape of ‘predominance’, which, as applying to the Rathantara, consists in its being mentioned first; as is going to be explained under Sutra 12. 2. 23.” 1894 SHABARA-BHİŞYA: SUTRA (61). [SIDDHÄNTA)—IN FACT, ON ACCOUNT OF THE ABSENCE OF THE CON- TINGENCIES, THE ACTION SHOULD BE DETERMINED BY THE SACRIFICE ITSELF. Bhāṣya. The term ‘vd’ (‘in fact’) implies the rejection of the views set forth above. There should be exclusion of both the contingencies (Brhat as well as Rathantara), and the sacrifice alone should be regarded as the determining factor; such being the case, it would be a case neither of Rathantara-Säman nor of Brhat-Saman; in fact, the Saman would be made up of both; con. sequently the verse adopted should be neither the one with Upa’ nor the one with ‘Agriya’; that alone may be adopted which is related to the sacrifice itself. ADHIKARANA (18): The Cup dedicated to Indra-Vayu is not to be brought up before all Cups. SUTRA (62). [PURVAPAKŞA]“INASMUCH AS THE CUP DEDICATED TO INDRA-VAYU IS SPOKEN OF AS THE FOREMOST’, IT SHOULL BE BROUGHT 6 UP AT THE BEGINNING Bhāsya. " In connection with the Jyotisjoma we read—’ Vāg vá aindravāyavo yadaindravā” wāyrā grahā gṛhyantē vāchamëvävarundhè’ [where the ‘aindra- vāyava’ cup is spoken as the ‘agra’, ‘first’, ‘foremost, of all cups ;—while in the Mantra-kända and the Brahmana-kānda, the order of the Cups is as follows (1) Upamshu-graha, (2) Antarydma-graha, (3) Andravāyava- graha, (4) Mastrāvaruna-graha and so forth, where the Andravayava has the third place]. In regard to this there arises the question–In accordance with the text quoted-Should the ‘aindravayavagraha’ (Cup dedicated to Indra- Vāyu) be brought (from the third place) to the beginning, before all the rest, even before the Upamshu and the Antaryāma Cups? Or is it to be taken up only before the Shukrāmanthi-Cups ↑ The Purvapakea view is as follows “The Cup dedicated to Indra- Vayu should be brought up before all the rest.—Why ?-Because it is spoken of as the ‘agra’ (‘foremost’, ‘first’), the text quoted above clearly lays down the first place for the Cup dedicated to Indra-Vayu Aindravayavāgram grhnäti’,-which clearly means that the Cup dedicated to Indra-Vayu should be dealt with before all the other Cups: so that, without any distinction, all the Cups should be treated so that the Cup dedicated to Indra-Vayu come before them. If the Cup in question were not brought up before all the others, then the Upamshu and Antaryāma Cups would not be such as have the Cup dedicated to Indra Vayu before them. On the other hand, when the Cup is brought up before all, then all the Cups become such as have the Cup dedicated to Indra-Vayu before them -Then, as a matter of fact, the text in question does not enjoin merely the ‘first’ place for the Cup dedicated to Indra-Vayu; if that had been enjoined, then that would have been fulfilled by halong that Cup ‘first’ in relation to any few Cups;-what is actually enjoined is that character of all the Cups which consists in having the Oup dedicated to Indra-Vayu before them; hence (according to this Injunction) that character has to be brought about in all the Cups; consequently the Cup has got to be brought up before all the Cups. How do you know that what is enjoined is the character of all the Cups?’–That it is so is clear from the assertion itself ‘One should make the Cups such as have the Aindra- Vayava Oup before them’; what this sentence lays down is not that the 1896 SHABARA-BHIṆYA: Oup should be ‘made’; what is asserted in that the Cups should be made such as have that particular Cup before them: so that the character of being ‘first’ (as belonging to the Andravayana-Cup) 18, not for its own sake, but only for imparting the aforesaid character to the other Cups. From all this it follows that the Cup dedicated to Indra-Vayu should be brought up before all the Cups.” SUTRA (63)

[SIDDHANTA]-IN FACT, THE OUPS HAVING THE PARTICULAR CHARACTER ARE EQUALLY ENDOWED WITH THAT QHARACTER, AND WHAT IS MEANT BY AGRA’ SHOULD, ON THE BASIS OF THE CONTEXT, BE TAKEN TO BE THAT THE CUP IN QUESTION SHOULD BE DEALT WITH IN ITS OWN PLACE Bhāṣya. The term ‘apti vă’ (‘in fact’) implies the rejection of the view sot forth above • agra’ The Cup in question should not be brought up before all the rest; it should be taken up in its own place.” Why ?"-Because what is enjoined in the text is not the fact of the Cup in question being the ‘first’ -which would be the indication of Syntactical Connection, what is enjoined is the taking up of the Cups of which the Cup in question is the (first), as is directly expressed by the words of that text which lays down that in the case of the Soma-sacrifice being one at which the Rathantara- Säman is chanted, those Cups which have been declared to have the Aindra- Vāyava Cup as their first should, by reason of that character, be taken up in that particular order’, so that the ’taking up’ enjoined is only of those Cups that, in their own normal position, have the Aindravāyava Cup before them [and not of those that are made so by the transference of the Aindra-Vayava Cup] Hence we conclude that the Andra-Vayava Cup is not to be brought up before all the rest. SUTRA (64) ALSO BECAUSE OF THE PRESENCE OF THE TERM DHĀRĀ ‘. Bhāsya Further, in the text speaking of the Aindra-Vayava Cup, we find the term ‘dhārā (stream)- Anva avyavachchhinnaya dharayā grīnāti’; from which it is clear that what is laid down is the taking up of those dhārā. grahas only which have the Aindra-Vāyava Cup before them [and not of all Cupe). ADHIKARANA (19): Even when the desire for a reward is there, the Aindravayava Cup is not to be brought up before all. SÜTRA (65). [PURVAPAKŞA]—“WHEN THERE IS DESIRE FOR REWARD MENTIONED, THE CUP MUST BE BROUGHT TO THE BEGINNING, BECAUSE OF THE DECLARATION TO THAT EFFECT.” Bhāsya In some cases we have a declaration of the Cup dedicated to Indra- Vayu in reforence to the presence of a desire for rewards, eg. ‘One who losures that there should be offsprings as before should take up the Cups in such a way as to make the Amdravāyava Cup the first’. In regard to this, there arises the question-Should the Cup in question be brought up before all the rest ? Or should here also the Cup be taken in its own place! The apparent answer to the question is that, in accordance with the principle arrived at in the preceding Adhikarana, the Cup in question should be taken up in its own place 4 As against this, we have the following Purvapaksa “In a case where there is desire for reward mentioned, the Cup must be brought up before all the rest-Why ?—Because of the declaration to that effect, there is the direct declaration to the effect that one who desires that there should be off- springe as before should take up the Cups in such a way as to make the Aindiavāyava Cup the first’; this declaration would serve a useful purpose only if it were taken as laying down the fact of the Aindravāyava Cup coming before all others, and if, in accordance with this the said Cups were actually brought up before all the rest If it were taken (as suggested by the Siddhantin in the preceding Adhikarana) that what is laid down is only the taking up of the Cups of which the Aindravāyava is the first, then the declaration would not lead to any particular form of activity (and as such, would be futilo) Hence it follows that the Cup in question must be brought up before all the rest.” SUTRA (66). [SIDDHANTA]-INASMUCH AS THE TERM AGRA IS RELATED TO THOSE OCCUPYING A CERTAIN POSITION, THE DECLARATION SPEAKING OF THE DESIRE FOR REWARD SHOULD REFER TO THOSE ; SPECIALLY ON ACCOUNT OF THE PRESENCE OF WHAT IS ESSENTIAL. Bhāṣya. What has been said regarding the Cup in question having to be brought up before all the rest is not right; the order of sequence can be 311898 SHABARA-BĦIṆYA:

" duly followed only when the Cup is taken up in its own place in the series hence it must be taken up in its own place-It has been argued that ΟΙ account of the text laying down the first place for the Cup, it must be brough up before all the rest”;-but that is not so; in fact, what the text lay down is in relation to those Cups which in their own normal position in th ‘stream’, have the Andravayava Cup before them ;-the reward in questio would be brought about only if there were the ’taking up of just thos Cups which have that character of having the Andravayava before it thus alone would the Direct signification of the words be followed; whil your view would have the support of Syntactical Connection; and Direc Assertion is more authoritative than Syntactical Connection.-It has bee argued that “if the declaration were taken as the injunction of the takin up (of just these Cups), then it would not lead to any particular form c activity” -The answer to this is that there are two distinct connections- by one connection, the essential (compulsory) act (of Taking up) is relate to the desire for reward, the meaning being that the particular rewar should be obtained by means of the Taking up’,–and by the other connec tion, there is the essential act by itself (without reference to any reward),- * in the sense that ‘one shoula take up those Cups which have the Aindra vāyava Cup before them -so that the particular form of activity is dul secured. Hence the declaration in question should be taken as laying dowr as a means of securing the reward, the taking up of the Cup in its own place so that the Cup in question has to be taken up in its own place in th

series. C ADHIKARAŅA (20): The Cups which have the Ashvina Oup as their foremost have to be brought forward. SUTRA (67) [PURVAPAKSA]” IN OTHER CASES ALSO, THE TERM SHOULD BE TAKEN AS BEFOR Bhāṣya C 33 AGRA ’ There is the Jyotıştoma acrifice, in connection with which there are *mentioned Cups other than that dedicated to Indra-l’ayu, in connection with a desire for particular results (a) For one who is ill, one should take пр th. Cups with thel Ashvina-Cup as the foremost (“agra “)’, (b) ‘For one who is performing a malevolent rite, one should take up the Cups with the Shukra-Cup as the foremost, (c) For one against whom a malevolent rite is being performed, one should take up the Cups with the Manthin Cup as the foremost C In rogard to all thus, there arises the question, should, in all these cases also, the Cups sporified as ‘foremost bo takon up in their own places ? Or should they be brought up before all the other Cups?

The Purvapakça is as follows In other cases, e. in the taking up of Cups other than the Aindravāyava, —also the term “agra’ (’ foremost ‘} should be taken as before, 10 the Cups should be taken up in their own places, and the result desired would be connected with those Cups of which certain Cups have been mentioned as the foremost “.” SUTRA (68). [SIDDHANTA]-IN FACT, IT SHOULD BE BROUGHT UP; BECAUSE THE ‘AGRA’, WHICH IS CONNECTED WITH THE ESSENTIAL FACTOR, HAS NO CONNECTION (WITH THE RESULT) Bhasya The Cups in question should be brought back before the Andravdyava Cup.-“Why?"-Because in this case the desire for results has no con- nection with the essential factor. If the desire were present in the case of the essential act also, the term ‘agra as appearing in the words ‘dahvinā- gran’ and ‘inanthyagrân ‘—could not be applicable to it; because the presence of that declaration is not found to give rise to any particular form of activity, while if it were withdrawn to before the Aindravāyava Cup, then the said declaration would serve a useful purpose. Then again, the Cups in question are those that are used at the Archetype, and in reference to these the sentence in question lays down the character of having the Ashvina 1900 SHABARA-BHAṆYA: for their first and of having the Shukra for their first. Hence it follows that the Oups in question should be brought up to the beginning. SUTRA (69). THERE IS A TEXT INDICATING THE SAID BRINGING UP J Bhāṣya There is the text Dharayeyustam yam kāmāya grhniyuh, aindra- väyavam grhitvä sädayet yam kāmāya grhniyuh’. [They should hold that which they have taken up with the desire for a certain result : having taken up tho Andraviyava Cup, they should deposit that which they have taken up with the desire for a result ‘1,-here it is said that that to be held which has been taken up with the desire for a certain result which shows that the Aindravayava Cup is to be taken up -For this reason also the Cups in question should be brought up before all the rest. P ADHIKARANA (21): The Ashvina’ and other Cups are to C be brought forward just before the Aindravayava’ Cup. SŪTRA (70). IT SHOULD BE PRIOR TO THE AINDRAVĀYAVA. “V 4 BECAUSE THAT IS THE POSITION ASSIGNED TO THE AGRA’. 4 Bhāsya " & There is the Jotistoma sacrifice; in connection with that certain Cups are spoken of as coming after the Andravāyava Cup, and as to be taken up for the flfilment of certain desires -eg Ashvināgrān grahân grhnāti amog ivinah’, For one who is ill, one should take up the Cups with the Ashvina Cup as the first’,- Shukrāgrānabhicharatah’, ‘For one who is performing a malevolent rite, the Cups with the Shukra Cup as the first’ ;- ‘Manthyagrunabhıcharyamānasya’, ‘For one against whom a malevolent rite 18 being performed, the Cups with the Manthin Cup as the first’ —It has been settled (in the preceding Adhikarana) that these Chips are not to be taken up in their places, but are to be brought forward Now there arises the question-Are these to be brought forward prior to all the Cups " Or prior to somo Cups (without any restriction) –Or prior def ely to the Aindravayava Cup? و گیاه The Pūrvapaksa 18 that " as there is no rule laying down the exact place whereto the Cups in question are to be brought forward, thore can *be no lestriction (and they may be brought forward anywhere on likes].” In answer to this we have the following Siddhanta -They should be brought forward prior to the Andradayava Cup-why ?-because that is the position assigned to the ‘agra’; it has been recognised that the place meant by the terin ‘agra’, ‘first’ (as occurring in ‘āshvināgrān’ and other words), 18 that after the Upāmshu and Antaryama Cups, and before the Aindraväyava Oup.-” “How so ?"-In accordance with the previous toxt-If the Soma- sacrifice should be one at which the Rathantara-Sāman is chanted, one takes up the Cups with the Andravāyava as the first-the Cups have been taken up at the Archetype as with the Aindravayava as the first,—and in this text the taking up of these Cups has been laid down as in relation to the Aindravāyava Chup,-and having been laid down there, it cannot be taken as laid down again in connection with those having the Ashvina for their first’, or those having the Shukra for their first’, or those having the Manthin for their first’;-hence all that the text in question can be taken as laying down is the fact of these being the ‘first’,-now here the Cups that have been spoken of in the context are those having the Aindravāyava for their first’, so that when the question arises as to what one should do, in the case of one performing a malevolent rite, to the Cups with the • 2 C 1902 SHABARA-BHİŞYA : Shukra as the first’,-the answer is that he should take these up’; and this naturally has to be taken along with the Context; we cannot connect the * Shukragrân’ with simply ‘grahân’; as there would be no term ex- pressing the ’taking up’.-With what then is it to be connected -It has to be connected with the term ‘andravāyavägra’ which appears in the context, -the full sentence being ‘Shukrāgrän grhniyāt aındravāyavāgrān’ (in the sense that one should take up the Cups with the Shukra as the first, which are prior to the Andravāyava’); and what these Cups are has been descrik, there. Thus the conclusion is that the Cups in question are to be brought forward prior to the Andravayava Oup.” C SUTRA (71) ALSO BECAUSE THEIR PROPERTIES ARE SIMILAR Bhasya The Cups in question have properties similar to those of the Aindi wā. yava; in the latter we find the presence of the ‘stream’; hence we con- clude that when the text speaks of the ‘first’, it is in relation to those Cups that are connected with the ‘stream’ SUTRA (72) TO THE SAME END WE FIND AN INDICATIVE TEXT ALSO Bhasya There 18 the text Dhārayeyustam yam kāmāya grhniyuh, andra- vāyavam grhitvä sädayēt, atha tam sadayet yam kāmāya grhniyuh — here the holding of the Andravayava 14 spoken of as coming after the holding of the Oup that has been taken up with the desire for a certain reward.- This also shows that the Cups in question should be brought forward prior to the Aindravayava Cup.

ADHIKARAŅA (22): The ‘depositing’ also is to be brought forward. SUTRA (73). THE DEPOSITING’ ALSO; AS IT IS SUBSIDIARY. Bhasya. There is the declaration- Ashvinägrän qrhniyāt āmavayāvinah, shukrā– grân grhmyät abnucharatah, manthyagrän grhniyāt abhicharyamānasya ’ ;— it has been explained that the Cups spoken of here are to be brought up prior to the Aindravayava Cup Now there arises the question-Is the ‘depositing’ also (of these Cups) to be brought up ?—Or not We assert (says the Purvapakṣin) that “there being no declaration to that effect, the Depositing should not be brought forward; our sole authority is the Vedic word; and what the Vedic word lays down is the bringing forward of the ‘Taking up’ of the Cups, not of the ‘depositing’: hence the Depositing 19 not to be brought forward.”

In answer to this, we have the following Siddhanta :-The ‘depositing also should be brought forward,-why ?-because the ‘depositing’ is only subsidiary to the taking up’,-the taking up of the Cups is for the purposes of offering; and this offering has got to be done of several substances at one and the same time; they could not be used for being offered as libations unless they were deposited, kept in proper places; in fact, It is by depositing that the taking up becomes fit for the act of offering :— hence it follows that the depositing is subsidiary to the Taking up; and hence when the Taking up is brought forward, the Depositing must also be brought forward SUTRA (74). ALSO BECAUSE WE FIND INDICATIVE TEXTS, Bhāṣya. “Which A text is also found to be indicative of the same conclusion. text?”-“Dharay@yustam yam kāmāya grhniyuh, aindravayavam grhitvā sddayēt, atha tam sadayēt yam kāmāya grhniyuh’; this clearly shows that the depositing also has to be brought forward. ► C ADHIKARAṆA (23): The offering’ is not to be brought C forward. SUTRA (75) [PURVAPAKṢA]—“THE OFFERING’ ALSO SHOULD BE TREATED LIKE THE DEPOSITING Bhāṣya There is the following declaration- Ashvinägrän grhnät ämayāvinaḥ, shukrägränabh charataḥ, manthyagrānabhicharyamānasya’;-it has been estab- lished that when the taking up’ of these Cups is brought forward, their ‘depositing’ is also brought forward Now there arises the question–When the ’taking up’ lias been brought forward, is the offering’ also brought forward? Or not! The Purvapakea is as follows “The offering 18 brought forward.- Why ?-Because of the relationship, the taking up and the offering are mutually connected, as the Cup is taken up only for being offered; it is only thus that it serves a visible purpose; otherwise, all that is done after the ‘depositing’ would be for an unseen purpose ;-the Taking up however is not for an unseen purpose; hence whenever, at any other time, the offering is to be made, the taking up has to be done Such being the case, whenever there is Taking up, Offering must be thore; such being the connection (be- tween the Taking up and the Offering), the Offering has to be treated like the Depositing, that is, just as on the bringing forward of the Taking up, the Deposuing is brought forward, similarly the Offering also should be brought forward " SUTRA (76) As a MATTER OF FACT, IT IS NOT SO, BECAUSE IT IS THE PRINCIPAL FACTOR, AS FOR THE DEPOSITING’, IT IS TREATED AS Above BECAUSE IT IS A SUBSIDIARY FACTOR Bhasya It is not true that the offering is brought forward Because the offering in the principal factor; it is not a mere auxiliary to the Taking up; hence it is not brought forward (along with the Taking up). It has been argued that it should be treated like the Depositing;-but Depositing is a subsidiary factor; that is why it 19 brought forward. ADHIKARANA (24): The mention of Aindravayavāgra’ in connection with the Tryanika’ is for the purpose 4 of pointing out the similarity of procedure. SUTRA (77). [PURVAPAKSA “IN CONNECTION WITH THE TOYANIKA, THE MENTION OF WHAT ARE ALREADY INDICATED BY THE GENERAL LAW CAN BE ONLY FOR THE PURPOSES OF EULOGISING Bhāsya 95 In connection with the Drādashāha sacrifice, there is the Tryanīkā, described in the following text—* Amdravāyavāgrau prāyaniyodayaniyau, dashamuñchāhah, athētarēṣām navānāmaḥnām andravāyavägram prathaman ahah, etc etc’ [‘Tryanīkā’ 18 that which has three anikas, facets, in the shape of the Aindravāyava, the Shukra and the Agrayana-Hays the Nyāyamālā —According to the Subodhini, Tryanikā’ is the name given to nine days of the Dvādashaho, excluding the first, last, and tenth days’ | 4 In the above passage it is declared that the first day’ has the Andra- vāyava Cup as the first, and the second day’ has the Shukra Cup as the first,-inasmuch as the Rathuntara-Sāman is chanted on the First Day, and the Brhat-Saman on the second Day, the prosence of both the said Cups as the first 19 already indicated by the General Law Now there arises the question-When the same fact (of the two Cups being the first on the First Day and the Second Dav respectively, which is already indicated by the General Law) 18 mentioned again in the passage quoted above, (a) is it for the purpose of reiterating the saino? (b) Or for precluding others? (c) Or as a mere commendatory declaration? Or (d) for the purpose of pointing out that the same procedure is to be adopted? The Purvapakṣa is as follows “It should be taken as incant to be only a commendatory declaration-Why -When a text morely reiterates what has been already asserted before, it does not lead to any particular form of activity [hence alternative (a) cannot be accepted] As for the second alternative (b), Preclusion is always open to a three-fold objection Hence the passage should be taken as a commendatory declaration What is the quality that is commended here ?’-It is the quality of propriety-it being regarded as right and proper that on the Third Day the Agrayana Oup should be the first.-How so ?-Because it has been declared that on the First Day, the Aindravāyava Cup 1s to be the first, and on the Second Day, the Shukra Cup is to be the first; and nothing has been said in regard to the Third Day; hence it is only right and proper that on the Third Day, the Agrayana should be the first.” 1906 SHABARA-BHIŞYA: SUTRA (78). [BIDDHANTA IN REALITY (WHAT IS MEANT IS THAT) AMONG THE ‘AHARGAṆAS’, THERE SHOULD BE SIMILARITY OF PROCEDURE ; & AS IN THE CASE OF AGNI ’ Bhasya The phrase ‘ap va’ (in reality’) implies the rejection of the view set forth above. The declaration is not for the purpose of eulogising a quality, it is for pointing out that the procedure should be similar.-It is not right to say that “what is declared being already implied by the General Law, its reiteration is useless, hence it must be taken as serving some other purpose 11 “What is the view then that can be held ?"-What has been done at the Jyotistoma in connection with the Rathantara Săman in accordance with Syntactical Connection is rendered admissible in the case in question by the General Law, and it is reiterated with the intention that I shall adopt the same procedure here also ‘—ds in the case of ‘Agni’‚—just as the sameness of procedure has been asserted in connection with the Agmatoma, in the following passage Athāto’gniştomēnanānuyajati, tam- ukthyena, tamatirātrēna, tam chatūrātrēna, tam pañcharutrēna, tam sadrātrēna, tam saptarātrēna, tamaştarātrēna, tam navarātrēna, tarn dasharātrēna, tamekāda- shardtrēna’. 6 THE PRSTHA Bhasya 6 Of the Dvādashāha, there are two forms-the C Analytic’ and the

1 ‘Synthetic’. The Synthetic’ form is described in the following passage— Aindrāvāyavagrau athāgrayanagram’,-and the Analytic form 18 described in the passage Aṁndravāyavāgrau prayaniyodayaniyau . dvě aındravāyavāgrē ’ In regard to these, there arises the question-Are the details laid down for the Dvadashāha in reference to both forms of it? Or are they laid down in reference to the Synthetic form of it, and the Analytic’ form is only a modification (or Ectype) of the former The Purvapakṣa is as follows “Of the Dvādashāha, both the Synthetic and Analytic forms stand on the same footing;-why ?-because both the forms form the subject-matter of the Context, and hence it cannot be differentiated to whom the details belong and to whom they do not belong. Hence both should be regarded as standing on the same footing-Like the ‘Pretha’; 1.8. in regard to the two Prathas, Brhat and Rathaniara, it being found that the Context appertains equally to both, they are taken as having the same details, so should be the case with the ‘Synthetic’ and ‘Analytic’ forms of the Dvadashāha also " SÜTRA (80) • [SIDDHANTA] IN REALITY, THE ANALYTIC’ FORM IS THE MODIFICATION OF THE SYNTHETIC FORM, BECAUSE WE FIND INDICATIVE C ? TEXTS TO THAT EFFECT Bhāṣya The term ‘va’ (‘in reality’) implies the rejection of the view set forth above. The Synthetic and Analytic forms do not stand on the same footing; in fact, the Analytic one should be regarded as the modification of the Synthetic form.-Why 1-Because we find indicative texts to that effecti the following is the indicative text- Andravāyavasya vā ētadāyatanam yachchaturthamahaḥ’;—this text occurs in connection with the Analytic‘ Dvādashāha; at the analytic Dvādashāha, however, the Aindravāyava does not •1908 SHABARA-BHÄṆYA : form the first on the Fourth Day’; in fact, it is the Agrayana that forms the first on that day;-such being the case, the assertion ‘Aindravayavasya vā šādāyatanam’ cannot be applicable. If however, the Analytic is the modification of the Synthetic form, then the said assertion becomes applic- able as referring to the Synthetic form; the sense being that the ‘dyalanam’ which should belong to the Aindravāyava (in accordance with the General Law) is asserted in reference to the Agrayana Hence from this indicative text, it follows that the Analytic is the modification of the Synthetic form. 4 SUTRA (81). BECAUSE OF THE PRESENCE OF Bhasya DESIRE’. There is the text’ Yah kāmayēta bahu syam prajāyêya, etc ‘, and whenever a prospective act’ or ‘contingent act’ is done, it comes in only as a modification of an essential act’; for instance, the eating of Mudga and Rice and sleeping away from the wind- in cases of eve-disease. SUTRA (82). IT OPERATES BOTH WAYS,-BEING ONE AND THE SAME ACT Bhasya This Sutra explains the purpose of the discussion The Dvādashāha operates equally both ways, among the Aharganas, because both are one and the samne act.—This in accordance with the Purvapaksa According to the Siddhania, on the other hand, the Analytic form is operative only when there is a direct declaration or an indicative text to that effect,-in all other cases it is the Synthetic form that is operative. 4 L 1912 SHABARA-BHİŞYA : SUTRA (86). AT THE ‘ÉKĀDASHINA’ THERE IS REPETITION BECAUSE OF THE DECLARATION TO THAT EFFECT Bhāṣya. It has been argued (under Sü. 83) that it should be as in the case of the Ekadashina—It is right that in the case of the Ekadashinas, there should be repetition ‘in the manner of the Measuring Rod ‘; because there is a declara- tion to that effect- Varunamantatah punaḥ paryāvṛttēşvāqnēyamēva pratha- mēhani ālabhēta ‘;-in accordance with this declaration, there is repetition in the manner of the Measuring Rod’ of those that are repeated over again; -this, being found to be impossible at the Dvädashäha, finds room in the Gavamayana. What is there that a Direct Declaration cannot do There 18 no burden too heavy for Direct Declaration L SUTRA (87). ALSO BECAUSE WE FIND INDICATIVE TEXTS Bhasya There is an indicative text also which points to the same conclusion, as to how the Ekadashimas are repeated in the manner of the Measuring Rod’ Prana vā ekadashanah yadēkādashinibhiriyurahānyatırichyante pashavo vā’.-If the components are augmented in their own places, there is no excess. It is only in the case of ‘repetition in the manner of the measur- ing rod’ that there is always either cxcess or shortage From this also we con- sider it only right that in the Ekadashina, there should be ‘repetition in the manner of the Measuring Rodl’. C ADHIKARANA (27): At the Analytic’ Dvadashaha, there should be change of the Metres of Mantras only. L 4 SUTRA (88). 2 INASMUCH AS THE CHANGE OF METRE HAS BEEN SPOKEN OF IN CON- NECTION WITH THE ANALYTIC DADASH AHA, IT IS THE TEXT OF THE MANTRAS RELATING TO BHAKSA’, PAVAMANA’, 4 PARIDHI, AND ‘KAPĀLA ’ THAT SHOULD UNDERGO MODIFICATION Bhāsya 4 There the Dridashāha sacrifice in its analytic and synthetic’ forms, of these the Analytic form is thus described—’ Amdravāyavāgrau atha dvě amdravāyavāgrē ’ – In connection with this Analytic form of Dvadashiha there is the following declaration- The metres ponder over the regions of one another -the Gayatri over that of the Tristup, the Tristup over that of the Jagati, the Jagati over that of the Clāyatri’ [Here we have an interchange of metres laid down 1-At the same sacrifice, there are (1) the Bhaksa, (2) the Paramānu, (3) the Paridhı, and (4) the Kapāla (1) Related to the Bhaksa, there is the mantra Bhuhợp là mũ PG gayatrachhandasah tristupchhandasah jayatichhandasah bhakяayāmı”, -(2) related to the Pavamana, there is the mantra-’ Shyēnos gāyatri- chhandah suparnos: tristupchhandāh sakhāsi jagatichhandāh pāraya” (3) in relation to the Paridh, there is the mantra—’ Gāyatro madhyamah paridhik, traistubho daksino, jāyata uttarah”,- -(4) in relation to the Kapālas, there is the mantra- Astākapālah L tartiyasavanikah’ In regard to this, there arises the following question - When there 18 ‘change of metre’ (as prescribed), is there to be change (1) of the Bhaksa- mantras as well as of the Bhakṣa, -(2) of the Pavamana mantras as well as of the Pavamina,—(3) of the Parıdhi-mantras as well as of the Paridhi8,- (4) of the Kapala-mantras as well as of the Kapālas " Or is there to be change of metre in the mantras only ?

The Purvapakṣa is as follows L “There should be change of the Mantras as also of the subject-matter of the mantras -Why Because the declara- tion is without distinction, the declaration that there is makes no distinction at all; it says “The metres ponder over each other’s regions —the Glâyatrī over the Triștup’s, the Tristup over the Jagati’s, the Jagati over the Gayatri’s’; there is nothing in this to show that the change is to be of the mantras only (not of their subject-matter). Hence there should be change of mantras as well as of their subject-matter As a result of this, (A) the Central Paridhi should be placed in the position of the Right one, the Right one in the position of the Left one, and the Left one in the position of the Central one; (B) the Asṭakapāla should be con- 321914 SHABARA-BHÄṆYA : nected with Midday, the Ekadashakapala with the Third Savana,-the Dvadashakapdia with the Morning Savana;~(0) the Drink connected with the Morning Savana should be drunk in place of the Midday Drink, the Midday Drink should be drunk in place of that related to the Third Savana, -and that related with the Third Savana should be drunk in place of that related to the Morning Savana; and (D) the Bahispavamāna should be used in place of the Midday Pavamana,-the Midday one in place of the Arbhava, and the Arbhava in place of the Bahuspavamāna.” · In answer to the above, we have the following Siddhanta-It is not right that there should be ‘change of metres all through, without distinc. tion, the change should be in the mantras only; it is the metres in the mantras alone that should be changed -Why so ?-Because it is only the metres of the mantras that are capable of being really changed; as for the Bhakea and other things, even on being changed, they remain what they were, -the Bhakaa still remams Bhaksa, and so on. For mstance, if the Bhakşa (Drink) related to the Morning Satana is drunk at the time of the Midday one, it would not become ‘related to the Tristup-metre’, so on, in all canes,-How so –Because oven at its own time the Drink is not related to the Gayatri-metre, it is only the Gayatri,-not what is not-Gayatri,-that can take the place of the Tristup, and certainly the Drink and other things are not Güyatri Thus there is no possibility of any change of the Drink and other things. On the other hand, the metres of the Mantras can very well exchange their places -Hence the change should be made only in the metres of the Mantras. 6 End of Pada r of Adhyāya X. ADHYAYA X. PADA VI ADHIKARANA (1): The Rathantara and other Samans are sung over a Verse-trind. SUTRA (1) [PURVAPAKṢA]—“AT THE SACRIFICE, THEY SHOULD BE (SUNG) OVER A SINGLE VERSE, JUST AS IN THE READING OF THE TEXT,” Bhāṣya. The San form the subject-matter of this Adhikaraṇa-such as Ruthantara, Brṛhat, Vairūpa, Vairāja, Shākvara, and Rawata. In regard to these, there arises the question-Should the singing of these be done over a single verse ? Or over a Verse-triad ? The Purvapaksa is as follows “At the sacrifice they should be sung over a single verse; they are so sung at the time of reading the text; and as they have been sung at the time of reading the text so should they be sung at the sacrificial performance,it is only right that there should be no difference between what is done during the reading of the text and what 18 done during the performance of a sacrifice; as it is only for the purpose of sacrificial performances that the text is read, hence at the sacrifice the Saman should be used just as it has been used during the reading of the text. From this it follows that the Samans should be sung over a single verse. The Samans that form the subject-matter of this Adhikarana are those which have their origin in single verses, not those that are based in their very origin upon Verso-triads. As has been said—’ Simāsantanıya ēvāpatyashāk- varavarnam’ (?)-[This is the reading of MS D MS C. roads Yathāhimasata. nyatashṛāpatyashākvaravantum’; in any case the words are not intelligible].” [SIDDHANTA SUTRA (2) IN FACT, THEY SHOULD BE SUNG OVER A VERSE-TRIAD ; AS WE FIND INDICATIVE TEXTS TO THAT EFFECT. Bhāṣya. It is not right that they should be sung over a single verse.-Why ?— Because we find indicative texts, there is the following indicative text- • Astākṣarēna prathamāyā rchah prastoutt dvyakṣarēna uttarayoh’ [where the details of the singing are spoken of as bearing upon the first verse’ and the two later verses’]; if the singing were done over a single verse, there 1916 SHABARA-BHĀṆYA: would be no sense in the use of the terms ‘first’ and ’later two ‘.-Hence it follows that they should be sung over a Verse-triad.-The following is another indicative text pointing to the same conclusion- The Rk said to the Saman -Let us pair together, Säman said-Thou art not fit to be my wife, the Veda is my majesty, then becoming two, the Bks said the same thing; the Saman said-You are not fit for being my wives, the Veda is my majesty, then becoming three, the Rks said the same thing, whereupon the Saman said- Let us be together-From this also it follows that when a hymn is sung, one Säman is chanted over three verses Says the Opponent “This that you have put forward is only an indicative text, state some direct reasons Answer-In the whole of the Ṛqueda, there is no verse that is named ’ Prathamā” (First), nor are there any named Uttarā’, in fact, both these names are relative, hence in the text quoted, when it is said that the hymning should be done with eight syllables of the Prathamā (first) verse, and with two syllables of the Uttara (two later) veraes, it is clear that three verses are being referred to. Sumilarly, though the taxt Elam sima trehë kriyatē stotriyam ’ appears to be only reiterative, yet on the basis of the commondatory passage describing the conversation between Bk and Saman, it is clear that the said text is injunctive (not merely reiterative) This is what has been explained under Sutra 3 5. 21. ADHIKARAŅA (2): The term ‘Svardṛk’ serves the purpose of indicating the time for the Vikṣaṇa’. C SUTRA (3) . J

  • LOOKING AT SVARDRK SHOULD BE TAKEN ONLY AS INDICATIVE OF TIME, BECAUSE IT IS FOR THE SAKE OF SOMETHING ELSE Bhāṣya ‘There 15 cho text–Ishvaram vai rathantaramudgātushchakṣuh, pra- mathītā rathantaré pro dūyamānē sammulēt svardisham prati vīksēta’ (‘The Rathantara is the all-powerful eye of the Udgātr, when the Rathantara 18 begun, the Pumathin should close his eyes and look towards the Svardek’ ] Or In regard to this, there arises the question -The looking at the Fire’ that is here laid down is it meant to be an accessory of the sacrifice? is it mentioned only as indicating a particular point of time?-What we have to consider in this connection is Is looking towards the Svardyk (Fire) ’ meant to be subsidiary to the closing of the eyes on the starting of the Rathantara” Or is the sentence he should look towards the Svardrk’, □ separate sentence by itself? י · C The Pūrrapaksa is as follows “The looking towards the Suardrk’ is meant to be an accessory and the sentence laying it down is separate by itself -Why -Because it is clearly understood to bo different, the sentenco ’ he should look at the Fire’ is found to be clearly distinct from the proceding sentence - But the sentence is actually found to be non-separate also from the preceding one. Having laid down that on the starting of the Rathantara one should close his eyes, it goes on to reiterate that he should look towards the Seardrk’ -The answer to this is that, in both these constructions, wo have to regard the two sentences as distimet, this difference would be inconsistent with the non-difference urged by the objector, and when there is a conflict between Injunction and Reiteration (and the question is whether the sentence he should look towards the Seardrk’ is an injunction or a reitera- tion), the night course is to take it as an Injunction firstly because in that case it says something new, and a more declaration serves no useful purpose”, as declared under Sūtra i 2 19, secondly because we find a clear injunction, a clear junction is perceived in the word ‘vīkķēta’ (should look’);-thirdly, the Direct Denotation of the words becomes accepted, for instance, the words should look at the fire’ clearly lay down the act of ’looking’ towards what is denoted by the term ‘avardrk’, that there is direct connection between what is denoted by the terin svardrk and the art of looking’. If the words were not taken to mean this, then the terin ‘svardrk’ could only indirectly indicate a particular time. And when there is conflict between Direct Denotation and Indirect Indication, the most reasonable course is to accept the former From all thus it follows C NO 1918 SHABARA-BHÄṆYA: that the ‘Looking’ is meant to be an accessory.-Or, the text ‘Svardṛsham prati viksēta’ may be construed in the following manner, to show that the ‘Looking’ is meant to be an accessory:-What is denoted by the term ‘avardsk’ is the means of accomplishing the ’looking’; this would be in keep- ing with the Indicative text, as also with Syntactical Connection, inasmuch as the term ’ svardyk’ is actually present in the sentence. From all this it follows that the act of looking’ is meant to be an accessory.’ "” 4 In answer to the above, we have the following Siddhânta:- Looking at Svardṛk’ should be taken only as indicative of time, because it is for the sake of something else. It is not that the ‘Looking’ is meant to be an accessory; in fact, the connection between what is denoted by the word ‘svardık and ’look’ is for the purpose of indicating time -“Why?"-Because the Saman is for the sake of something else; in the text ‘Rathanlaram pretham bhavati’, the Saman is declared as to be used in the Pratha-hymn; which means that when the words of the verses are making up the Hymn, the said Saman helps in this making up by showing forth the words of the hymn to an advantage by means of note-combinations and other details. Such being the case, when the Saman is employed in the Hymning, those words of the verse which are inter-related also come to be employed in the same: consequently, inasmuch as the term ‘svardrk’ also occurs in the text of the verse, it follows that that term also is employed in the Hymning;- hence we conclude that, inasmuch as it is for the sake of something else, its presence must be indicative of time. Says the Opponent “The term ‘svardrk’ is only contained in the verse, the actual injunction 14 of the Rathantara, which must set aside what might be merely inferred from the presence of a particular term; hence the sentence could directly point to the looking being an accessory "

Answer-As a matter of fact, one thing can be taken as setting aside something else only when it is found that, if it did not set aside this latter, it would serve no useful purpose In the case in question, the injunction in question does not become useless by not setting aside the implication of the term ‘svardrk’, as even so it serves the very useful purpose of indi- cating the time during performances It might be argued that-” on account of the presence of the term in the Mantra, and by reason of the injunction of the Saman, the connection of the term with the act of Hymning is direct, while the relationship of an act and its means is expressed by Syntactical Connection, and as both facts are cognised by valid means of knowledge, there can be no incom- patibility in the case " But it is not so; if one accepts the relationship of an act and its means, in the case of the term as taken apart from the Mantra-text, he cannot at the same time, recognise the connection of that word, uttered only once, with the Hymning;-in fact, if he did recognise this connection, he should utter it again, not otherwise. Hence the relationship of the act and means also should rest in the Hymn itself. What is recognised is the connection of the means with the connection of the act in the Hymn itself,-not in the connection of the Hymn; as no particular means are present. Thus then, it " ADHYAYA X, PADA VI, ADHIKARAṆA (2). 1910 being proved that there is no inconsistency between the text of the Mantra and the injunction of the Saman and the sentence one should look at the Seardrk’,-the presence of the word should be taken as serving the purpose of indicating the time. That is why we say that the presence of the term serves to indicate the time It has been argued that—” Where both difference and non-difference are possible, it is difference that should be accepted, and where both Injunction and Reiteration are possible, it 19 better to nocept the Injunction; and as we find the Injunctive affix, we should conclude that at is an Injunc- tion.” Our answer to this is as follows:-True, between Injunction and Reiteration, Injunction is superior, on the ground that it puts forward something new; but this can be so only if there is no other means of know- ledge bearing upon the matter in question In a caso, however, where the admissibility of what torms tho subject-matter of the Injunction happens to be already expressed by some other word, or already implied by something that has gone before, - such cases, the subject-matter being one that is already known, the text (though with the Injun, tive affix) has to be taken as only reiterative-Now in the case in question, the act of ’looking’ 18 already indicated by the man’s own needs, because unless the nan looka at tlungs, he cannot take part in the activities involved in the performance ; and thus the act of looking being already thus implied, the injunctivo affix (inviksēta) must be taken to be merely restorative But the direct assertion that C on the starting of the Rathanlara, one should close his eyes’ would set aside the looking if it were only implied; just as the Prajāpatī-vratas (observancos laid down for the Religious Student) set aside, by Direct Assertion, all those activities which would be prompted by the desires of the man.” LC " It is not so understood Why? -Because it is prefaced by the beginning of a particular action- ’ when the Rathanlara is started’, so that when this starting has been done, this sentence has fulfilled 198 purpose, and hence it cannot set aside the looking that is unplied by the needs of the man. It has been argued that” the connection of what is denoted by the term ‘svardṛk’ and the ’looking’ is got at by Syntactical Connection, wlule the act of looking is already indicated by the meaning of the sontonce and the undicative term in the shape of the root drah’ (to gec In the term ‘avardrk’)” Our answer to this is as follows The term ‘pratt’ (in the sentence Svardrsham prati vikķēta ‘) is a preposition, and hence it sigrufies, by Direct Denotation, the fact that what is denoted by the term ‘avardṛk’ is An indicative signi And it has been already understood that Direct Assertion sets aside the Indicative word, as also Syntactical Connection –Or, there need be no setting aside of Syntactical Connection in this case, what Syntactical Connection signifies 18 mere relationship, sometimes the rela- tionship between an act and its means, sometimes the relationship between the qualification and the qualified, sometimes the relationship between the indicator and the indicated and so forth, several other forms of relation- 1920 SHABARA-BHĀṢYA: ship; in the case in question, it is the relationship of indicator and indicated which is found necessary and hence accepted as the particular relationship; so that Syntactical Connection is not set aside. As for instance, in common parlance, when it is said it is flaslung at the tree’, the relation- ship between the Tree and the Flashing is not that of cause and effect, all that is understood is that the Tree is mentioned as the mark, the indicator of the flashing that has proceeded from somewhere else In the samne manner, in the case in question the term * svardrk’ is mentioned as the indicator of the looking, which has been already prompted by the needs of the man, and hence the sentence is not useless, because, unless the indicative and the indicator are spoken of in a sentence, their relationship cannot be recognised It has been argued that on account of the presence of the root ‘draha’ (’ to son’, m‘avardṛk’), the indication of this is honoured (under the Purvapakea view)” L L 4 6

"

But as a matter of fact, we do not find even this (reason) yielding the con- clusion desired (by the Purvapakşın) ‘The root draho can denote the art of looking only when it is used for its own sake, not when it is used for the sake of something else in the term ‘svardık’, the root drshi’ appears with a prefix, and hence it is understood to be a subordinate factor in the character of the Nominative Agent, which agent is the predominant factor When the Nominative Agent is expressed, he is not recognised as an indicative of the act of looking, because the root drshi’ is an entirely subservient factor, and the word that denotes the Nominative Agent cannot be construed with the root viksa’, to look’ If what is enjoined were that one should look at Svardrk’, -and the question arose who Svardrk’ was, the only answer available would be that it is one looking at whom has been enoined, so that being in ignorance, we could not determine what should be done On the other hand, if the meaning of the sentence is that One should accomplish the looking by means of the Svardrk’, there also, as it is not known who or what Seardrk’ 18, the same difficulty remains –Thus we find that if we hurriedly accept any of these constructions (possible under the Pūrvapakṣa), we follow neither the Indicative Word nor the Syntactical Connection On the other hand, if we connect the Looking with the Svardrk as the indicative (of time), then at the time of the utterance of the word ‘vikpēta’, the said connection does, somehow or other, become recognised, -then, as for the connection with the Hymning, it is not inconsistent even with the denotation of the Nominative Agent, as the necessary co-ordination is there, it being connected with ‘Ishāna’ as a qualification of this latter,— in the Mantra– Ishānam svardrsham tasthusaḥ’ —It is for these reasons that we assert that the sentence Svardrsham prati viksēta’ is connected with the act of Hymning, as indicating the time " “What is the use of all this discussion?” If the looking’ were taken as an accessory, then, in the case of the transference laid down in the text Rathantaramuṭṭarayorqāyatı”, the injunc- tion, that when the Rathantara starts one should close his eves’. would present itself; and as the term ‘svardrk’ is not present in the Uttarā ADHYAYA X, PADA VL, ADHIKARANA (2). 4 *、 1921 verses, there would be no restriction regarding the ’looking’,-in accordance with the Purvapakṣa, whils according to the Siddhânia, the Svardrk’ being an indication, the time for looking would not be past till the time indicated (ie at the time that the word ‘svardrsham’ is uttered during the singing), and hence the restruction becomes secured (that the Looking should be done at that time) ADHIKARANA (3): At the & Gavamayana’ sacrifice, during the Prathya-Sadaha”, the Bṛhat’, and the ‘Rathantara’ should be separated. SUTRA (4) C [PURVAPAKṆA]—” IN THE CASE OF THE PRSTHYA’, AS THERE IS SIMUL- TANEOUS INJUNCTION, BOTH THE SAMANS SHOULD BE CHANTED; AS IN THE CASE OF THE ĒKĀHA ‘.’ Bhāsya There is the following text - Prathyah sudaho brhadrathantarasāmā ’ [‘The Prathya-sadaha should have the Brhat and Rathantara Saman”] In regard to this, there arises the question-Should, on each of the six days, both the Samans be chanted? Or, on some days, the Brhat and on some, the Rathantara » “Why should such a question arise at all?” C The compound brhadrathantarasāmā’ becomes applicable to the ‘Sadaha’ in both cases,-1 e. when the term ‘brhadrathantara’ is taken as standing for the Brhat and Rathantara conjointly, as also when it is taken as standing for them severally. Hence what is to be considered 18, whether the compound *brhadrathantarasāmā’ is a Bahuvriki containing within itself a Dvandva, it being expounded as `bi hadrathantarē sāmani yasya’ (‘at which the Brhad Rathantara are the Saman ‘), or it is a multi-membered ‘Bahuvrih,,— being expounded as ‘brhat yasya-rathantaram_yasya—ṣāma’ [’that which has Brhat –that which has Rathantara-for its Sāman’) —If it is the former Bahurriki, then both the Saman should be chanted conjointly on each of the six days, if, on the other hand, it is the latter kind of Bakuoriki, then they should be chanted separately (on different days) &

The Purvapakṣa on this question is as follows: -“Both the Samans should be chanted conjointly; hence we explain the compound as a Baku- vrihs with a Dvandva compound within itself Why –Because the terms ‘brhat’ and rathantara’ are in close proximity to one another, and we therefore regard the term ‘brhadrathantara’ as a complex formation, and when there is a complex formation, compounding is essential, further, in the case of a Dvandra compound, if it is taken as denoting its own meaning, then alone is Direct Denotation followed, as well as the intimate relationship between the terms preserved; otherwise, both these would be militated against. For this reason, we conclude that the compound ‘brhadrathan- tarasāmā’ is a Bahuvrihi with a Dvandva within itself;-and such being the case, on each of the six days, both the Samans should be chanted jointly. Why so? Because the Duandva compound, in this case, 18 of that kind which denotes mutual companionship between the two numbers; so that the meaning is that ‘wherever there 18 Rathantara, it should be accompanied . ADHYAYA X, PĀDA VI, ADHIKARAŅA (3). 1923 by the Brhat’. It is this mutual companionship that is meant by the term simultaneous injunction’ (in the Sutra). From this it follows that on each of the six days the two Samans are to be chanted together, ‘As in the case of the Ekaha (Sū.),—just as in accordance with the text ‘Jyogāmayāvinah ubhë kuryāt, samsarē ubhē kuryāt apach|tāva pyēkāhë bṛhadra- thantarë kuryāt’ [both the Brhat und Rathantara are chanted together at the Ekdha]” SUTRA (5) [SIDDHANTA-IN FACT, THE COMPOUND HAS BEE FORMED WITH THE “WO MEMBERS TAKEN SEPARATELY HENCE THERE IS NOTHING WRONG IN THEIR BEING, SEPARATED

Bhasya It is not right that both the Nūmans should be chanted on each of the six days, act, on some days, the Rathantara, and ou some days the Brhat is to be chanted, and it is not true that the two Samans are enjoined con- Jointly -Why? Because, even if the term ‘brhadrathantarasāmā’ bo expl- cable according to both views (the Pūrrapaksa as well as the Siddhānta), even so the night course would be to chant the two Samans separately.- -Why -Because at the Archetypal Sacrifice, the Pratha has been made up of only one Samman, hence in accordance with the Gonoral Law, it should’ be made up of only one Săman at the Eetypal Sacrifice also Such being the case, everything due to the Bhat as well as everything due to the Rathantara would be done

If it be held that-‘what makes up the Pratha is the combination of Bihat and Rathantura, neither the Bhat alone, nor the Rathantara along " then, in that case, the conditions of neither one would be adopted, as that would go against the General Law It is not only that the conditions of neither would be adopted, in fact, neither the Bihat-Prstha nor the Rathantara- Pratha would be secured And by reason of this discropancy, it would become an entirely different performDAIK (. 4 Then again, that the Pratha is to consist of the two Sămans combined can be only indirectly implied While such assertions as Brhat pratham bhavalı’, ’ Rathantaram pratham bharats’ aro iudicativo of the fact that the two are not to be combmed Further, the term brhat’, standing in nood of connot tion with the term ‘sāman’, cannot be connected with the term rathantara’ -and as for close proximity, this is equally present between the terms rathantara’ and ‘sāman’ -Then again, if the view is adopted that the terin brhadrathantara’ 18 a complex formation, the chances of its being taken as a Dvandva compound becomes very much lessened Nor is it necessary that whenever there is complex formation, there must be compounding; because the revered Panini has made it a matter of option -Further, the mention of the term ‘adman’ clearly shows that the Brhat and the Rathanlara are the characteristic marks of the Saman-From all this it follows that the two Sămans are not to be chanted together1924 G SHABARA-BHIṆYA : It has been explained already that even when the Sămans are separated, there is no incongruity in the term ‘brhadrathantaraṣāmā’, for instance, when it is said that for a month Devadatta is to feed on clarified butter and oil, what is moant is that he is to be fod, for half a month, with clarified butter, and for the other lulf, on oil,-sularly the term ‘brħad- rathantarasāma’ also may be explained As for the Ekaha, as it is to be done only on one day, there is no possibility of separation’, hence it has been said that ‘Samasta jyoqāmayavinah ubhē kuryūt”. SUTRA (6) [PURVAPAKSA continued]” AMONG THE EKADASHINAS’, THERE VERILY SHOULD BE COMBINATION, AS THAT IS WHAT IS DONE AT THE ARCHETYPE Bhasya “} There is the following text- Ēkādashinṇān prāyaniyodayanıyayoralı- ratrayorālabḥāta ‘|’ One should sacrifice the eloven anuals on the Prāyaniya ard Udayaniya Atiratras “| In regard to this, there arises the question -Should all the eleven annals be sacrificed on the Prāyaniya day, und again another eleven on the Udayaniya day” Or, out of the eleven animals, some are to be sacrificed on the Prāyaniya dax and some on the Udayaniya day ?—This question arises because the form of expression 14 the same in both cases

18 The Purvapakṣa is as follows The term ’ (verly ‘) implies the absence of all doubt Among the eleven animals there must be combination; e all the eleven are to be dealt with together on the Prayaniya day, and agam all the eleven, on the Udayaniya day —Why —Because this is what is done at the Archetype, at the Archetypal Sacrifice of the Jyotistoma all the animals are sacrificed together, and the same combination rendered admissible in the case in question also, by the General Law Further, the Prayanıya or the Udayaniya day is spoken of only as a distinc- tive qualification, and when all the eleven are found to be enjomed in con- nection with the Prāyaniya day, there is nothing to differentiate which ones fron, among the eleven are so enjomed Similarly in connection with the Udayaniya also -From all this it follows that there should be combination.” SUTRA (7) [PURVAPAKSA-concluded- • 77 ALSO BECAUSE DISTRIBUTIVE TREATMENT HAS BEEN PROHIBITED Bhāṣya “There is prohibition of distributive treatment in the text ‘On the Prayaniya and the Udayaniya, one should sacrifice the eleven animals’. In the ordinary way, there is distributive treatment, as asserted in the text one animal should be sacrificed on each day’, and in accordance L 1926 SHABARA-BHĀṆYA : with this, one animal would be sacrificed on the Prayaniya day and the other animals on other days-Under the circumstances, what the text in question does is to prohibit those to be dealt with on the other days; and all of them come to be dealt with at the Prāyaniya, and so again at the Udayaniya. Hence it follows that all the animals concerned may be sacrificed on the Prayaniya day 11 SUTRA (8). [SIDDHANTA]-IN FACT, THERE SHOULD BE SEPARATE TREATMENT, ON THE BASIS OF DIRECT ASSERTION,AS IN COMMON PRACTICE. Bhārya The term ‘v’ (’m fact’) implies the rojection of the view set forth above. It is not right that they should all be dealt with together.-there should be separate treatment —Why -Bocause of the Direct Assertion of Duality; wo have the assertion of Duality in the word ‘prāyaniyodayani- yayoh’; and this duality is asserted as something to be made up,-and not as a distinctive feature-Why ?-The injunction of the Ekadashini being close by, what is done is that after having enjoined the Ekadashini by direct declaration,-agam having indicated it by Direct Assertion,-for the purpose of laying down the purpose, it is again added—’ Prāyanıyoda- yan yayoh’, the compounding found here becomes possible because members of the Deandra compound are predominant factors, and hence there is need for the compounding The compound being there, it denotes mutual companionship, so that the Ekadashini appertains to the Prayaniya, not alone, by itself, but as accompanied by the Udayaniya,-similarly it apper- tains to the Udayaniya also (as accompanied by the Prayaniya). Hence the significance of the sentence is complete with the whole lot (of the eleven animals). If, on the other hand, the two (Prayaniya und Udayaniya) were not regarded as something to be secured, then the members of the Dvandva compound would become subordinate factors, and hence there being no need, the compound itself would become impossible; and in that case the signification of the sentence would be complete with each one of the eleven animals -As a matter of fact, we find it spoken of as something to be secured.-Hence there must be distributive (separate) treatment. As in common practice,—as in common practice, when it is said ‘give a hundred to Devadatta and Yañadatta’, what is signified by the compound (‘devattayajñadattayoh’) is what is enjoined (predicated), and what the sentence means 18 that the hundred that is to be given should be given to Devadatta and Yajñadatta’, and on the strength of the predica. tion of the Dvandva compound, the hundred’ is divided (between the two persons). Similarly in the case in question, the Eleven animals’ have to be divided (between the Prayaniya and the Udayaniya). 4 ADHYÄYA X, PĀDA VL, ADHIKARAṆA (4). SUTRA (9). ALSO BECAUSE THERE IS DISTRIBUTIVE TREATMENT AT THE АВОНЕТУРЕ. Bhāṣya 1997 For the following reason also there should be separate treatment.- “For what reason?"-There is distributive treatment at the Archetype: as we read in the text-At the Ekādashini one should sacrifice one every day It is a modification of this Ekadashini that is laid down in the text in question—’ One should sacrifice the Ekādashınas at the Prāyaniya and Udayaniya 4’ırātras’ -Hene, we should, as far as possible, preserve the distributive treatment SUTRA (10) IN CASE OF UNCERTAINTY, THE COURSE IS DETERMINED BY THE PROXIMITY OF THE ARCHETYPE Bharya Thus Sutra anticipates the following objection-Says the Opponent– “If distributive treatment is desired, then five will have to be sacrificed on one day and six on the other; and it cannot be decided which number shall be sacrificed at which of the two-the Prūyaniya and the Udayaniya; -and as it cannot be ascertained, there will be uncertainty, and when there is uncertainty, there can be no activity, so that the injunction would become futile “. In answer to this, we have the Sutra -In the case of uncertainty,-1 e. the doubt raised in the objection,-proximity to the Archetype is what is principally followed, hence we decide that five of the animals would be sacrificed on the Prayaniya and six on the Udayaniya day. CC SÚTRA (11). IN THAT CASE THERE SHOULD BE ONLY THREE”,—if this is urged [then the answer is as given in the next Sutra.] Bhāṣya. “If you think that proximity to the Archetype is to be principally followed, then, in that case, only three should be sacrificed at the Prāyaṇiya, —just that number which would be in keeping with the plural number.” This objection has been urged against the Siddhänta. 1928 SHABARA-BHĀṆYA : SUTRA (12). NOT SO, BECAUSE OF EQUALITY; AS IN THE CASE OF THE PRAYAJAS Bhāsya. It cannot be as has been urged.-Why ?-Because of equality; when, as a matter of fact, the Ekadashimas have been laid down in connection with the Prayaniya and the Udayaniya, which are dependent upon one another,- and at neither of the two are all the animals to be sacrificed,–with reference to that one at which they are not sacrificed, their entirety becomes set aside, and you will therefore have to admit of this rejection at least to the extent of that number which is not sacrificed at one or the other of the two days.- Hence the distribution should be equal just as in the case of the Prayājas ; for mstance, the six additional Prayājas, being the modifications of the first and the last, are equally distributed between both, similarly in the case in question, the animals shall be so distributed over the two days as to make the distribution as equal as possible, and if there is an odd animal left over, it shall be sacrificed at the Udayaniya, as that would be in accordance with the proximity to the Archetype Thus we find that there is no force in the objection. SUTRA (14) [SIDDHANTA]—IN FACT, THERE SHOULD BE DISPERSAL, ON ACCOUNT OF THE INJUNCTION. ’ " Bhāṣya. The term tu (in fact’) implies the rejection of the view set forth above. What has been urged above on the basis of reasoning should be set aside on the strength of Direct Injunction; and the Direct Injunction 18 that one Saman only is to be used as ‘Pratha’ and the others are to be used as ‘Parisāma ‘.-” How so?”–There is the (injunctive) text—’ Pavamânë rathantaram karoti, ārbhavē bṛhat, madhya starāṇı, vairūpam hotuḥ pretham, 33 1930 SHABARA BHAṆYA: varājam brahmasāma, shākvaram maitrāvarunasāma’. ADHIKARANA (6): The Vairūpa-Sāman’ and the ’ Vais rāja-Saman’ are to be used as ‘Prstha’. SŪTRA (15). [PURVAPAKṢA]—“THE VAIRUPA-SAMAN SHOULD FIND PLACE IN THE ENTIRE SACRIFICE, BECAUSE OF ITS CONNECTION WITH THE (ENTIPE) SACRIFICE; JUST LIKE THE TRIVRT’, IT SHOULD HAVE ONLY ONE SIMAN.” Bhasya Thero 14 the Jyotistoma-sacrifice, at which there are two particular termunu Ukthyn and Sodashin, in connection with these, wo road– * Uhthyo vairī pa-sāmā Sodashi vairājasāmā’ [‘The Ukthya is that which has the Vairupa-Sāman, the Sodashin is that which has the Vardja- Saman ‘1 In regard to this, there arises the question-Does the l’aerūpa-Sāman enter into the whole of the Ukthya-sacrifice, land tho Vairāja-Sāman, into the whole of the Sodashin-sacrifice? Or are they to be used only in place of the ‘Pratha’! The Purvapaksa is as follows Throughout the whole sacrifice, there should be the one Saman, the Vairüpa only (at the Ukthya), and the Vairāja only (at the Sodashin) –Why ?-Because of its connection with the entire sacrifice, without any specification, the Vairupa-Säman has been enjoined in connection with the whole sacrifice (Ukthya),—so also the Vaja (with the Sodashin), consequently neither of them can be used in place of the Pratha only–Just as in the case of the Trivrt’,– in the case of the text- The Agniştoma is trivrt’,-the Trivrt-stoma enters into the whole sacrifice (of the Agnistoma),—in the same manner, the two Samans in question should extend respectively into the whole of the sacrifices –Or, as in the case of the text “Dhēnurathaiṣa bhūrvaishvadēvah trwydēva sarvaslanya vishva- vatyah stotriyā dhēnurdaksınā,”—the milch cow (Dhēnu) is used in place of the entire Sacrificial Fee, so also should the two Samans in question enter respectively into the whole of the two sacrifices (Ukthya and Şoḍashın).” L SUTRA (16). [SIDDHANTA IN REALITY, THEY SHOULD BE USED ONLY IN PLACE OF THE ‘PRSTHA’, BECAUSE OF THE PRESENCE OF THE INDICATIVE OF THE ARCHETYPE Bhāṣya. In reality, the two Sämans should be taken as to be used in place of the Pratha.-How-In the two compound words ‘Vairüpa-sāmā’ and 1932 SHABARA-RHÄṆYA:

  • Vairāja-adma’, there is the term ‘Saman’ which is indicative of the Archetype; and it indicates that compounds are to be taken as Bahuuriki; so that what is enjoined is, not the Varupa-Saman or the Vairija-Saman, But the fact of the sacrifice having the character of having the Varupa Saman and the character of having the Vairāja Saman. The connection too is with the Sacrifice, not with the Hymn; in fact, even in a single Hymn- if the Vairūpa and the Vairaja Säman are chanted, the sacrifice can have the character of having the Varupa Saman and the character of having the Vairāja Saman.-How ?-If the Saman is laid down in connection with a Hymn, then it would be chanted over all Hymns; because all equally are Hymns-such however is not the case; hence, when over a single Hymn, the Vatrupa and the Vairāja Säman are chanted, there comes about the oharacter of having the Vatrupa Saman and the character of having the Vairāja Saman. And when this is done in connection with a single Hymn, they should be used in the place of ‘Pratha’, because the character of having the Vairupa Saman that is enjoined is a quality, and so also 18 the character of having the Vairaja Saman,- and as such they could be used only in place of a quality of the same kind;-at the Archetype, the qualities of this kind are the character of having the Brhat Saman and the character of having the Kathantara Sāman ;-so that the presence of these indicatives of the Archetype shows that the character of having the Vairüpa Säman and the character of having the Vairāja Sāman are to be used in the place of ’ Pretha ’ ¡—in accordance with the principle arrived at in Sutra 8. 1. 2.– From all this it follows that the two Samans in question are to be used in the place of ‘Pratha”.
