For the following reason also the Manase should be regarded, not as a distinct ‘Day’, but as an accessory “For what reason “-Because it is, spoken of as the dismissal of the Tenth there is a text speaking of the Mänasa as the ‘dismissal of the Tenth’ ‘What is known as the Manasa in the dismissal of the Tenth Day’; this text speaks of the Mänasa as the ’ dismissal *— 1e the end of the Tenth Day’. This shows that it is the end of the Tenth Day’, and it is not an independent act by itself.-From this also it follows that it is an accessory of the Tenth Day’, not a distinct act. 1 1950 SHABARA BĦAŞYA : SUTRA (40). ALSO BECAUSE OF THE EXPRESSION ON THE TENTH DAY’, WHICH SPEAKS OF IT AS AN ACCESSORY Bhāsya For the following reason also the Mūnasa should be regarded as an Агоевногу. “How “-It is only in that case that the following texts which speak of accessories, would be explicable (a) Dashame’ hanı mānasāya prasarpanti’ [’ On the Tenth Day, they proceed to the Manasa ‘]; -(b) ‘Dashamē’ hanı sarparājñíbhɩr rqbhih stuvants’[‘They hymn with the Sarparājili verses, on the Tenth Day’], in these toxts, the Tenth Day 18 spoken of as the principal factor and the Cup is spoken of as something forming part of that factor. It must therefore be taken as an accessory of the Tenth Hymn’, not as a distinct act SUTRA (41) 4 BECAUSE THE NUMBER IS CONSISTENT (ONLY UNDER THIS VIEW) Bhāsya * P The number denoted by the name Drādashāha’ (‘Twelve Days’) too becomes consistent only if the Manasa 19 an accessory, otherwise the name * Drūdashāha’ would be applied to Thirteen Days, and as such would be inconsistent, as ’twelve’ is not expressive of Thirteen It has been argued that “the number would apply figuratively, as in the case of the number thousand “That however 19 not possible, as in the case of the number thousand, the things numbered have been cognised by other authoritative means of knowledge: and as the numbered things have been actually found to be more than a thousand, the term ’thousand’ is taken as applied to them figuratively In the case in question however thero 18 no authoritative evidence to show that the number of things is actually Iarger (than twelve), on the basis whereof the figurative application could be assumed As for the declaration-’ Anayā tvā pātrēna, etc.’, it only lavs down an embellishment of the Cup, and hence what it enjoins is a repetition of the sacrifice on the tenth day.and it does not enjoin a distinct act; this we have already explained before. C Such being the case, the direct declaration in question cannot justify the assumption of another ‘Day’-nor is there any other means of knowledge pointing to such another action, on the basis whereof we could take the term as applicable to a larger number of things.-Consequently the term ’twelve’ cannot be taken as used figuratively. Then again, it has been asserted that-“the term ‘Duädashāha’ being the name of a group of acts, as many would be taken as included in it as there would be in the context,—and the repetition would be in the form of the name “.–Thus also is not right. It is true that the term is the name ADHYAYA X, PĀDA VI, ADHIKABANA (13), C 1951 of a group of acis, but not in such a way as would be inoqnsistent with actual facts; the fact of the mattor is that there are twelve acts measured by ‘days’ which have been grouped together and given the name Dvādashdha’ ; it is in this sense that the name applies to the group of acts, not merely in its verbal form. In the case of the names of all acts, the name is applicable on the basis of the actual facts, which is in a way referred to by the name; it is never applied irrespectively of the real state of things, as a mere technicality, like such terms as irddhi’, ‘guna’ and tre like This is what is found to be the case with all such names as ’ Agnihotra’, ‘Shyëna”, Jyotistoma Thus we conclude that the torm dvā ishāha’ is a name applied on the basis of facts, not without basis in facts. Hence the argument C

of the Opponent has no force at all. SUTRA (42) IN CONNECTIN WITH THE EXCESS OF ANIMALS, THERE IS ONLY ONE THAT IS MENTIONFD Bhāsya กา accessory of the

The text’ Yah For the following reason also the Mānasa 18 Dvādashāha -“For what reason?"-With the excess of animals,–the excess that is indicated by the texts is of one only, not of two pashuratirichyēta sa andrāgnaḥ kāryah’ [The animal that is in excOSA should be dedicated to Indra-Aqni ‘having laid down the Ēkādashini in connection with the Dvādashāha, indicates that after the Ēkādashini has been dealt with, there is one more animal that is required. [According to the Pūrvapaksa] either there would be no more animals required, or it would not be one only - How so?” –Thore are eleven animals (of the Ēkādushini), and there are twelve Days’ (of the Dvūdashāha) that there are twelve ‘Days’ is shown by the text speaking of only one more boing roqured, if there had been thirteen days’ (as in the Purvapakṣa, the Mānasa being the additional thirteenth day ‘), then there would have been two more required, not only one -From this also it follows that the Mānasa is an accessory of the Dvādashāha, not a distinct act by itself. 4 SUTRA (43) THE ‘EULOGY’, OR THE ‘DECLARATION’, IS NOT INCONSISTENT WITH ITS BEING AN ACCESSORY; AS IN THE CASE OF THE C VRATAS’. Bhasya, This Sutra supplies the answer to two Sutras (34 and 35) It has been argued (a) that “the Minasa should be regarded as a distinct ‘day’ because it has been declared to be different (under Sú 34), –and (b) that there must be difference, as the Drādashāha has been eulogised 1952 SHABARA-BRISTA: through the Manasa; no one thing is ever eulogised through itself”.-The answer to this is as follows :—’ There is no inconsistency in this; because the Composite has often been found to be eulogised through its component part; for instance, the Samvatsara-sattra has been eulogised through the details of the Mahāvrata (which is one of the components of the Samvatsara-sattra). For instance, the text Yanti vā ētë mithunād yè samvatsaramupayantı, antarvēdī mithunau sambhavatah, tēnawa mithunā na yantı ‘—describes the defect of the whole Composite (Samvatsara-sattra), and then palliates it by pointing out the redeeming feature of the Mahāvrata, which is a component of that Saura,-the whole thus being eulogised through its part. In ordinary experience also, the whole is often eulogised through the part; when, for instance, Devadatta is said to be ‘beautiful’ on account of his long hair;— simularly in the case in question also, the Deadashāha would be eulogised through the Manasa (one of its accessories), and there would be no incongruity in this SUTRA (44). It is on account oF THE DECLARATION THAT IT IS NOT TAKEN AS ENDING WITH THAT. Bhāṣya. It has been argued (under Si 36) that” thero is a text speaking of the Doddashāha as ending with the Manasa,-this would be applicable only if the Manasa were a distinct Day’ by itself, not if it were only an accessory of the Drädashāha; in the latter case it would be ending with the ‘Preparation of the Wife’ -Our answer to this is as follows —It 8 on account of the declaration that il 18 not taken as ending with that; as a rule, the ‘Days’ of the Dvādashāha end with the Preparation of the Wife’, but it is a peculiar feature of the Tenth Day’ that it ends with the Mānasa, in accordance with the declaration– Having prepared the wives, they proceed to the Manasa ‘;—and for a declaration there is no burden too heavy For this reason also there is no incongrunty in our view ·

From all thus we conclude that the Manasa 1a an accessory of the Tenth ‘Day’, not a distinct act by itself ADHIKARAŅA (14): The ‘Sattra’ is to be performed by several ’ Sacrificers’. SUTRA (45). [PURVAPAKṢA]—” ONLY ONE MAN SHOULD PERFORM THE SATTRA, LIKE ITS ARCHETYPE Bhasya " The Dvādashāha and other Sattras form the subject-matter of the prosent Adhikarana. In regard to these, there arises the question-Should only one man perform the Sattra Or several ? The Purvapaksa is as follows Only one, why ?-it is like its Archetype, at the Jyotışfoma (which is the Archetype of the Sattras), there is only one Sacrificer; and as the Sattra has that for its Archetype, it should have only one Sacrificer, in accordance with the General Law But we find several sacrificers spoken of-in such texts as-Those who, knowing this, have recourse to the Sattra’, ‘knowing thus they have recourse to the Sattra’ —The answer to that is that the Sattia has been enjoined for persons desiring certain rewards; and these must be many, independent of one another; so that, even when each of them performs the Satira singly by himself, it is possible to speak of the performance of the Satira as done by several men; as in ordinary life, even when men do an act separately, the plural number is used. If the Heaven were to rain many people would cultivate the fields’, or, if there is a good harvost, many Brahmans would porforin si rifices’. Similarly in the Veda also, we find such expressions as- Having risen from the Sattra, they should perform the Prathashamaniya sacrifico’.–In the case in question also the plural number in axiran’ and ‘yajēran’, may be similarly explained.” L SUTRA (46) [SIDDHANTA]-ON ACCOUNT OF DIRECT DECLARATION, IT SHOULD BE PERFORMED BY SEVERAL MEN Bhasya 事 It is not right that there should be only one Sacrificer, not several. In fact several persons should perform the Sattra-sacrifice -“Why ? Because there 18 a Direct Declaration; there is the declaration containing the verbs äsiran’ and ‘upēyuh’, all in the plural form, which shows that what is enjoined is connected with plurality (of men); and this fact, thus directly declared, sets aside the notion of there being only one Sacrificer, which is based only upon the implications of the General Law.1954 SHABARA-BHĀṢYA : SUTRA (47) IF IT IS ARGUED THAT " IT IS A MERE ASSERTION is as follows]. Bhāsya. [then the answer It has been argued (under Sü 45) that “the plural number may be taken as based upon the similarity of action, as in ordinary experience we meet with such expressions as they would perform sacrifices’,-and in the Veda also, Much expressions as they should perform the Prathashamaniya-sacrifice’, the same would be the case in the present instance also This has got to be refuted, [and the refutation 19 as follows]. 4 4 SUTRA (48). • THAT CANNOT BE, AS ONE’ IS MENTIONED (IN CONNECTION WITH ANOTHER) Bhasya That it should have only one Sacrificer is not possible for the Sattra. Why ?-Because ‘one’ is mentioned in connection with another -How 50 *— There is the following declaration-One who receives a gift at the Sattra eats a dead corpse; only one should perform the sacrifice’, where having (in the first clause) disposed of the Sattra, the second clause lays down, in regard to another sacrifice, the fact of there being only one performer, and this implies that at the Saitra there should be several sacrificers . As for the analogy cited of ordinary experienco’, that is not right because in ordinary life, the word is only a reiteration of what has been known from elsewhere, and hence when it is used it is understood to be based upon the presence of surular activities. The instance that has been exted (under Sú 45) of the Udarasāniya— it all right in regard to the Udarasāniya, as there mere performance hus been laid down in connection with various Udarasāniya», and it is this plurality, thus indicated, that is reiterated in the text cited, this has been already explained. In the case in question however, the activity is one prompted entirely by the verbal injunction, and the verbal injunction connects the performance of the Sattra with performers, as qualified by plurality, so that when the action comes to be undertaken on the authority of the verbal Text, duo significance has to be attached to the pluraity; hence It follows that the Sattra should be performed by several persons. SUTRA (49) C THERE IS ALSO A TEXT SHOWING COMMINGLING Bhāṣya 1 For the following reason also there should be several sacrifices at the Sattra.-” For what reason ↑ “’. -Because we find ‘comnungling’; there is a ADHYAYA X, PĀDĀ VI, ADHIKARAŅA (14), [ 1935 text which declares the commingling’ of several ‘Fires’ in one place- ‘Panchabhih pashubhıryakṣyamânaḥ sannıvapēran’, ‘Sāvītrāni hogyantaḥ sannua pèran ‘[’ When going to sacrifice five animals they should commingle the Fires’, ‘When going to offer the Savitra libations, they should commingle the Fires’] It is only when several persons perform the act conjointly. that such ‘commungling’ of the Fires is possible, if e.ch man did it separately on his own account, the mention of commingling’ could not be explamed. From this also it follows that there should be sovoral Sucrificers at the Sattra. 6 SUTRA (50) IF THERE WERE ONLY ONE PERFORMER, THEN THE SPECIFIC MENTION f OF SEVERAL WOULD BE MEANINGLESS Bhasya.

For the following reason also we conclude that the performance 14 done hr several persons conjointly” For what reason ? “—We rend —’ Yo vas bahūnām yaramānānām grhapatih sa sattrasya pratyētā sa h bhūmsthām rddhimārdhnot’ [ Among the several sacrificers one who is the master of the house is the propounder of the Sattra, and he obtams the lughest prosperity’], this text speaks of a particular rosult accruing to one Master of the House operating with several sacrificers, and houre shows that the performance is by several persons jointly Otherwise, if there were only one Sacrificer,-as thore would be only one Agent and only one result,-any distinction between general and special results would be incongruous, and hence any mention of a particular result accruing to the Master of the House would be meaningless, and yet, we do find such a particular result mentioned,—from thus also we conclude that several persons should perform the Sattra-sacrifice. C ADHIKARANA (15): At the Sattra, the Sacrificers’ them- selves act as Priests’. SUTRA (51). [PORVAPAKSA]” OTHERS SHOULD BE THE PRIESTS, AS AT THE ARCHETYPE.” Bhāṣya. Sattras are the subject-matter of consideration here also-It has been explained that it is performed by several Sacrificers, The question that arises is.-Are the sacriticers of the Sattra themselves to get as ‘Priests’ ? Or are others to be secured?

The Purvapakea is as follows Other persona should be secured as Priests Why 1-At the Jyotistoma, which is the Archetype of Sattras, it has been declared that other persons should be secured as performers (priests); similarly in the case in question also, when the Sacrificers are performing the sacrifice, they should, in accordance with the General Law, secure other persons; it is only thus that the performance would be like the Archetype””. SUTRA (52). [SIDDHANTA-IN FACT, THE SACRIFICERS THEMSELVES SHOULD BE THE ‘PRIESTS’, BECAUSE OF THE CONNECTION OF THE PRIESTS ’ NAMES HENCE THE CHARACTER OF SACRIFICER’ BELONGS TO THE PRIESTS Bhasya

It is not right that other persons should be secured as priests’; in fact, the Sacrificers themselves should be the Priests “Why?"-Because of the connection of the Priests’ names; the embellishment of Initiation, which is done for the Sacrificer only, has been laid down in connection with the names of the priests, Adhvary and the rest, which are all based upon the per- formance of certain functions; which shows that the Sacrificers are connected with the functions of the Adhwarya and other priesta-“How so?"-It is only when they perform these functions that they can be referred to by names based upon those functions,–not otherwise, from this we conclude that they are actually connected with those functions: “What is that text where the Initiation is spoken of ? " It is thus Adhvaryurgrhapatim diksayitva brahmanam dikṣayati, tato hotāram, tata udṇātāram’, and so on all the priests become connected with Initiation.-From this it follows that the Sacrificers themselves—and none others–should perform the Priestly Functions. ADHTİYA X, PADA VI, ADHIKABANA (15). SUTRA (53). 1987 “THE EMBELLISHMENT WILL BE OF THE PERFORMER, ON THE STRENGTH OF THE DECLARATION,—AS IN THE CASE OF THE INSTALLER IF THIS IS URGED [then the answer is as in the next Sütra]. 1

Bhāṣya. " The Opponent may argue as follows:- “It is not right that the Sacrificers should be the Priests; because at the Archetype, the Priests are declared to be other than the Sacrificer; hence, as the Archetype, so in the se in question also, the Priests should be other than the Sacrificers. It 19 the same Pūrvupakṣa view that is reiterated Only it is necessary to refute the Siddhänta view. It is this refutation that is set forth in the Sutra–The Embellishment will be of the Performer, on the strength of the Declaration, as in the case of the Installer; -How so -All that we read in the Text 18 The Adhvaryu, having initiated the Master of the House, initiates the Israhman-priest —even if the Performers (of the priestly func tions) are other than the Master, the text may be taken as laying down the embellishment of Initiation for those Performers, mentioning these latter by their names (brahman’ and the rest), and there would be nothing icon- gruous in this ;-as it would be as in the case of the Installer ;-1.0. it would be like the case of Fire-installation, in connection with which the Embellish- ment of the Performers has been laid down, in the following text-’ One who is going to instal the Fire on the following day should keep an observance during the night, he should not eat meat, nor approach his wife’,-here the declaration enjoins an observance for the Adhvaryu;—or again, in connection with the Jyotiștoma, wo road all the Priests keep & fast’, where fasting has been laid down for the Priests,- –in the same manner, in the case in question also, the Embellishment spoken of should be taken to be that of the Priests.” SUTRA (54). WHEN THERE IS A DOUBT, IT SHOULD BE AS DETERMINED BY REASON, AS AT THE ARCHETYPE. Bhāṣya. It is not right that the Priests should be other than the Sacrificere ; in fact, the Sacrificers themselves should be the Prassla Why 1 When there is a doubt as to whether the same persons who are the Sacrificera should be the Priests, or these should be different from them,-the reasonable course is that those same should be the Priests; the reason for this has been explained already above, under Su. 52; from what has been said under that Sutra, we conclude that those same should be the Priests. It has been argued that “the Embellishment shall be of the Priests, as at the Installation “.-But that is not right. “Why?"-When the Embellishment (Initiation) has been laid down in connection with the Sattra, 1968 SHABARA-BHIGYA: it may be taken, either as enjoined for the Priests and serving no useful purpose in connection with the Archetype,- -or as serving the same purposes as at the Archetype, but mentioned in the text as laying down the order of the Initiation, in view of the fact that there are several Sacrificers. Between these two alternatives, it is much simpler to take it as describing what is already known to be admissible (under the General Law, 1.6. the latter alternative), because in that case the text lays down only the order (of the Initiation), while if the Embellishment were for the Priests, it would be necessary to assume an unseen (transcendental) factor, and to take the text as laying down several factors Honce the right course is to take it as doscribing what is already admissible under the General Law, and not as laying down anything not already known. It has been argued that " Just as there is the injunction for the Priests to koop fast, or for the Fire-installer to keep an observance,- -90 in the case in question also, (it should be an injunction of the Initiation of the Priest)”. -But in those casos it 19 only right that it should be so, as there are the distinct declarations’ The Priests keep fust’, ‘He should keep an observanco during that night’,-in these cases what is laid down is something new, and hence there can be no suspicion of its being already known; hence the texts aro takon as Injunctions SUTRA (55) THE NAMES MAY BE TAKEN AS THOSE OF The Master, LIKE THE NAME

  • GRHAPATI -IF THIS IS URGED, [then the answer is as in the next Sutra] Bhasya Thus Sutra embodies an objection (against the Siddhanta) — ’ Why cannot the term Idharyu and the rest be taken as names of the Master, like the term grhapati - What would be the effect of this - The effect of this would be that the fact of the priestly functions being perforined by persons other than the Sacrifice, which is what is admissible under the General Law -would not have to be set aside, und at the same time, the Adheargu’ and the rest would come useful as standing for the Sacrifier,–just like the name · Grhapati L 559 The objection thus set forth is answered in the following Sūtra SUTRA (56) THAT CANNOT BE, BECAUSE THAT ALONE SHOULD BE ACCEPTED WHICH IS WELL-KNOWN, THE OTHER NAME IS APPLICABLE TO ONE WHO IS NOT ENDOWED WITH THAT CHARACTER Bhasya It is not right that the names Adhvaryu’ and the rest should be taken as standing for the Sacrificer,-hke the name Grhapat:’-“Why? " ADHYAYA X, PĀDA VI, ADHIKARAṆA (15). 1959 Because that alone should be accepted which is well-known; as a matter of fact, these names are well-known as applicable, on the basis of the functions performed, to persons performing the functions of the Adhraryu and other Priests, not to those performing the functions of the Sacrificer, hence it is not right or possible that they would be applicable to the Sacrificers who have no connection with the priestly functions.” But how about the name “Grhapati ‘"—The answer to that is that the name ‘Grhapatı’ (Master of the House) applies to the Master who has no connection with the priestly fimetions Further, even etymologically the term grhapat: 18 expressive of the Pati (Master), and hence it would be only night that it should be a name of the Sacrificer In fact, oven in connection with the Archetype, thus te has been used in that sonso, in the text ‘qhapaliryajzēta’ (‘The Master of the House should sacrifico’ As for the terms ‘Adhvaryu’ and the rest, on the other hand, which are related to the functions of the Prieste, they cannot, in any way oe applicable to the Master, hence, on account of their being connected with other functions, they are taken as different. 1 Further, it hey were equal, then the specific mention of ‘several’ we dd be ineaungless

For the following reason also, the Sacrificers themselves should perform The peatly functions - For what reason” -Says the text-‘Yo var bahānām yuzamānānām grhapatih sattrusya pralyētā sa ki bhūyisthām rddhi- märdhnote’ [‘Among the votal Sacrificers, the one Master of the House who 14 the propounder of the Satira secures the highest prosperity ‘];— the very specific montion of ono Sacrificer, by the torm grhupatı’, can be explated only if all the Sacrificers do not stand on the saine footing,- not otherwise, if all of them were to perform the functions of the Sacrificer, and did no other work, thon, in that case, there would be no distinction among them, so that there would be no justification for the specific mention of one of them If, however, the other Sacrificers perfrin both functions -those of the Sacrificer as well as those of the Priests—while the Master of the House perforins those of the Sacrificer only, then, in that case, the specific mention (of the latter) is right and proper From the said specific mention, therefore, it follows that the Sacrifters themselves aro Priests.

SUTRA (57) C 1 · THE MENTION OF THE INITIATED AND THE UNINITIATED’ ALSO IS NOT EXPLICABLE, AS THE FACTS ARE ALWAYS THERE Bhāsya. For the following reason also Sattras are performed by the Nacrificers themselves - For what reason?"-Because there is mention of the ‘initiated’ and the uninitiated’; the text says-The initiated perform the Sattra-sacrifice, the uninitiated perform the Ahina-sacrifice’, the two facts are always there-that those who are initiated perform sacrifices for their own sake alone, while those who are uninitiated perform sacrificos also for the sake of another sacrificer’; if, as regards these two facts, there were 1980 SHABARA-BHIṢYA: no difference between the Sattra and the Ahina,—then there would be no sense in the amertion made in the text quoted; on the other hand, if there is this distinction between the two that at the Satira all the acts are done by the initiated (sacrificer) only, while at the Ahina they are done by the uninitiated (priests), then the said assertion becomes explicable, not otherwise. Hence from the said assertion we conclude that at the Sattra all the functions are performed by the Sacrificers themselves. SUTRA (58). ALSO BECAUSE THERE IS NO SACRIFICIAL FEE. Bhāṣya.

For the following reason also the Sattra should be performed by the Sacrificers themselves.- “For what reason?"-Because there is no Sacrificial Fes; they say that at Sattras, there is no Sacrificial Fee; there is no cow, or cloth or gold given at it’, says the text, this declaration of the absence of the Sacrificial Fee is possible only if the priestly functions are performed by the Sacrificers themselves; not otherwise, if they were performed by others, then it would be impossible that there should be no Sacrificial Fee, no one ever takos up any activity for the sake of another person, unless there is some purpose of his own.-From this also it follows that Sallras are performed by the Sacrificers themselves “ ADHIKARAṆA (16): Difference between Sattra’ and ‘Ahina’. SUTRA (59) TO THE DVADASHÄHA BELONGS THE CHARACTER OF ‘SATTRA’, (a) WHEN THE INJUNCTION IS OF SITTING’ AND ‘PROCEEDING, AND (6) WHEN THERE IS A PLURALITY OF SAORIFICERS,-— THESE BEING ASSOCIATED WITH THE NAME ‘SATTRA’. Bhāṣya The Dvādashāha is the subject-inatter of this Adhikarana. C , It has been explained above that the Dvādashäha is a Sattra and also an Ahina, of these two forms of the Dvādashāha, the definition is provided now— when tho Dvādashāha has such and such characteristics, it is Saltro, and who it has such other characteristics it 18 Ahina’ -In order to understand this distinction, it is oxplained that (a) when there is injunction of sitting’ and * proceeding’, and (b) when there is plurality of Sacrificers, it should be regarded as Sattra, as a matter of fact, the two injunctions in the form of ‘ūsule’ (’they sit at ‘) and upayanti’ (’they proceed’) are always found to be associated with the name ‘Sattra’, in such texts as- (4) Those who knowing thus su at the Saltra’, and (b) Those who knowing thus, proceed to the Sattra’, -the name is also associated with the plurality of ancrificers, in such texts as The number of persons sitting at the Sattra should not be more than twenty four, nor less than seventeen’; so that of two things thus associated, when one is found, it brings the other to the mind. C SŪTRA (60). L TO IT BELONGS THE CHARACTER OF ‘AHINA’, (a) WHEN THE INJUNCTION IS OF SACRIFICING’, AND (b) WHEN THERE IS NO RESTRICTION

C REGARDING THE NUMBER OF MASTERS’. Bhāṣya. Question “When is tho Dvādashäha an

Ahina’ ?” Answer (a) When there is injunction of ‘sacrificing’, and (b) when the number of Sacrificers is not restricted, then it is understood to be Ahina, As a matter of fact, Ahinas are invariably enjoined by means of the root " yaja’ (’to sacrifice ‘), as in the text-’ Dvirātrēna yajēta. The number of Sacrificers, also at these is not restricted, while that of the Sacrificers at the Sattra 18 restricted that they must be many. The purpose served by the definition of things defined lies in itself, and no other purpose noed bo sought for. 35 < ADHIKARANA (17): At the Paundarika’ sacrifice, the Sacrificial Fee should be given only once. SUTRA (61) [PURVAPAKSA] -“AT THE ́AHINA’, THE RULE REGARDING THE SACRI- FICIAL FEE SHOULD VARY DAY BY DAY, BECAUSE IT IS AN ACCESSORY DETAIL, AND EACH DAILY PERFORMANCE IS DISTINCT BY ITSELF. Bhasya There is the Paundarika sacıfice lasung for eleven days, laid down in the text-’ Paundqrikēna ēkādaskarātrēna svārājyakāmo vajēta’ [‘Desiring Rovereignty of heaven, one should perform the Paundarika sacrifice lasting for eleven days ‘]; in connection with that sacrifice, we read-‘At the Paundarika one should give ten thousand,- a thousand horses on the eleventh ‘. C 4 In regard to this, there arises the question-Are the Ten Thousand’ and the Thousand Horses’ to be given every day (of the eleven days)? Or are they to be given only once 4 The Purvapalga is as follows “At the Ahina, the rule regarding the Sacrificial Fee should vary day by day Why Because the Sacrificial Fee 18 an accessory detail, and the ’ days’ (constituting the Paundarika sacrifice) are the principal factor, and when the Fee has been laid down through the name of the Composte whole ( Paundarika), it is with reference to the ‘Days’ composing that sacrifice; and when a subordinate detail is thus laid down, it must differ with each one of the principal factors’ m the shape of the components of that composite,-just as, whon Bathing or Smearing of Sandal-paste is laid down for a group of men, it is done by each member of the group ;—so should it be in the case in question In this way, the General Law also becomes followed, as it applies to each individual Rite; and the excess of the Fee would tend to the excess of the Reward (obtained by means of the Sacrifice).-From all thus it follows that there should be a distinct fee given on each day.” SUTRA (62). [Objection against Pūrvapaksa]BUT THE WHOLE IS ONE RITE (HENCE THERE SHOULD BE ONLY ONE FEE]. Bhāṣya. It is not right that there should be a distinct fee for each day; as a matter of fact, the ‘Ten Thousand (Cows)’ and the ‘Thousand (Horses)’ should be given only once.-Why ?-Because the whole is a single Rute; there is one purpose to be served by the Fees, viz. the securing of the ADHYAYA X, PĀDA VI, ADHIKARAŅA (17). 1963 services of the Priests; these services having been secured for the accom- plishment of the entire sacrifice with all its subsidiaries and details, there can be no need for the same in course of the performance of that sacrifice; and hence it is not done over again.-The argument that an oxcess in the accessory detail (Fee) will be conducive to excess in the reward ”,—this la so only when the fact of a certam thing being an accessory detail has been duly recognised, not otherwise, and the Fee us an accessory of the entire composite sacrifice, not of each of its components ;-as has been explained already-It has boon argued that The Conoral w appertains to cach individual rite and hence indicates the admisibility of the details at cach “. Bu the General Law becomes set aside when it is found that on the bassA of the direct declaration the Sacrificial Fce is taken as enjoined with reference to the entne sacrifice regarded as one composite whole there is no incðngru y at all. SUTRA (63). Honce [The Purvapakain’s answer to the above objection]-“THE INJUNCTION OF THE ACCESSORY DETAIL SHOULD PERTAIN TO EACH OF THE ‘DAYS’, LIKE THE ‘PRŞADĀJYA ‘.’ Bhasya CL It is not right that the Fee should be given only once; in fact, it has to be given several times Why What is laid down in the text m question 14 a peculiar feature of the Fees that are already known as to ho given day by day, and as such, that foature has also to be adopted day by day;- like the Prsadajya (Mixed Clarified Butter), just as in the case of the text, ‘Offers the Anuyājas with Mixed Clarified Butter’, the ’nuxed’ character of the Butter, which is a peculiar feature laid down in connection with the Anuyājas, is taken as refering to each one of the Anuyājas separately; so should it be in the case in question also.” SUTRA (64) [Another objection against the Purvapaksa]-THE FEES CONNECTED WITH THE JYOTISTOMA APPERTAIN TO ALL, AS ALL CONSTITUTE A SINGLE ACT, HENCE, AS AT THE ARCHETYPE, THERE SHOULD BE NO MODIFICATION IN THE MATTER OF THE FEES Bhāṣya. It 19 not right that there should be a separate Fee on cach day; in fact, it should be given once only as common to all days.-“How so?”- As a matter of fact, the Fees connected with the Jyotiatoma are given as appertaining to the whole set of acts (that go to make up that sacrifice); and all these Fees, which are for the purpose of securing the services of the Priests at the Composite Sacrifice, are admissible (according to the General1964 SHABARA BHIŞYA:

Law) at the Paundarika; it is in reference to the Fees thus admissible that the text in question lays down the peculiar feature that the Fee should be ’ten thousand (Cown) and one thousand (horses)’;-when this peculiar feature is thus laid down, it leads us to the conclusion that it is in modification of all those Fees that are given at the sacrifice (under the General Law), but it does not set aside the notion that the securing of services is done once only. From this it follows that it is to be given only once. As for the instance of the Anuyājas that has been cited, it is only right in the case of the Anuyājas, as it is a distinct substance (Mixed Olarified Butter in place of Clarified Butter) that is laid down; a substance is always laid down as an accessory of the sacrifice; so that when the Sacrifices are different, the substance used at one sacrifice does not help the other, hence it has to be used separately with each. In the case in question however there is only one securing of services (for the entire sacrifice, which is one composite whole), as already explained; hence there can be no analogy between the two cases. SUTRA (65) [Purvapakṣin’s answer to the second objection]–” AT THE DVADASHAHA THERE IS A SEPARATE FEE GIVEN ON EACH DAY, ON THE STRENGTH OF A DIRECT DECLARATION, AT OTHER SACRIFICES ALSO, WHICH HAVE THAT FOR THEIR ARCHETYPE, THERE SHOULD BE A MODIFICA- L TION IN THE NUMBER OF FEES Bhasya "” “It is not right that the Fee should be given once. in fact, the particular Fee that is laid down should be given separately day by day-Why ?- Because in connection with the Dvādashāha, there is the direct Declaration to the effect that one gives 1200 every day’,—the Pasndarika sacrifice has the Dvādashāha for its archetypo,—honce undor the General Law the Fees become payable every day, and in regard to these the text in question lays down the peculiar feature (that it should be ’ten thousand (cows) and one thousand (horses)’,-so that it follows that this feature is in modifica- tion of those same Fees that are connected with each part of the sacrifice ;- consequently thus peculiar feature of the Fees has to be adopted separately (on each day).” SŪTRA (66) [SIDDHANTA-IN FACT, INASMUCH AS THERE IS NO SEPARATE ‘SECURING OF SERVICES’, THE MODIFICATION SHOULD BE THAT OF THE WHOLE, Bhāṣya. It is not right that, there should be separate Fees on each day; in fact, the Fee is given only once.-“Why ? “Because there is no separate ADHYÄYA X, BĪDA VI, ADHIKARAŅA (17), £ 4 1965 securing of services’, therefore, it is the whole Fee that should be modified. It is in reference to the Sacrifice as a whole that Fees are prescribed.—“How so !"-Because that is what is needed by the raan; the man wishes to do that alone which is fruitful;-when the man proceeds to do any such act and is on the look out for assistance,—it is for that occasion that the text lays down the hiring’ (of priosts);-now, as a natter of fact, no single component part of a sacrifice is fruitful,—the fruit following from the sacrifice as a whole; no that, when the ’luring’ has been done with reference to the whole sacrifice, it should continue till the accomplishment of the whole; so that there can be no hiring’ during the intervals of the sacrifice. Further, when the peculiar feature of the Fec has been enjoined in connection with t ume Paundarika’, it follows that it appertains to that sacrifice which is donoted by that term, it is the whole sacrifice, and not any part of it, that is donoted by the torın ‘Paundarika’, the part is only indirectly unlicat d by the whole Thus the Purvapakṣa view involves the incongruuty of recourse to indirect indication, such indirect interpreta- tion is accepted only when there is no other way possible, in the case in question however, it is not that no other way is possible ;–hence the only right course is that the Priests should be appointed only once, with reference to the whole sacrifice, thus the securing of services’ being done only, once. Lastly, if the Fee is given only once, −(z) the declaration of the entire procedure becomes duly followed,—(b) and the entire performance becomes expedited, and the seripture comes to embrace a vast sphore of activity Hence this 14 the most roasonable course [ SUTRA (67) THERE CAN BE DIFFERENCE ONLY WHEN THERE IS A (DIFFERENT) ACCESSORY. Bhāṣya It has been argued that “Inasmuch as the Paundarika has the Dvādashāhu for its archetype, and at the Dvādashāha there are distinct Fees given on each day, the peculiar feature laid down in connection with the Paundarika should be taken as pertaining to the said distinct Feen given on each day “This has to be refuted. Our answer to this is as follows:- At the Dvādashāha also, the whole sacrifice being one, there is only one ‘hiring of services as for the difference (in the Fees), that is based upon direct Declaration to that effect,-being due to the connection of the Sutyd and also to the idea of ’embellishing’ the Fee. this diversity therefore does not make a diversity in the hiring of services’. 3 + * < ADHIKARAŅA (18): At the Poundarika all the Fees’ should be’ carried’ instalments. qk SUTRA (68). [PURVAPAKṢA (A)]—” EACH DAY THERE SHOULD BE EMBELLISHMENT OF ALL, AS AT THE ARCHETYPE, BECAUSE THE FEE IS AUXILIARY TO ALL Bhasya In The sumo Pr „undarika is the subject-matter for discussion ngam.-It has boen understoo’ that the hiring of services’ is to be done only orce connection with the Archetype, it has been laid down that At the Mid-day Extraction, As Fees are carried up’ In regard to thus, there arises the question—(z) Should the entire Fee be carrie up each day?-(or) should it all he carried up only once -or (0) should it be carried up (each day) in instalments ? 15 he Pūrvapakșa (A) is as follows “Each day there should be embellish- met of all-why as at the Archetype; at the Archetype, the entire Fee embellished at the stated time; hence here also the whole of it should be embellished.-How so -The Days’ are the predominant factor, and the Fees are subordinate to them, hence the entire Fec’ is auxiliary to all the ‘Days’ ;—and the embellishment of the auxiliary therefore becomes necessary on each of the days’, honce it follows that the whole Fee should be ombollshod each day.” SUTRA (69). [PURVAPAKṢA (B)]—“ INASMUCH AS THERE IS ONLY ONE PURPOSE TO BE SERVED, IT CANNOT BE AS STATED 4 + Bhasya “It is not right that each day there should be embellishment of the enture Fee; in fact, there should be embellishment only once,-why ?— because there is only one purpose to be served by the Fees, that purpose being the securing of services -these Foes are to be given after they have been duly “ombellished’ by having passed through all such embellish- ments as carrying up and the like; and when, after being thus embellished, they have been given away on one day, the injunction has been duly fulfilled and thero would be no need for any further embellishment. Hence it follows that the Fees should be embellished (by being ‘carried up’) only once.” 4 ADHYAYA X, PÂDA VI, ADHIKARAṆA (18). SUTRA (70). 1967 [Pūrvapakṣa (B)-refuted]-IT SHOULD BE (EVERY DAY); BECAUSE IN THEIR VERY ORIGIN, THERE IS DIFFERENCE OF TIME. • Bhasya

4 It is not right that the embellishment should be lone only once; in fact, it should be done every day Why 1 -Because in their very orıyın, there 18 difference of time, in their originative junction the Foes are found to be connected with particular pomts of time -For instance, it is declared that Le Fees are carned out during the Mid-day oxtruction, in the regions of the Tristup’. As a matter of fact, all the Fees are auxiliary to all the days’-the Mid-day Extractions of the several days’ are different from one another, and musmuch as no further distinction 19 recognised if the Fees, were not embellished during the Mid-day Extraction of any day, then, so far as that ‘day’ is concerned, the Fees would havo had no embellishment at all, as the actions on the differont days’ are different, and hence those that have been embellished on one day could not be regarded as embellished in connection with another Hence it follows that they have to be embellished separately. L SUTRA (71) [SIDDHANTA-AS A MATTER OF FACT, IT SHOULD BE DONE IN INSTAL- MENTS, BECAUSE THERE IS A DECLARATION TO THAT EFFECT AS AT THE DVADASHAHA Bhāṣya It is not right that all the Fees should be embellishod together on every day; in fact, they should be embellished in instalments.–Why - Because there is a declaration to that offert, at the Deūdashāka, the ‘carrying out’ and other embellishments are done every day, on account of a declaration to the effect that Each day one gives 1200’,-the Paunuluriko has the Dvādashāha for its archetype, -not the Jyotışfoma,—hence even though the hiring of servicos 18 one only, yet the embellishment should be done separately ↓

C ADHIKARANA (19): By the term Manu’s Verses’ only as many of those verses may be used as may be necessary for the purpose in view. SUTRA (72) [PURVAPAKSA] LE WHEN A THING IS SPOKEN OF BY ITS INDICATIVE MARK, THE IDEA SHOULD BE OF ALL THAT HAS THAT MARK, BECAUSE OF THE PRESENCE OF THE INDICATIVE MARK 4 IN ALL, AS IN THE CASE OF AGNEYA’ Bhāṣya L In connection with a cortam Rite, we rend Manorrchah sām dhẽnyo bhavant[‘Manu’s Veras are to be the Sămidhēnis’ | In regard to this, there arises the question Are all those verses con- tangd in the Tenth. Mawlala which are marked by the presence of the term ‘Manu’ to be brought together and used as Sāmelhēnī verses, in the kindling of Fire * Or only a few of them are to be so used, not all " The Purvapaksa is as follows • All the verses marked by the presence Why " Because the indicative mark is Manu’s verses are to be the of the term ’ Manu’ are to be used present in all, all that we find in the text is that Sāmidhēnis’, hence the presence of the term. Manu” is the only indicative features of the verses that have to be brought together, and when the toxt indicates the versos with the presence of the term Manu’, it must be taken an indicating without distinction as many verses as might contam that term, and all that the junctive text lays down is the use of certain verwes solely on the bass of that indicative mark, and it does not mean to mark off only a few selected ones Henco all the verses containing the said indicative mark should be brought together, as in the case of ‘ägnēya’; —in connection with the annual placing of the Rigas with the agnēya”, where we have the declaration ‘āsīta sūktēna sūktasya avuhchhēdāya ’ [‘It should be so done that there may be no disjunction of one hymn from another’], and the hymn meant m the *āgnēya’, and the bricks are laid with all those hymns of the Tenth Mandala that contain the term ‘agni’, similarly, in the case in question also, the purpose of Samidhēnī 14 to be served by means of all those verses that contain the term ‘Manu’ —Or again, just us in the case of the Ahargana, when it is laid down that the ‘Ṛjisa is thrown into water’,-what is thrown into water is the Ṛjīga of everyone of the ‘Days’, without distinction; similarly, in the case in question also, all the verses with the term ‘Manu’ should be taken up " ADHYAYA X, PÄDA VI, ADHIKARANA (19). SÜTRA (73). 1969 [SIDDHANTA IN FACT, AS MANY ALONE SHOULD BE TAKEN AS MAY BE NECESSARY; BECAUSE THEY ARE SUBSERVIENT TO THE MAIN

PURPOSE; AND THE PURPOSE MAY BE SERVED BY A FEWER NUMBER TO THAT EXTENT ALONE LIES THE FORCE OF THE INDICATIVE MARK. Bhāṣya. It is not right that all the verses of the Tenth Midala that contain the term ’ Manu’ should be brought together, in fact, only as many should be brought in as may be necessary —“Why ?’ Because they are subservient to the main purpose, the Sămidhini verses are taken up only with a view to accomplish the purposo in view -and that purpose is served by only a few verses, so that the purpose in view having been accomplished.—even though there might be other versos containing the indicative mark in question, yet they are not to be takon up, simply because there is no need for them Hays the Opponent “Whether or not a corta thing is subservient to a purpose depends upon scriptural toxts, -m the present instance, certain versos indicated by a definito mark have been laid down as to be used as Sāmidhēni, so that it must be taken as an injunction of the use of all those verses that contain that mark " The answer to this is as follows -It is true that in all caso the subservient character of a tlung dopends upon scriptural texts, but as matter of fact, in the case in question it is not the Sōmidhēnis that have been enjoined by the text in question, what it does is to mention the poculiarity that they should be ‘Manu’s verses’ of those Sam dhēnis which under well defined limits, are already admissible at the sacrifice under the General Law This peculiar feature, thus mentioned, qualifies only thos Sām dhēnis that had come in by virtue of tho General Law, and having qualified these, it has its purpose fully served and therefore 10sts thore, so that there is no possibility of any more verses containing the indicative term ‘Manu’ coming in than the number that are admissible under the General Law (whuch number is Fifteen only) Hence out of the verses that contain the indicative mark only a few are to be taken up, not all. Nor can it be right to repeat the prmcipal act (sacrifice) for the sake of the subservient factor, for the ригрово of affording an opportunity for the coming in of the other verses containing the indicative mark By selecting only a few of the verses the performance would become simpler and more expeditiously finished. Further, the indicative mark itself favours this same view.–” How so?” The indicative mark has been mentioned as a qualification for the Sāmidhēnis; so that, even though all the verses containing that mark may not be taken up, yet if only those are admitted that have that mark, not any verses having other marks, even so the indicative mark becomes duly honoured, not ignored. From all thus it follows that only so many verses are to be taken up as are necessary, not all. 1970 SHABABA-BHASYA: SUTRA (74) AS REGARDS THE AONEYA’, THERE IS INJUNCTION OF ALL. Bhasya It has been argued that—“ just as in the case of the text one lays the bricks with Agnèya bymus’, all those hyinns are used that have that indica- tive mark, not only a few,–so should it be in the present case also”. This has got to be refuted The answer to this is as follows-In the caso of the Agnèya’, it is only right that all should be used Why ?”-(a) Because there are m that case, many bricks (b) because with each hymn we have the term ’lays’, so that, when thero are inany bricks to be laid, and the number of hymns is less than that of the bricks, there can be no incongruty in the use of all the hymns In the case in question however, the peculiar feature laid down is with regard to verses whose number is well- defined fifteen only, hence it would be lughly incongruous to use more than fifteen verses, and the number of verses containing the term ‘manı’ IN very much larger than fifteen, so that the reason put forward becomes annulled The analogy cited, therefore, is not correct 4 SÜTRA (75) INA MUCH AS THE RJISA IS THE PRINCIPAL FACTOR, 17 19 ONLY RIGHT THAT THE WHOLE OF IT SHOULD BE DISPOSED OF Bhasya The other argument urged is that Just us at the Ahargana, the entire Bjiga is thrown into the water, so here also all the verses should be used without any distinction This has got to be refuted. The answ OF to this is as follows -Inasmuch as the ‘Rjisa’ is the principal factor, it is only right to take the text as laymg down the disposal of the whole Riga, without any distinction, the disposal, in this case, should be done to the whole Ṛjiga, if it were not done to any part of it, that part of it would be beroft of its embellishment, hence that Bisa which is connected with all the Days’ should be thrown in its entirety. In the case in question how- over, what is laid down is subservient to the purpose in view; hence the reason put forward becomes annulled; and the analogy of the Ria that has been cited is not correct L ADHIKARAṆA (20): The Mana’ (Measuring) and the L C Upāvaharana’ (Gathering up) are to be done on a piece of cloth. SUTRA (76) C THE MEASURING’ AND THE GATHERING Ur’ OF THE SOMA SHOULD BE DONE, AT THI. ARCHETYPE, ON A PIECE OF CLOTH, ON THE STRENGTH OF THE DIRECT DECLARATION Bhasya E L In connection with the Jyotistoma, the measuring and gathering up’ (of Soma) have been laud down In regard to this there arises the question -May this measuring’ bo done on anything, and the ‘gathering up’ done by any thing, without restric- tion ? Or should the meusining be done on a piece of cloth and the “gathering up’ also by the piece of cloth * 1 + The Purrapaksa is that “The measuring’ and the gathering up’ may be done on and by anything that may be suntable for the purpose, this absence of restriction making things simpler and expediting. The performanc P 14 4 C In answer to this we have the following Siddhänta The measuring should be done on a piece of cloth and the gathering up’ also should be done by a piece of cloth “Why” " On the strength of the Ducet Declara. tion, there is the Direct Declaration to the effect that One Hsures on a piece of cloth, and gathers up by a piece of cloth’, and on the strength of thus declaration, both are restricted to the Piece of Cloth) L Or, there can be no occasion for the question to arise at all, when thero is a clear dechuation to the effect that the measuring’ and the gathering up’ are to be done on and by a piece of cloth The explanation of the Sutra is that it sets forth this well ascertamed fact, for the purpose of raising the further discussion (in the next Adhikarana), and where something is stated only as introductory to a further discussion, there is no noed for stating the Pūrrapaksa or the Siddhanta’ C 1 門 il ADHIKARANA (21): At the ‘Ahargana’, it is necessary to secure another piece of cloth. SUTRA (77). AT THE ‘AHARGAṆA’, THERE SHOULD BE SECURING OF (ANOTHER) PIECE OF CLOTH,—ON ACCOUNT OF THERE BEING NEED FOR IT Bhasya There is the Dvidashāha sacrifice, the ‘gathering up’ of Soma has to be done at it, in accordance with the General Law, as laid down in the text ‘Gather it up by a piece of cloth’. In regard to this, there arises the question - For the purpose of this ‘gathoring up, should a separate piece of cloth be secured (for each day ‘) or not? The Purvapakṣa is as follows-“It hould not be so secured, why because there is no declaration to the effect that another piece of cloth should be brought in’, and in the absenco of any such declaration, we do not recognino tho nooessity of bringing up a separate piece of cloth, hence no separato piece of cloth should be brought m”. 1 In answer to this, we have the following Suddhanta -At the ‘Ahargana”, another pieen of cloth should be brought in, because there in need for it, as there are several days’ in the Ahargana’, and ’the gathering up by a piece of cloth is to be done on each of those days, under the General Law ; so that if a separate piece of cloth were not brought in every day, the ‘gathering up’ would not be accomplished Hence a separate piece of cloth should be brought in every day. ADHIKARANA (22): The separate piece of cloth is to be C secured only for the Gathering up’. SUTRA (78) [PŪRVAPAKṢA]—” IT SHOULD BE SECURED WITH A VIEW TO THE ‘MEASURING, BECAUSE AT THE ARCHETYPE, THE GATHER- 擎 ING UP IS FOUND TO BE DONE BY THAT SAME PIECE OF CLOTH Bhasya. L "” In connection with the same Ahargana’, we are considering a further question. It has hoon explained that a separate piece of cloth is to be secured there is need for it -The question that arises now is Is the piece of cloth to be secured with a view to the Measuring ’ * Or with a view to the Gathering up’ · The Purrapaksa view is as follows · & It should be secured with a view to the measuring’, -why–because at the Archetype the *Gathering up 18 found to be done with that same piece of cloth, at the Jyotiatoma we find that the gathering up’ is done by that same piece of cloth in which tho moasuring has been done, and at the Eetype things have to be done as at the Archetype, according to the General Law,–hence the piece of cloth should be brought in at the time of the ‘measuring " J SUTRA (79) [SIDDHANTA-IT SHOULD, IN REALITY, BE SECURED WITH A VIEW TO THE GATHERING UP’, AS THERE IS NO DIRECT DECLARATION, 4 & AT THE ECTYPE, IT HAS TO BE DONE BY A SEPARATE PIECE AS THERE IS ACTUAL NEED FOR IT 1 Bhāṣya. 44 4 It is not right that it should be secured with a view to the measuring in fact, it should be secured for the gathering up’ Why ?"-Because there is no Direct Declaration; we do not find it declared anywhere that the piece of cloth should he brought in for the ‘measuring’; and in the absence of any such declaration, we cannot be certain that it must be done for the measuring alone. When a certain thung is used for a definite purpose, it is only right that, being needed for that purpose, it should be brought in at the time that it is needed, not at any other time; in the case in question, the need for a fresh piece of cloth arises at the time of the ‘gathering up’; and hence the right course is that it should be secured for, and at the time of, the ‘gathering up ‘.1974 SHABARA-BHÄṆYA : It has been argued that-” At the Archetype that same piece of cloth is used for the gathering up which has been used for the measuring-and hence, according to the General Law, the fresh piece of cloth should be brought in at the time of the measuring “This has to be refuted; and our answer to this is as follows.-There is no such declaration as that ’the gathering up should be done by that same piece of cloth on which the measuring has been done’, it is done so at the Archetype only because there is need for it and it can be so done, because the ‘Day’ is only one; so that the piece of cloth not being otherwise engaged, it is used for the ‘gathering up’ also-what is done only by reason of the needs of the situation cannot be applied elsewhere under the General Law,-as it is something not amenable to verbal authority. Further, in the case in question, there being several days’, the same piece of cloth could not possibly be used for both the purposes From all this it follows that the fresh piece of cloth should be brought in at the time of ‘gathering up’. PADA VII ADHIKARANA (1): At the Jyotistoma, each limb of the animal forms a distinct cffering SUTRA (1) [TURVAPAKSA “THE ANIMAT SHOULD BE REGARDED AS A SINGLE 6 OFFERING, BECAUSE THE WHOLE OF IT HAS BEEN ENJOINED.” Bhüsya In connection with the Jyotistoma, the Animal Iquiṣomīya (dedicated to Aqui Soma) has been enjoined Who. being tinted, sacrifices the animal dedicated to Agni Soma ’ I J 1 1 4 In regard to thus, there arises the question- Does the whole animal form one offering’ 9 Or 18 each limb of it a distinct offering’? C It is not right that the whole animal forms a single offering’; as B matter of fact, each limb is a distinct offering.-Why Because each has been assigned separately, each limb has been separately assigned by means 1978 KHABARA-BRIŞYA : of moh texts as— First of all, he slices out of the heart, then the tongue, the chest, the arms, the sides, the arms’; where the slicing laid down is out of various substances in the shape of the Heart and the rest. This cannot be possible unless the arumal is cut up; hence it follows that for the purpose of getting at the Heart and other limbs, the animal has to be cut up, and when the animal has been cut up, the shape of the animal can no longer be there. Thus then, it comes to this-When the sacrifice is being performed, one should help it by means of the substance in the shape of the animal,-but it is not possible to accomplish the sacrifice by bodily introducing the animal into it, hence it is only indirectly that the animal’s body can help the sacrifice,–consequently the ‘offerings are to consist of the Heart and other limbs forming parts of the substance in the shape of that animal,-and the offerings are to be made out of those limbs’; as in the case of the ‘Cup’; for instance, in connection with the Soma-sacrifice, it is laid down ‘Takes up the (up dedicated to Indra Vaya,-takes up the (‘up dedicated to Mira-Varuna, -takes up the Cup dedicated to the Ashvins’,-where each Cup forms a distinct offering’, the offering’ consisting of the Soma. juce in each Cup, not of the entire Soma-creeper; similarly in the case in question also (the offering consists of the parts of the animal, not the entire animal). 4 As for the injunction of the whole animal’, this can be explained also on the busus of the limbs constituting the ‘offoring, even so the whole animal forming the offering’ indirectly through the limbs L As for the indicative text that has been cited, that can be explained all the more easily on the basis of there being several offerings’ consisting of the hubs -How 1–When it speaks of one slice helping the other, it shows that the whole of the animal is not meant to be sliced out as a single offering”. ADHIKARANA (2): The Sacrifice is to be performed with the Heart and other specified particular limbs of the Animal. SUTRA (3) [PORVAPAKSA INASMUCH AS EACH LIM IS A DISTINCT OFFERING, THERE SHOULD BE REPETITION OF THF ACT PENCE THERE + SHOULD BE OFFERING OUT OF ALL THE LIMBS Bhasya " offermg We have understood that each limb forms a distmet The question that arise, now is-1s the sacrifice to be accomplished by tho offering of any one of the limbs ? Or should offormgs be made out of all tho limbs " On could there be specification–the offering being made out of a now specified Innbs only ? The Purvapaksa is as follows 4 The offering should be nude out of all the rubs, hence the act of offormg should be reponted -Why ?- - Because each Limb is a distinct offering, each of the limbs described in the text speaking of the slings Heart, Tongue and the rost, - form so muy distinct offerings, so also do the other limbs (not so mentioned) which become included indirectly, ns forming parts of the animal’s body, hence offerings should he made out of all these hubs Some of them are specially characterised by the shape of the animal, under the circumstances, if the offering were made out of any one limb only, all that is characterised by the shape of the animal would not become included, so that the shape of the animal’ would not have been made an accessory of the sacrifice Ti shape of the aumal becomes such an accessory only when it charterises und qualifies a flesh-lump endowed with several qualifications,–not other- WISC If however all the lumbs formung part of the animal’s body were made a single offering, then the onjoined offering of the whole would be accomplished without the repetition of the act of offering But when ench lunb is regarded as a distinct offering,-if one were to make the offering out of a single limb, one would naturally abandon some of the limbs, while if he were to repeat the act of offering, he would be able to take in all the limbs From all this it follows that offerings should be made out of all tho limbs Say the Opponent (to the Pūrvapaksa) When all the particular parts of the body are meant to accomplish the sacrifice, then the sacrifico could be accomplished by means of any one of them’ «The answer to this is as follows -Tho sacrifice may be accomplished, but the particular limbs have been spoken of as connected with the sacrifice, what is spoken of, however, as connected with the sacrifice is the shape of the animal; and this shape of the animal becomes an accessory of the sacrifice when the particular limbs are used, and it is for thus reason that the declaration of the procedure speaks of the parts of the body; but it is 36 1978 SHABARA-BHĀṆYA: not ascertained what particular part is taken up and what not; consequently all come to be taken up for the purpose, by following what has been said in the declaration of procedure. If any particular part has not been taken up, it is assumed that even without that, the sacrifice is performed in accordance with the injunction, so that, having become qualified by the shape of the animal, nothing fhore is brought in; but in that case it would mean a disregard for this latter-Hence we conclude that offerings should be made out of all the limbs, the Heart and other specified ones, as also others not so specified SUTRA (4). [Objection to Purvapakṣa]—As A MATTER OF FACT, THERE SHOULD BE SPECIFICATION, BECAUSE OF THE SPECIFIC MENTION,—AS IN THE C CASE OF THE AJYABHAGA’ Bhāṣya. The offerings should be made out of the Heart and other specified limbs, not out of the rost —Why 1-Because of their specific mention; the Heart and other limbs have been specifically mentioned, in the passage beginning with ‘These are the eleven offerings out of the animal’.-As regards the text in question, it cannot be taken as an injunction of these same offerings, as these are already known to be admissible under the General Law,—nor can it be takon as a more reiteration, as such a reiteration would be useless; -the reiteration too is without any details,all which shows that the text 18 meant to proclude those not mentioned (and to specify those mentioned). For instance, when it is said one should not go’, or ‘one should not eat’, it is a clear prohibition; in the same way in a case of Preclusion and Specification also there is prohibition. As in the case of the Agyabhāga ‘; as in connection with the Grhamēdhiya, it has been explained in Adhyāya V, that the mention of ‘Ajyabhāya’ as one alternative serves the purpose of preclusion, the same should be the case in the present instance also - Hence the text is to be taken as a preclusion and specification. SUTRA (14) [Siddhāntin’s answer to Pūrvapaksa-argument]—BUT IT CANNOT BE SO, AS THERE IS NO INJUNCTIVE TEXT TO THAT EFFECT, Bhasya The term ’tu’ (‘but ‘) implies the rejection of the view set forth above. As a matter of fact, the text cannot be taken as restricting the share (to the Hotr); it must be taken as laying down the modification of the Ida- portion “Why”-There is no injunctive text to the effect that there 1986 SHABARA-BHĀṆTA: should be the Adhyüdhni-portion even where there is the Ida-portion at the same time. “But we have pointed out the text-They enlarge the cake with boneless pieces of flesh ‘” The answer to this is that this text is a mere reiteration, the boneless-pieces having been already enjoined elsewhere- Yadu parishiṣyatë tat samavatta- dhanyāmānayatı, yat hrdayım präsynti, pihvām vakṣaḥ, tanimam alastasyā vanıghum ’ — Hence it follows that the text cited by the opponent is only a reiteration. Then again, the adhyūdhni is not mentioned in the text at all, hence it cannot be regarded as enjoined elsewhere as to be used,–and when it is not so enjoined elsewhere, it must be taken as enjoined in the text in question (’ adhyūdhnim hotrē harantı ‘) in reference to the ‘presenta- tion to the Hotp’ It has been argued that in this case it would be necessary to assume a syntactical connection (between ‘adhyūdhnim’ and harants’) which is interrupted (by the intervention of the word ‘hotrē ‘)” —Wo shall certainly assume such a connection when we find—(a) that the adhyūdhni’ is not something already enjoined elsewhere, (b) that the text, therefore, cannot be a reiteration, and (c) that it would be meaningless if the said assumption were not mado In this way, the mjunction would be of the ‘presenting’ which is expressed by a word contained in the text itself, otherwise, in the other caso, what would be enjomed would be the connection between the Adhyūdhni and the Hotr, not the presenting which is expressed by a word of the text itself For this reason also the Adhyūdhni should be regarded as a modification of a former eating-portion SUTRA (15) [Pūrvapaksin’s objection]” IN FACT, IT WOULD BE A MERE GIFT, AS THERE IS NO CONNECTION WITH THE TERM Bhāṣya EATING-PORTION P The term api rā’ (‘in fact ‘) implies the rejection of the view just set forth “If it be as explained above, and the Adhyūdhni has not been enjoined in any other text as to be presented even when the Ida-portion is there,– then, it comes to this that what the text in question enjoins is something entirely new to be presented’, in the shape of the Adhyūdhni, and in that caso it cannot be treated as the modification of an eating portion; as all that the words ‘adhyúdhnim karants’ expresses is the mere giving away of the thing to the Hotr, nor is there any connection laid down with the term ‘bhaka’ (’eating-portion”) Hence the Adhyūdhni cannot be regarded as the modification of an eating-portion.” ADHYAYA X, PĪDA VII, ADHIKARAŅA (4). SUTRA (16). 1987 [Answer to the Pūrvapakṣin’s argument]-As A MATTER OF FACT, IT MUST BE THE MODIFICATION OF AN EATING-PORTION, AS THERE IS NO C ‘GIVER’,-ALL (THE SACRIFICER AND THE PRIESTS) BEING EQUAL IN RELATION TO THE REMNANTS Bhāṣya. L & The term lu’ (‘as a matter of fact’) implies the rejection of the View just set forth-that “it is a mero gift, not the n dification of an eating- portion”. It cannot be a came of giving away’, because there is no giver’; the annal, in fact, has been dedicated by the Master of the sacrifice In the sense that saving the sacrifice, I shall not use this animal for any other purpose of mine own’, so that there being no longer any ownership over the animal, there can be no going away (of any part of it) Why Is there no ownership !"-Bocauso all are equal in relation to the Remnant ; ns regards the Remnants of the sacrifice, the Sacrificer stands on the same footing as the Hotr, neither of them is the owner of the substance Hence there can be no giving When there is no connection with the term ‘cating-portion’, how can the Adhyūdhni be regarded as an eating-portion?” It follows the presence of the Dative ending (in ‘hotre’), this Dative ending has the sense of for the sake of’, so that what the words of the Text mean is that the adhyūdhni is for the sake of the Holy’, ‘it is the Hoir who is wanted by it as its recipient’, which means that it benefits the Hotr’; it can do so only when it is eaten and thereby imparts strength to the person, thus conferring upon hum a perceptible benefit; and to the extent that it confers this benefit, to that extent does the Dative ending become justified, otherwiso, if the benefit conferred were an improeptible one (as it would be, if it were a case of mere gift), the agnification of the Dative would become ignored. From all this it follows that the Adhyudhni is a modification of the eating-portion of Idā. ADHIKARAŅA (5): The Vanistu’ is the modification of an Eating-portion. The term và’ (‘in reality ‘) implies the rejection of the view set forth abovo Li The Maitrāvaruna should not have two shares, he should have only one Why “Because the share has not been declared; it has not been declared that the Adhvaryu’s sharo is to go to the Mautrāvaruna, or that the Hor’s share is to go to hum If those two had been so declared, then, even though the requisito embellishinent would have been secured by a single share, yet, on the strongth of the said declaration, he would receive the second share also As a matter of fact, however, the share comes to the Matträvaruna only by virtue of the General Law,-hence, as the Maură- varuna is only one, a single share will suffice to accomplish that archetypal condition, and no second share could be indicated by the General Law hence the Priest in question should have one share only. SUTRA (22) [PURVAPAKYA]“THE PRATIPRASTHĀTR ALSO SHOULD HAVE A SHARE, ON ACCOUNT OF HIS COOKING THE OMENT M Bhasya In connection with the same anmal sacrifice to Agni-Soma the •Pratiprasthātr’ priest is spoken of In regard to him, there arises the question-Is this Priest to have a share in the eating of Reinnants ? The l’urvapakṣa is as follows · He is to have his aluare, why ?- because when he cooks the omentum,-mn accordance with the text “The Pratiprasthätr priest cooks the omentum’, -he performs the functions of the Adhvaryu, hence he should have hus share in the eating-portion’ SUTRA (23) [SIDDHANTA IN REALITY, HE CAN HAVE NO SHARE, BECAUSE THE ACTION IS DIFFERENT, AND BECAUSE THE WHOLE OF IT IS OFFERED AWAY Bhāsya — L The Pratiprasthātr can have no share in the eating-portion- Why? -Because at the sacrifice wherein he arts for the Adhvaryu, there is no remnant of the substance offered, what he does is the cooking of the omen- tum, and the whole of it is offered away, so that, there, being no remnant, what is there to be eaten At those sacrifices where there is a remnant,- that is. those in which offerings are made out of the Heart and other specified lumbs,-this Priest does not act for the Adhvaryu¦—as a matter of fact, the transcendental rosult connected with the omentum is entirely different (from that connected with the Heart, otc ), because it is connected with a subsidiary act; and what the General Law indicates is that that priest alone becomes entitled to the eating-portion who has worked at the sacrifice the substance used at which is to be disposed of by that eating; in thus way the eating would come to help in the sacrifice, if, on the other hand, the eating were done by a priest who has done work other than any connected with the sacrifice, as he would have rendered no service, his mating would not help the sacrifice in any way, and hence it would be no part of it. Thus then, the Ayabhiqa-offerings being equal to (standing on the same footing as) the other accessories, the text cannot be taken as taking in the Aryabhaga-offerings which have not been taken in by the General Low.” SÜTRA (32) [PorvapakṢa (G), and its refutation]-THERE WOULD BE THE SAME OBJECTION AGAINST THE AJYABHĀGAS ALONE BEING TAKEN IN (UNDER THE GENERAL LAW) Bhasya • The following view may bo put forward (as Pūrvapaksa (G)]—“ What the General Law indicates is the Аjyabhāga-offerings only, as constituting the Grhamēdhīya sacrifice, when performed in the manner of the Archetype; the question having arisen as to how the Ãƒyabhāqa-offerings are to be made, -the answer is that it is in such and such a manner (as at the Archetype)’ Just as in the case of the text There are seventeen Sūmidhēnis at the Adhvarakalpas’, the number ‘seventeen’ does not find place in any other sacrifice, —or, in the case of the sentence Bring the Shimshapā tree’, no other tree is brought up, and the Shimshapā alone is understood to be spoken of by means of the term ’troe’,imilarly in the case in question, the Āṇyabhāga-offerings alone should be understood to be taken in by the General Law”. Our answer to this is as follows -There would be the same objection against the Aryabhāgas alone being taken in under the General Law,-the idea that the Āzyabhāgas alone are taken in is equal to (open to the same objections as) the idea that they are not taken in, as for the other accessories, their non-inclusion (under the General Law) might be possible if the General Law dealt with the accessories separately, but no such non-inclusion is possible when all that the General Law indicates is the fulfilment of the archetypal transcendental result (as explained above) SUTRA (33). SUTRA (38) IN THE MATTER OF ENDING WITH THE SHAMYU AND THE IDĀ’, THERE SHOULD BE OPTION, AS OTHERWISE, THE PROHIBITION OF THF PATNYANUYĀJA’ WOULD PE MEANINGLESS”. Bhāsya In connection with the Jyotstoma, we read—(a) ‘Shamyvantā prāyaniyä santisthatë, na patnih samyāzayanti’ [’ l’ho Prāyaniyā becomes complete when ending with the Shamyu, –they do not make the wives offer the sacrifice”, (b) ‘Idäntä älthyā santisthatē, nānuyājau yazantı ’ [“Pho ÃÄtithyā becomes complete when ending with the Idā,—they do not porform the Anuyājas ‘] In regard to this, there arises the question,—(6) Is it meant that the Prāyaniyā may be regarded as complete, either with all the Terraumnes duly performed, or with the Shamyu only Or that it must always end with tho Shamyn —(b) Similarly, may the Anthy be regarded as complete either with all the Terminuses duly performed, or with the Ida only Or raust it always end with the Ida The Pürenpakan is as follows “In the matter of ending with the Shamya and the Ida there should be option,-why-been there is prohibition of Patnyanuyāja There is the clear declaration to the effect that the Prāvanīvā becomes complete when ending with the Shamyu’, then there is the other declaration to the effect that they do not make the wives offer the sacrifice’ If the Prayaniyā must always end with the Shamyn, then the prohibition of the Panyanuyāja would be meaningless Hence this prohibition of the Patnyanuyāja should be taken as laying down the completing of all the Terminuses –How so -At the Prāyaniyā, they do not perform the Patnisamyāja alone, and nothing else, similarly at the At thyŭ, they do not perform the Anuyājas alone, and nothing else Hence the two (prohibitive) texts should be taken as distinct sentences precluding those details that should not be performed [Hence, the performance where these details are omitted forms one option; and that in which they are not omitted forms another option]“2004 SHABARA-BHĀṢYA: SUTRA (39). [SIDDHANTA IN REALITY, IT 19 ONLY A DESCRIPTION OF THE EXISTING STATE OF THINGS; AS THE ACT IS NOT WHAT IS ENJOINED BY THE TEXT. Bhāsya. It is not right that there should be option; in fact, there is only one alternativo, that it should end with the Shamyu; as there is a specific declara- tion to that effect, there can be no second alternative, there is no declaration of any such other alternative The prohibition of the Patnyanuyāja cannot be taken as laying down the completion of all the Terminuses; it is, in fact, only the description of an existing state of things; it describes things as they exist; just like the statement that ‘Fire is not to be installed in the sky or in hoaven Thus the two sentences The Prāyaniyć becomes complete with the Shamyu’ and ‘They do not make the wives offer the sacrifices’—are to be construed and Syntactically Connected with one another —Similarly also with the two sentences-The Atthya becomes complete with the Idā’, and ‘They do not offer the Anuydjas’.—The purpose served by the description is that the course of action laid down becomes eulogised with very littlo effort. “There is the prohibitive text, which may be taken as laying down the completion of all the terminuses.” This would involve an assumption for which there is no justification in the Voda, and such an assumption would be as wrong as the abandoning and ignoring of what has been actually laid down in the Veda. From all this it follows that the Prāyaniya must end with the Shamyu and the Atthya must end with the Idā. There is the Vājupēya sacrifice, laid down in the text-‘Sharadr vāza- pēyēna svārājyakāmo yajēta” [“Desiring self-sovereignty, one should perform the Vājapēya sacrifice during the autumnn’],-in connection with thus Bacrifice, we road- The Post shall be of Khadira wood”. (A) In regard to this, there arises the question-Can the Post at the Vājapēya be made of any of the three kinds of wood, Khadira, Palāsha, and Rohitaka (which are the three laid down as optional alternatives in connection with the Jyotistoma, which is the archetype of the Vajapeya) -Or must it be of Khadira-wood only? (B) Sumilarly, in another connection, we read-Brhat is the Saman used’,—and in regard to this, there arises the question-May the Saman used be either Brhat or Rathantara " Or must it be Brhat only 9 (0) Similarly, in connection with the Traidhātavyā, we read-The middle one is made of barley’, and in regard to tlus, there arises the question Can the middle one be made either of Barley or Vriha ? Or must it be of barley alone?

To all these questions, the natural answer is as follows When, from among several mutually incompatible things, any one is specially mentioned, there should be restriction, that is, (a) The Post should be of Khadıra-wood only, (b) the Saman should be the Brhat only, and (c) the muddle one should be of Barley only “Why?"-As thus alone does the special mention serve a useful purpose, that it is only when there is such restriction that the special mention of the Khadira, the Brhat and the Barley has some sense, otherwise, it would be a mere reiteration of what is already known, and as such, super- Aluous. Inasmuch as the Khadira, the Brhat and the Barley have been specified by the Vedic lerts, they must exclude the other possible alternatives, (a) Palasha and Rohitaka, (b) Rathantara, and (c) Vrihi;-just as in the case of ‘Reeds’; that is, when we have the specific mention of Reeds in the text ‘The grass consists of Reeds’, Kusha becomes excluded, so should it be in the case in question also.
