As a matter of fact, it cannot be as suggested above; because it is not the ‘scratching’ that is enjoined in thus caso, the ‘scratchung’ is done only on account of the need arising for it “What if it 1940 ?"-If the scratchung’ wore enjoined, it would have to be regarded as serving an unseen (transcendental) purpose, as the injunction is useful only when what is enjoined is not already known [and it is only the transcendental result that would not be known in this case];-and as with each act (of scratching ‘) the said result would vary, it would have to be assumed that there are several acts, and in that case a distinguishing feature would be perceived [which would justify the repetition of the Mantra with each act]- When, however, as a matter of fact, the scratching’ is only indicated by the actual need for it that arises there (in the shape of the itching in the body), then in that case the act that one wishes to do would be that (series of acts) by which the tching would be allayed, and there would be nothing to distinguish one part of this entire process from the other [and hence there would be nothing to justify the repetition of the Mantra].” When one itching limb has been scratched, it has become embellished by that scratching,—and after that another itching limb would be scratched [andADHIKA SHABARA-BHÄṆYA: uld be a distinct sot of scratching].”—Answer-The activity in this > not for scratching the body, but for allaying the stching; and this itching ch is a sensation) is in the conscious soul, not in the body; hence there is thing to distinguish one (itching or scratching) from the other. Con- [Bequently the conclusion is that the Mantra should be recited only once. ADHIKARANA (18): At the Jyotistoma, in connection with ‘sleep’ and the like, the Mantra is not to be repeated. SUTRA (50) IN CONNECTION WITH (a) SLEEP, (b) RIVER-OROSSING, (c) RAIN-WETTING, AND (d) J JOKING AT AN UNG MAN THING, THE SAME L CONCLUSION HOLDS GOOD. Bhāṣya With reference to the Tyatıştoma-(a) the Mantra, ‘Tvamagnē vratapā as, etc’ has been laid down in connection with ‘sleeping’,-(b) the Mantra, Devirapah, etc’ in connection with rivor-crossing’,-(c) the Mantra, Udantarirajo dhatte, etc’ in connection with rain-wetting’,-(d) the Mantra, Adabdham chakṣuh, etc’ in connection with looking at an unclean thing’. • 4 " The question that arises is-when one-(a) sleeps again after having risen from sleep, or (b) crosses several streams of a river, one after the other, or (c) 18 wetted by rain over and over again,—or (d) looks at several unclean things at one and the same time, should there be a repetition of the Mantra concerned ? Or should it be recited only once The Purvapaksa view is that “inasmuch as each of the repeated acts is a distinct act, there should be repetition of the Mantra " The Siddhanta is as follows:-In the case of sleeping and the rest also, it should be the same as in the case of scratching,e the Mantra should be recited only once. When the man recites the Mantra in connection with sleep, it refers to sleeping throughout the night, not to only one instalment of sleep. Similarly, it is with reference to the crossing of all the streams, to all rain-wettings and to all unclean things. And as in each case the reference 18 made to the entire series at one and the same time, there is nothing to Indicate with which particular action the Mantra is connected.-Hence there should be no repetition of the Mantra. ADHIKARAŅA (19): At the retirement of the Initiated sacrificer the Mantra is not to be repeated. SUTRA (51). IN THE CASE OF RETIREMENT, TILL THE PURPOSE HAS BEEN ACCOMPLISHED. Bhasya When the Initiated Person is retiring to rest, in connection with his starting, there is the Mantra, Bhadradabhishreyah prehi, etc.’. " In regard to this, we proceed to consider the question Should the Sacrificer repeat the Mantra each time that he retires to rest? or only once, at the beginning? The Purvapakea is that “inasmuch as each retirement is perceived to be a distinct act, the Mantra should be repeated with each Retirement.” In answer to this, we have the following Siddhānta :—In the case of Retire- ment, till the purpose has been accomplished, it is for some purpose that the man retires,—and till that purpose has been fulfilled, it is all a single act of Retirement’, hence the Mantra should be recited only once.

ADHIKARAŅA (20): There should be repetition of the ‘Uparava-mantra ‘. SUTRA (52). [PURVAPAKSA]— 4 “THE UPARAVA-MAN RA’ SHOULD BE HELD TO BE C COMMON, BECAUSE OF THE PLA JMBER, AS IN " COMMON PARLANCE.” Bhasya + In connection wit i the Jyotıştoma, here is the following Uparava - Mantra-’ Riksohano algahano vuṣnavān khanāmı’ [Inıd down for the digging of tl • four pit called u Darawa’ | In regard to this thore arises the question–Should this Mantra be recited only once in common for all the Pits or should it bo ropouted with each Pit separately? The Purvapakṣa is as follows -“ The Uparava-mantra should be held to be in common’,- it should be recited only once,-why ?–because of the plural number, we find the word ‘vaisnavān’ in the plural number; if the Mantra were meant to be repeated with each Pit, then the word with the plural ending would not be applicable to the single Pit, as in common parlance, the plural number is not used with reference to any single thing.- Further, as a matter of fact, the Mantra, on being recited once, is capable of applying to all the Pits; and when it can do this, its repetition would be useless-Hence it should be recited only once.” SUTRA (53). [SIDDHANTA-NOT SO, BECAUSE IT HELPS DIRECTLY. IT IS ONLY AMONG SUCH ACTS AS ARE NOT DIRECTLY HELPFUL THAT THERE BEING NO DISTINCTION PERCEPTIBLE, THE RECITAL IS DONE ONCE ONLY, AS THE TIME IS ONE Bhasya. Not so; ie the Mantra should not be held to be ‘in common ‘.—Why ? -Because it helps directly, the act of digging (of the Pit) is directly helpful; and it is recognized as to be related to that particular Pit which it has helped. -The Mantra also is directly helpful; because the end of the Mantra coincides with the beginning of the act (of Digging);—hence when the Mantra has been used in helping the digging of one Pit, the embellishment brought about by that Mantra belongs to that Pit alone, not to all the Pits. Hence in the 53 2250 SHABARA-BHĀŞYA: case in question, the Mantra is to be recited, not once only [but once with each of the four Pits]. L It is only among such acts as are not directly helpful that, there being no distinction perceptible, the recital is done once only -e those Mantras that are related to acts that are not directly helpful, -og the Mantra Devá brahmânah, etc’ used in connection with the Inviting of the Subrahmanyā,- as the Upavasathya day is the one time for them, and no other distinction Is perceptible, they are recited once only

As for the argument that " the word with the plural ending cannot signify any single thing”, what is really moant to be signified by the word is what is denoted by the basic noun, as for the ending, that denotes the objective character (of the Pit); and thero is nothing that is denoted separately by the plural number itself, in fact, it does not deserve to be denoted soparately, as there is no term that can denote it.–Or the plural number may apply to a single thing, the plural number being explained as signifying Thus there is no mcongruity in the Siddhanta view reverence SUTRA (54) IN THE CASE OF THE HAVISKRT,’ THE ‘ADHRIGU,’ THE ‘PURONUVĀKYA,’ AND THE MANOTĀ,’—THERE SHOULD BE REPETITION, BECAUSE C OF THE DIFFERENCE IN TIME Bhāsya L , Thus Sutra sets forth the counter-instances to what has been said in the last three Sūtras,-boing an answer to the question-Why has the Sūtra (53) added the phrase · Kāla katat, as the time is one -The answer IS provided in this Sūtra which cites certam cases where the time not being one there is repotition Of this Sutra (54) may be taken as setting forth a distimet Adhikarana as the following • 4 $ ADHIKARANA (21): There should be repetition of the Mantras connected with the Haviskṛt, etc. L SUTRA (54) Bhasya (a) In connection with the Jyotiatoma, there are Savaniya-cakes offered at each Extraction’, at these there is Invitation of the Havişkrt (the sacrificer’s wife, who prepares the offering) [for which the Mantra is Havskrdehi, etc ‘1,-(b) in connection with the Vagapeya, there are the Sacrificial annals’, and also the ‘animals dedicated to Prajapati, in ADHYAYA XI, PĀDA IV, ADHIKARANA (21). 2251 reference to which there is the direction addressed to the Adhrigu-priest [this direction being in the form of the Mantra—’ Dawyäh shamitāraḥ, etc.’]; (c) there is the Puronuvākyā-Mantra [* Agnē naya supathā, etc’] related to the ’two black-necked goats,—and (d) there is the Manota-hymn [* Tvam hyagnē prathamo manotā, elc’| In regard to these, we proceed to consider the following question –In those cases, the Mantra to bo rocited only once? Or is it to be repeated ? The Pūrvapakṣa is that—“ in order ’ preserve the joint character of the actions, the Mantra should b. cited only once In answer to this, there is the following Studhinta: -There should be repetition.—why ?—because of the difference in time,-when the Inviting of the Harskrt’, or the ‘Directing of the Agu. is done at the Morning- Extraction a d’‘inctive feature is perceived whereby it is recognized that the Haviskrt referred to s cne who makes Cakes for the Morning Extrac- tion and the Ihrigu is one connected with the sacrificial animals —Similarly, inasmuch as he two black-necked goats’ are separated by the ‘Saumya animal’, it is understood that the Puronuvākyā and the Manota appertain to the former of the two goats — In all those cases the time is different, and by reason of this difference in time a distinction is perceivod, hence there should be repetition SUTRA (55) ALSO BECAUSE THERE IS REVERSAL OF THE ADHRIGU. Bhasya In regard to the Adhruqu, there is this further peculiarity, that there would be reversal’ That is, if the mantra were used in common’, –then, if those details relating to the Adhrigu which come before the details of the animals dedicated to Prajapati ‘,-e g. the mantra · Ashrutapratyā- shrute ajaidagnih, etc ‘,—wore performed at the Morning Extraction,then the section ending with the Paryagnikarana would not be abandoned,—if, in order to avoid thus incongruit v, the said details were performed at the Brahmasāman, then there would be reversal’, by porforming, after the Adhrigu, of what should have been done before. For this reason also there should be repetition Further- SUTRA (36) BECAUSE OF THE DECLARATION OF WHAT IS GOING TO BE DONE Bhasya L There is the following declaration of the Adhrigu Arabhadhvam- upanayata’, which speaks of what is going to be done at the time; if this were said at the Morning Eatraction, then us that would not be the proper time for the act spoken of, the sentence would be unable to express that idea; 2252 SHABARA-BHAṢYA: if the declaration is meant to be a direction,then too, the Direction is for the purpose of bringing about activity; yet, in connection with the animals dedicated to Prajapati, the sentence is not used for prompting activity,- because there is an intervention of a large lot of actions; so that the notion of ‘Directing’ is lost sight of; and thereby also the sentence becomes inex- pressivo. For this reason also the Siddhanta is that there should be repetition of the Adhrigu-mantra End of Pada wv of Adhyāya XI. End of Adhyaya XI.

ADHYAYA XII. " PADA I 4 ADHIKAKANA (1): The Prayāja and other rites connected with the Agniṣomiya animal help the Cake. Bhāṣya L Tantr 1 1 (Common, Centralization d’Avāna’ (Uncommon, Decen- tralization) have bn dealt with under Discourse XI. Now under Discourse XII is going to be explam 1 ‘Prasanga’ Extended Application The exact signification of the term ‘Prosan, has been already explained above (under Sutr 11 1. the words [That which is com mon is Tantra; it is not prompted by tu neds of other things], so also is Prasanga wluch has its own mjunction present’ -In short, when sometlung done in one place is helpful in another place also, it is a case of ‘Prasanga ’ (Extended Application), for instance, when the Lamp lighted in the house illumines the public road also —It is thus Prasanga that we are going to consider now In connection with the Agnisomiya-animal-sacrifice, there is an offering of Pashu-purodāsha (Meat-cake), laid down in the toxt- Having offered the omentum of the animal sacrificed to Agni-Soma, one should offer the Meat-cake baked on eleven pans, dedicated to Agni-Soma ‘.—The question in regard to this is- s-Should the subsidiaries (Prayāja, etc) be performed in connection with thus Meat-cake-offering separately or is it to be taken as helped by those same subsidiaries as they have been performed in con- nection with the main Animal-sacrifice The Purvapakea is stated in the Sutra itself SUTRA (1) [PURVAPAKSA continued] WHEN THERE IS A CONGREGATION OF SUCH MAIN SACRIFICES AS HAVE COMMON ACCESSORY DETAILS,—THER IS A COMMON PROCEDURE AMONG THOSE THAT ARE SIMILARLY ENJOINED, AMONG THOSE NOT SO SIMILAR, THERE SHOULD BE DIVERSITY, BECAUSE IT IS FOR THE PURPOSE MANCE, OF UNDERTAKING THE PERFOR- AND THAT IT IS FOR THAT PURPOSE IS DUE TO THE DIRECT DECLARATION OF TIME” Bhāṣya. “The term ’tantra’ stands for that set of accessory details which is common-such as the Ajyabhāga’ and the rest for the first half, and 4 2254 1 " SHABARA-BHÄŞYA : 5 ‘Svistakrt’ and the rest for the second half,-those Main sacrifices that have such a common set of accessory details are called tantrin’;-when there is a congregation of such Main Sacrifices, 1e when they are such as are to be perforined at the same time and place and by the same performers, then, among those that are similarly enjoined, -10 among those that are enjoined by the same sentence,–there is a common procedure, as we find in the case of the Darsha-Purnamasa and the Chitra-Iştı -Among those not so similar there should be diversity, ve among those that are not similarly enjoined, c. are enjoined by distinct sentences,–there should be diversity of procedure; as we find in the case in question itself,—of such injunctions 48, ‘One should sacrifice the animal dedicated to 1gm-Soma’, One offers the Meat-cake baked upon eleven pans, dedicated to Agni-Soma -‘Why should it be so -Because it is for the purpose of undertaking the performance, vidhi’ is procedure, the performance of the subsidiues, the ‘prakrama’ of it is proceeding with it, it is for the sake of undertaking the said performance, e it is recognized that the undertaking of the perform- ance is for that purpose, ie it is understood that the undertaking of tho perforinance is for the purpose of the Animal-offering, not for that of the Cake But how is it recognized that the undertaking of the performance 14 for the purpose of the Animal-offering “’—That it is for that purpose 18 due to the direct declaration of time, it is by Duect Declaration that the time 19 indicated, the time for the Animal-offering being indicated as after the bringing up of the animal dedicated to Agni-Soma, it is in reference to that time that it has been enged, the time for the Cake-offering being after the offering of the omentum So that the undertaking of the performance that is done on the occasion of the Animal-sacrifice is recognised to be for the purpose of the Animal-offering only As for the Cake, it is not even known as yot (ns to be offered), hence its procedure should be entirely distinct Thero is an indicative text also which points to the fact that the procedure in question is for the purpose of the Animal-offering- Yadēkādasha prayājān yajati pashumēva tat prayajats’ and Yadēkādashānuyāzān yazati pashumēra tadanuyazats’;–the presence of the particle era’ indicates emphasis, the senso being that it is the Ammal-offering only, not the Cake-offering” C L SÚTRA (2) [PORVAPAKSA–concluded]” THE PROCEDURE SHOULD BE DIFFERENT, ALSO BECAUSE OF THE MODIFICATION OF THE ACCESSORY AND THE TIME Bhasya "” Further, the Prayājas and Anuyājas connected with the Animal-sacrifice are all such as undergo modifications regarding Accessories and Time, for nstance, (A) at the Animal-offering, both the Prayājas and the Anuyājas are eleven in number,-w lule at the Cake-offering there is need for only five Prayājas and three Anuydjas,-the Anuyājas at the Animal-offering are performed with the Curd-Butter-Mixture, wlule the Cake-offering needs only ADHYAYA XII, PĀDA I, ADHIKARAŅA (1). 2255 Clarified Butter ;-(B) similarly thero 18 modification regarding Time also: The Prayājas connected with the Cake-offering are performed when the offering-substance is close at hand, while those connected with the Animal- offering are performed while the animal is actually standing there,—as laid down in the text. They offer the Prayājas over the standing animal’-Thus if both thee (Pravājas and Anuvājas) we e not done separately for the Cake-offering, they would not be done properly For thus reason also, there should be separate performance " SUTRA (5). [SIDDH INTA]—, FACT IT SHOULD BL ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH THE PROCEDURF OF THE MAIN OFFERING ITSELF, BECAUSE IT HAS BEIN ENJOINED IN THE MIDDLE OF THE PROCESS, SPECT- ALLY AS THF PURPOSE OF THE PROCEDURE IS NOT DISTINCT

Bhasya In fact, the procedure of the Cake-offering should not be performed soparatek, it should be accomplished through the Procedure of the Mam offering itself. - - the Procedure of the Animal offering itself would help the Cake- offering Why so?"-Because it has been enjoined in the middle of the Process, as a matter of furt, the Cake-offering has boon laid down in the middle of the process of the Ammal-offering, in the text-Aynisomīyasya rapayā pracharya aqnişomiyam pashupurodāshamē kādashakapālam nirvapatı”. “What if it is so ?"-It moans that the purpose of the Procedure is not distinct, the term ’tanträrtha’ stands for the purpose of the Procedure, 1 e, the help rendered by the subsidiaries,—and this romains non-distinct, 1e the same, in the case of the Animal-offering and the Cake-offering, house the condition of proximity is the same in both cases, the subsidiaries por- formed in connection with the Animal-offering are in proximity to the Cake- offering also, and by virtue of this proximity, they also help the Cake- offering,—like the Lamp, 10 just as the Lamp lighted in the house illummes the public road also Objection “The example cited is not appropriate, the help rendered by the Lamp is visible and is hence recognized by Direct Perception, the help rendered by the subsidiaries, on the other hand, is imperceptible, how can it be recognized ? " Answer This latter also is visible (cognisable) through the scriptures, and can be recognized on the authority of the scriptures, the scriptural text boaring on the case being They (the subsidiarios) should be per- formed as in the case of the Darsha-Purnanāsa sacrifices’ If, then, they are done as in the case of the Darsha-Purnamasa sacrifices’, why should they not help In the case of the Darsha-Purnamasa, they have rendered the help when performed at the same time and place and by the same performers as the Main sacrifice, so in the case in question also, they are2256 SHABARA-BHĀŞYA : performed in the same manner; and hence it follows that they render the same help here also. Says the Opponent’ The subsidiaries in the case in question are not quite like those in the case of the Darsha-Purnamasa; they have been performed at the Darsha-Purnamasa in connection with the Main sacrifices; here also they should be performed like that, they are however done, not in connection with the Cake, but in connection with the Animal; hence they cannot be regarded as done, in regard to the Cake, in the manner of the Archetype ‘.’ C The answer to this is as follows. In regard to the Archetype, the tenclung is not verbal, -there being no such declaration as that the sub- sidiaries should be porforined in reference to the Main Sacrifices’, in fact, it 18 so done simply because of the oxigencies of the situation, simply because it is desired to perform them in that manner,-what is done at the Archetype undor the stress of exigencies cannot be made adınıssible elsewhere (at the ectypes) by virtue of the General Law, because it is only the procedure of the action that is needed at these latter, hence only that much is brought in under the General Law which has been actually onjoined by a text, not anything beyond that Thus it is that, even though not performed in reference to the Mam Sacrifices, the subsidiaries may be regarded as por- formed ’m the manner of the Archotype’ -From all this we conclude that help is actually rendered by Prasanga (Extended Application) LI Opponent Such boing the case, thus ‘Prasanga’ is in no way different from ’ Tantra Not so, 717 what is common In the case of ‘Tantra’ is the subsidiary itself, whule in the case of ‘Prasanga”, it is the help rendered by the subsidiary that is common ‘, as a matter of fact, thus help too is not exactly common; what happens is that the help rendered to one benefits the other also . SUTRA (4) EVEN ON ACCOUNT OF MODIFICATION THERE WOULD BL. NO DIFFERENCE AS THE PURPOSE SERVED IS NOT MODIFIED

Bhasya "” It has been argued above that “the procedure should be different, also because of the modification of the Accessory and the Time (ST 2) Our answer to this is as follows Fren on account of a’ modification’ there would be no difference, as the purpose served is not modified, the ‘purpose served Is the help rewlered by the subondiaries,—this is not modified, it remains the same as at the Darsha Pūrnamāsa How do you know that “-Answer— The Prayājas und Anuyāgas that are performed are related to the Darsha- Pūmamāsa,–the names Prayāju and Anuyāza’ aro well known, all these come into the sacrifice in question by virtue of the General Law and are in close proximity, –it is also only reasonable that words should refer L ADHYAYA XII, PĀDA I, ADHIKARAŅA (1). · 2257 to things in the same context;-nor is it right to take a word as having more than one meaning;-hence it follows that the Prayājas and Anuyājas aro those related to the Darsha-Purṇamāsa, and that the help rendered by them is also related to the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa, in connection with the Darsha- Purnamasa, this help is well known, if the Prayājas and Anuyājus rendered help other than that related to the context (benefiting the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa), then, by reson of their doing what is not related to the context, they would not become admissible under the Genera’ Law; they would, in fact, be some- thing entirely new.-just like the anointing with Gungulu’ at the Satra. –If then, they did not come in under the no al Law, then one and the same text would have two functions of laying down the Prayājas, as well as this modication of the Prayājas–an et a single toxt, appearing only once, carnot enjon two things. If, under the circumstances, these Prayājas were something ent.rely new (unknown) then the dotails related to the Archetype would also come in by virtue of the General Law, and in that case it would not be possible for the number of oblations no the Vaishvadēva to become Thirty’, 8 dcsibed in the text-Nine Prayājas,- -nine Anuyājus,-two Āzyabhābqus,-eight offerings one takes out for Igm, and then ofters to the Iāgins,-in order to make up the number Thirty”. From all this it follows that, oven though thero is modification of the Accessorios, the help rendered to the Archetype remains unmodified; and this help, as rendered there, benefits the Cake-offering ulso, so that even on account of the modification of the Accessory and the Tune, there is to be no difference in the Procedure Thus it is that this help is sought after by both, the Animal-offering as well as the Cake-offering, at both of these the subsiduiries are performed in the manner of the Archetype’,—hence, by being performed once, they help both For what purpose then is the modification *” It is for the purposes of the Animal-offering, the said modification is found mentioned among the Prayājas and Anuyājas related to the Annal- offering, and the subsidiaries are not common to the Animal-offormg and the Cake-offoring, the fact of the matter is that these subsidiaries belong to the Animal-offering only, and yet even so, they benefit the Cake-offering also, on account of proximity, as already explamed above G Then again, even when the Anujājas are performed with the Curd- Butter-Merture, they may be regarded as performed with Clarified Butter’, because the mixed character does not destroy the nature of the Butter for instance, when a man is told to feed on milk, if the null given to him is mixed with sugar, that does not involve an infringeinent of the former statement, as mixed with the sugar also the mulk remuns milk all the same Similarly, when a man performs the eleven Prayagas, the fire of those that he perforins are those same that are related to the Archetype, and if the six others that he performs are other than those related to the Archetype, this latter act of his does not mean that the former fire have not been performed. So also if the Prayājas are performed while the Animal 18 standing there, they may be regarded as perforined in connection with the Cake, all that has happened is only that the original order of sequence has 2258 SHABARA-BHÄṆYA : been abandoned, but the order of sequence is only an accessory detail ;- and it is not right for the Main act to be repeated for the sake of an accessory detail, as the Main act cannot be under the influence of the Accessory Detail; It may be that the abandonment of the order of sequence necessitates an Explation, but there cannot be repetition of the Main act.-“In that case, the Expiation would have to be done -It is certainly done, the oblation offered with the mantra ‘Ayashchāgnē, otc’ being declared to be an expiation for all sins (of omission and commission)-Or even the Expiation may not be necessary, as the abandoning of the order is due to certain circumstances, Thus then there is no incongruity at all “3 SUTRA (5) ÁLSO BECAUSE IN THE CASE OF SOME, IT CANNOT BE DONE. Bhasya. 4 In the ease of some of the details, it is not possible for them to be done separately, as for mstance, the Bringing up of the Fire to the Platform, and the Tratopayana (Restricted Feeding) When the Platform has been set up once and remains undemolished, it cannot be set up again, for ቤ thing that hus been made once need not be made agam, so long as the ono made continues to exist —It might be argued that " ’ a second Platform can certainly be set up”-Thus would be sheer fool-hardiness; and soc dly, tho second one set up would be not quito straight (as the exactly straight position would be taken up by the Platform already in existence), and this would lead to a confusion of the quarters,–and it would also involve soparate alturs, which is not countenanced by the scriptures, and lastly, it would mean the abandonment of the principle that the subsidiaries should be performed at the same time and place and by the same performers as the Mam sucrifices -7 bus then the said Bringing up of the Fire bomg for the purpose of securing the Ahavaniya l’ure,–and thus having been secured by the first Bringing up,—it cannot he secured ovet agam m the saune manner in which it has been already secured -It might be argued that one can set up another Ahavaniya Fio”–But as a matter of fact. so long as the first Ahavaniya romains unextinguished, there can be no second Ahavaniya, becauso firstly, the Gathapatya Fire and the Ahuraniya Fire are both located in the same place—and if the Ahavaniya were removed, the Gärhapatya would be left alone, just as, when out of the Clarified Butter contamed in the Dhruvă- vesad, which is common to all offerings, the Clarified Butter for the purposes of the I pūmskuyāja has been taken out, what is left becomes useful for the offerings to other deitios,and secondly, the process suggested would bring about the anomaly of two separate Alturs, as in the previous case, and this would involve all those incongruities that have been pointed out above Sumlarly the low taken up once cannot be taken up agam, unless the former has been given up, and it cannot be given up until the final completion of the Mam sacrifice L ADHYAYA XII, PĀDA 1, ADHIKARana (1), SUTRA (6). ALSO BECAUSE THERE IS A TEXT INDICATING THE SAME FIRE Bhāṣya 2259 The following text shows that the Animal-offering and the Cake-offering are related to one and the same Fire Madhye’qnērā yahutirjuhoti, puroḍā- skākadik pashrākulishcha’ [ At the centre of the Fire, on offers the oblations of Clarified Butter, those of the ‘ake and thos of the Animal’] This meuns that there can be no soparate Bringing up of the Fre, from which it follows that the Procedure of the An mal-offering: applicable to (and helps) the Cake-offer ng * ADHIKARANA (2): The Two Ajyabhāga-offerings’ should be made in connection with the Cake offering”. SUTRA (7) ACCORDING TO JAIMINI, WHEN THERE IS POSSIBILITY OF THE EXTERNAL PROCEDURE COMING IN, THE INTERNAL PROCEDURE SHOULD BE EXCLUDED Bhāṣya In regard to the same Mont-cake’, there arises the following question -Should the Inyabhāga-offerings be made or not L [There is the distinct prohibition–‘These two Azyabhāqu offerings are not made at the Animal-sacrifice”, thus, when they are absent at the Anumal-sacrifice, they camot come into the Cake offering by Extended Application’ (Prasanga) by votue of the preceding dhakarana, hence, the conditions of the proceding Adhikarana not being fulfilled, the matter remains in doubt ] C It is remarked in thus connection, that what has got to be considered hero 19–Does the ‘General Law’ become set aside by the Declaration of Proceduro? Or the ‘Declaration of Procedure’ by the ‘Genoral Law’↑ -If the General Law’ is sot aside, then the Ajnabhāga-offerings should not be made, while if the Declaration of Procedure’ is set aside, then the said offerings should be made —What thon is the right course? • L "

The Purvapakea is as follows It is the General Law that is set aside.–Why? -Bocnuse the General Law 18 inferential (functioning in- directly) while the Declaration of Proceduro’ is directly perceptible, and what is perceptible is cortamly more authoritative than what is inferential, and the setting aside of the inferential is more reasonable than that of the perceptible Such being the case, the Aryabhāga-offerings should not be made, as they could come in only by virtue of the General Law, and thus, having been set aside in this case, is not operative at all " In answer to this we have the following Siddhanta -The opinion of the revered Teacher Jaimini is that the Aryabhaga-offerings should be made in the case in question —“Why “–Because when there is possibility of the external procedure coming in, the internal procedure should be excluded; in a case where the adopting of the action’s own procedure brings in the proce dure of another action, the former should be excluded, eg the procedure of the Animal-sacrifice becomes excluded in the case of the Prayājas related to the Cake offering, where however, no such external procedure is likely to come m, it is not right to exclude it, eg when Devadatta gets on to Yajñadatta’s conveyance, it is only Devadatta’s conveyance that goes away, not his clothes and ornaments-In the case in question, the adopting of the Ayabhagas does not bring in any part of the procedure of the Anunal-sacrifice, hence, it is not right to exclude it, honce, they should not be excluded As regards the argument that “the ‘Declaration of Proce- ADHYAYA XII, PĂDA I, ADHIKARAŅA (2). 2261 dure’ is directly perceptible”,-as a matter of fact, the Declaration of Procedure’ is not operative in this case at all; all that the said Declaration could do would be to bring in the subsidiaries, and the Meat-cake-offerings have all their subsidiaries in the subsidiaries of the Animal-sacrifice itself; hence, even though it is directly perceptible, it does not take in the Ã¡yabhāgas ; the Declaration of Procedure, as a rule, takes in only that subsidiary which is close by in the context,-the jyabhagas however are not present at the Animal-sacrifice at all, having bec preceded by the Prohibition ‘one should not offer the Aryabhāgas at the Animal-Picrifice or at the Soma. sacrifice. Then again, it has been already explained that the Declaration of Procedure takes in only such subsidiaries as are already there, while the General Law’ brings them into existence d also takes them in, hence, it 18 this later that is the more authoritative of the two. • ADHIKARANA (3): At the Soma-sacrifice, the Platform related to the Darsha shall not be erected. SUTRA (8) [PURVAPAKSA]“INASMUCH AS THEY SERVE DIFFERENT PURPOSES, THERE SHOULD BE ERECTION OF THE SECOND PLATFORM AT THE SOMA-SACRIFICE FOR THE ECTYPES OF THE DARSHA-PORNAMĀSA Bhāsya In connection with the Soma-sacrifice, there are certain rites related to the Darska-Pūmamāsa which are performed on the Major Platform.— In regard to tlus, we proceed to consider the following question- For the performance of these rites, shu uld another Platform be erected ?—or not? The Pūrrapaksa 19 as follows – A separato Platform should be erected, →why 1–because the General Law indicating the erection, the erection of such a Platform would be in accordance with that Law The Platform of the Soma-sacrifice itself would accornplish all that is necessary, through Prasanga (Extended Application)’ It could not accomplish it,-why ↑ because they serve different purposes, the two Platforms in question servo two entirely different purposes the one related to the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa is used for the secut mg and keeping of the offering-materials, while that related to the Soma is used for the moving about, so that in this case, there could be no extended application, as there is extended application’ only in cases where the subsidiary of the Original sacrifice serves the same purpose as the intervening subsidiary, as for instance the Prayājas related to the Animal sacrifice find extended application in the Cake-offerings This condition is not fulfilled in the case in question, hence the second Platform should be erected " A SUTRA (9) L [SIDDHANTA-AS A MATTER OF FACT, THERE SHOULD BE NO ERECTION, AS IT WOULD ONLY VITIATE (THE OTHER). Bhāṣya. As a matter of fact, the Platform related to the Darsha should not be erected at the Soma-sacrifice.” Why “-Because it would only vitrate the other, e if another Platform were erected, it would only mean that the Soma-Platform already erected is defective, and it would not accomplish any purpose of its own “It would serve the purpose of keeping the offering- materials “That however could very well be done on the Major Platform itself. But that is for a totally different purpose, as we have already pointed out “.-Even while serving that different purpose, it could certainly serve ADHYAYA XII, PĀDA I, ADHIKARANA (3). 2263 the purposes of a receptacle for the offering-materials–it has been laid down that the offering-material should be kept upon the Platform, the Major Platform also is a platform,—and there are no conditions laid down as that the materials should be kept on a Platform włuch sorves that purpose alone. -From all thus it follows that the Darsha-Platform should not be erected at the Soma-sacrifice ADHIKARANA (4): At the Soma-sacrifice, the oblations relating to the Savana-Animals, etc. should be offered with the Sruva and other implements used at the Darsha-sacrifice. SUTRA (10). [PURVAPAKSA]“IN REGARD TO THE IMPLEMENTS, THERE SHOULD BE ‘EXTENDED APPLICATION’, BECAUSE THEY ARE FOR THE PURPOSE OF OFFERING OBLATIONS Bhāsya. In connection with the Soma-sacrifice, there are certain rites related to the Darsha-Purnamasa which would appear to be connected with the Ladles and Cups used at the Soma-sacrifice, such rites for instance, as the ‘Sāvana Animal, the Savana Cakes’, the Sauma Cooked Rice’ • C In regard to these we proceed to consider the question-Should the oblations at these Rites be offered with their own Ladles and Cups ? Or with the Sruva and other implements used at the Darsha-sacrifice 46 The Purvapaksa is as follows In the case of implements, there should be’ Extended Application’ ;—why ?—because they are for the purpose of offering oblations, the implements in question only serve the purpose of the offering of oblations, and this purpose can be served by the said Cups and Ladles also ;-the Rites in question too, are included within the sphere of the Soma-sacrifice; hence, the oblations at these should be offered (as at the Soma) with the Cups and Ladles.” SŪTRA (11). [SIDDHANTA-THE RIGHT COURSE IS TO USE THE IMPLEMENTS IN QUESTION, AS THEY HAVE BEEN IN USE ALREADY, IT IS ONLY IF THEY COULD NOT BE USED THAT THERE COULD BE C EXTENDED APPLICATION’. Bhāṣya. The right course would be to use the implements used at the Darsha- Pūrnamāsa,—and it is with these that the oblations should be offered ;- why because they have been in use already; the implements in question are there, having been already used; it has been declared that “if they were to obtain the Soma before having taken up the Clarified Butter, they would destroy the sacrifice, and if they obtain the Soma after having taken up the Clarified Butter, then they would not destroy the sacrifice’; 20 that (for the taking of the Clarified Butter) first of all the aruva and other ADHYÄYA XU, PĀDA I, ADHIKARANA (4). L " 2265 implements of the Darsha have to be used,-they have to be washed and cleaned and then the Clarified Butter is to be taken up with them; hence, these implements are there already, having been used in connection with the Clarified Butter. It is only if they could not be used that there could be ’ extended application’; in a case where the subsidiary of the sacrifice included in the sphere of the Soma-sacrifice is one that has not been used, then alone is there an extended application of the subsidiary of the Soma-sacrifice, for serving the purposes of that subsiny, because it is only when one has not got the thing of his own tl. it he obtams it from another, it is only when Devadatta has not got his own convey aner ear at hand that he rides in Yagñadatta’s conveyance, if his own conveyance is at hand, he goes on his own; because the pleasure that he dern es from riding in anothor’s con- veyance 14 not ut l like that which he derives from riding in his own conveyance Suailarly, the excellence that is acquired by the Cakes through the use of the implements of the Darsha-ofice is not attamed through the use of the Cups and Ladles, because in the case of the former the articles are of wood used at the Ar hetype, and hence it is possible to perform the Washing and other Embellishments, in the case of the Cups and Ladles, on the other hand, they have to be omitted Further, those implements that are related to the Soma itself have no connection with the Cakes 44 + In case the unplements of the Darsha had not been used, would it be possible for the Cups and Ladies to come in by extended application”?” Not so, we reply, even so, what would cono in by extended applica- tion’ would be the implements of the Darsha itself There is extended application’ only in casos where the subsidiary performed in connection with the Main Sacrifice becomes performed (1e helpful) also for the other sacrifice, og when the Prayājas are performed in connection with the Animal-sacrifice, they help the Cake-offerings also. In the case in question however, if the Cups and Ladles are used, the others do not become used by that use, certainly when the Sonua is offered, it is not the Cakes that becomie offered. For these reasons, there can be no Extended Application’ in tlus case. “What happens then ?” We explain :—There would be extended application’ if they had not been in use, le if the use of the implements in question were not possible,— or if it were actually prohibited, then alone would there be an extended application’ (of the Soma-accessories) L Then again, the right course is that in the case in question, the Darsha- Implements should be used, not the Cups and Ladles (of the Soma).-” Oa what grounds would this be the right course ?"-The implements in question come into the Darsha-Purnamāsa in accordance with scriptural texts, and therefore they become transferred to the Cake-offering by the General Law. The touch of the scriptural text is quite distinct. On the other hand, in connection with no sacrifice has the offering of oblations been laid down as to be done with the Ladles and Cups; so that such offering could be made only if there were an actual need for doing it, when there is no verbal declaration to that effect, an act can be done only if there is actual need for it. 542266 SHABARA-BHĀṢYA : There is the following text wluch also indicates the use of the Darsha- implements in question at the Soma-sacrifice- Yunajmi të prthivīm jyotiṣā sahēti dhruvāmabhimrshati, yunajmi vāyunāntariksēna të saha tyupabhrtam, yunajmi vācham saha divů suryēnēti juhūm’ [where three implements are montioned—Dhruvā, Upabhuta and Juhu, all which are connected with the Darsha-sacrifice] " From all this it follow that at the Soma-sacrifice, the oblations should be offered with the implements in question. L ADHIKARANA (5): The Meat- ake’ shall not be cooked at the “Shāmitra Fire’. SÚTRA (12) THE MEAT-CAKE SHALL NOT BE COOKED AT THE SHAMITRA FIRE, AS THE OTHER HAS BEEN IN USE ALREADY Bhāṣya. In connection with the surne Cake, we proceed to consider the question– Is it to be cooked at the Shamitra Fire or at the Shālāmukhiya Fuo ? The same Principle The other bemg already in uso-18 applicable here also It has been laid down that the cooking of offering-materials should be done at the Garhapalya Fire, and this is already in uso, it having been declared that The Shālāmukhiya Fire itself becomes the Garhapatya after this’, hence, the cooking in question should bo dono at this Shālā- mukhiya Fire ADHIKARANA (6): At the Kauṇḍapāyināmayana’ the & Agnihotra-material’ should be cooked at the “Prājahita’ (Gārhapatya) Fire. SUTRA (13) THE COOKING OF THE AGNIHOTRA SHOULD NOT BE DONE AT THE SHALAMUKHIYA FIRE, BECAUSE THE PRĀJAHITA FIRE IS PRESENT. Bhasya In regard to the Agnihotra performed in connection with the Kaunda- pājināmuyana, we proceed to consider the question-Should the Material to be used therein be cooked at the Shālāmukhiya Fire " Or at the Prajahita Fire? Prajahita’ is the name given to the Garhapatya Fire by the ancient Teachers Hero also the same principle is applicable The cooking of offering- materials has been laid down as to be done at the Garhapatya;—this Gārha- patya, therefore, is in use there already,-it 18 only when something 18 not already in use that there can be extended application (Su. 12).—There are many explanations possible here -The Shalamukhiya comes in by virtue of the General Law,-in connection with the Jyotistoma, tlus same Shālāmukhiya has been declared to be the Garhapatya,-and indirectly through the General Law, this same Shälämukhiya comes on into the Kaundapayınamayana, while the cooking is indicated by Name as to be done at the Prājahita Fire (which is another name for the Garhapatya on which the Cooking of all materials has been laid down),-the Name is more authoritative than the General Law; hence, the cooking in question should be done at the Prājahita Fire. 1 C ADHIKARANA (7): The Vegetable-cakes’ should be pre- pared in a cart other than the two Havirdhana Carts’ that come in at the Jyotistoma. SUTRA 14). [PURVAPAKŞA]-“THE TWO HAVIRDHANA CARTS SHOULD SERVE THE PURPOSES OF THE PREPARATION, AS THEY HAVE BEEN ALREADY IN USE Bhasy After the two Fiavirdhānu Carts have been set up,-there follow certain sacrifees at which the su stance offered contains vegetable ingredients,~ such as, the Ment-cake-offering, the Savaniya-cakes, the Saumya-charu. In regard to these, we proceed to consider the question–Are these substances to be prepared in one of the two Havırdhāna Carts themselves ? Or should another cart be secured for that purpose? The Purvapaksa is as follows - The two Havirdhānu Carts should serve the purpose of the preparation, or one of them only Why ?-Because they have been in use already; the Havrdhāna Oart has been in use already, and it is quite capable of serving the purpose of preparing the substances in question ; under the circumstances, if another cart were to be secured for that purpose, it would be a superfluous act Hence, the substancos should be prepared with the help of one of the Havırdhāng Carts themselves (and no other cart is to be secured) " SUTRA (15). [SIDDHANTA]-AS A MATTER OF FACT, THERE CAN BE NO FULFILMENT (BY THAT MEANS), AS THE PLACE BEING DIFFERENT, THE MAIN SACRIFICE WOULD BECOME DEFECTIVE ;—AND THERE CAN CE G 1 BE EXTENDED APPLICATION ONLY WHEN IT CAUSES NO DEFECT. Bhasya, There can be no fulfilment of the preparation, by means of the Havirdhāna Carts; that is, the substances should not be prepared with the help of these carta Why” Because the Main sacrifice would become defective,— [on account of the place being different-the place’ of the preparation is as follows -The cart is placed behind the Garhapatya Fire and in front of the Iga, then the Priest gets upon its right wheel and makes the preparation there. Such being the place of the Preparation’, if the Preparation ware done on the Haverdhāna Cart, then, this Havirdhana Cart (which contains Soma-shoots), would have to be brought up to the place just described; and 2270 SHABARA-BḤĀṆYA : this would make the Main Soma-sacrifice defective, the erection and location of the Haverdhâna Carts have been made with suitable mantras and in accord- ance with certain strict rules, and all this would become nullified (by the removal of the Havirdhāna); it is possible that the erecting and locating might be done again; but this would involve a repetition not sanctioned by the scrip- tures —As a matter of fact, it is only when it causes no defect in the Main act, that’ Extended Application’ inay be right; because it is the character of the Main act from which all the rest derive their sustenance, each according to the texts bearing upon it, all the rest being, as they are, entirely dependent (on something else) If, for some reason, the purposes of these subordinate factors are not accomplished by the means laid down in the scriptures, then those purposes might well be left unfulfilled, or any other means might be employed, but they could not accomplish their purposes by upsetting the Main sacrifice – “But why cannot the Preparation be made at the very place where the Haverdhāna has been located?"-In that case the said acts (involved in the Preparation’) would become defective” That may be so, thoso nets are subordinate factors and as such they must follow the predominant factor just as it happens to be, eg. the Meat-cake follows the Prayājas of the Animal-sacrifice, even though these latter appear at a different time “The answer to this is as follows:-In the case cited, it is right that It should be so, because the Prayājas have been performed already, and what has been already done cannot be done again simply to preserve the order of sequence (of something else) In the case in question however, the Preparation is still to be made, and if it is possible to make it fully equipped with all its details, it should be made as so equipped;-as a matter of fact, it 18 possible to make it so equipped by securing another cart; hence, it follows that the said Preparation should not be done in one of the Havirdhāna Carts. L SUTRA (16). ALSO BECAUSE WE FIND THE CARTS’ SPOKEN OF (IN THE PLURAL NUMBER). Bhasya We find a plurality of Carts spoken of in the text—’ Anāmsı pravartayantı " [‘They set up several Carts’].-From this also it follows that another cart (other than the two Havırdhāna Carts) should be secured. C ADHIKARANA (8): At the Prayaniya and other offerings, there should be separate Keeping of Vigil’ in con- ’ nection with the Initiation. SUTRA (17). THAT WHICH IS CONNECTED WITH THA’ [CANNOT APPLY], ON ACCOUNT OF THE DIFFERENC Bhasya זיך . & InConnection with the Soma-sacra, the keeping of Vigil’ has been and down as to be done at the time of io Initiation-’ Vām prathamām rātrim jāga ti, etc In connection with the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa ulso, for some people the said ‘Vig 1’ has been laud down as to be done on the Arpava- sathya Day This Keeping of the Vigil becomes admissible, under the General Law, to the Prāyaniya’ and other offerings (which have the above Mam Sucrifices for their Archetypes). C Ta regard to this–[the question being- Does the Vigil kept at the time of the Initiation serve the purposes of the Prāyaniya and other mmor sacrifices— or should a separate Viqd be kept m connection with these latter 7-the Pūrvapaksa is that “the l′igil that has been kept at the tune of the Initiation will, by Extended Application’, serve the purposes of these minor sacrifices [and hence it should not be done separately]” –Tu answer to this, we have the following Siddhanta —That which is connected with that,- e the Vigil kept in connection with the Initiation-cannot have its application extended to other arts;-why because of the difference in time, if, as a matter of fict, the Vigil is kept for the purpose that there may be no carelessness in the safe kooping of all sacrificial accessories, then what are so guarded by the Vigil kept at the time of Initiation are only those accessories that are there at the time, so that no other become guarded by that Vigil, hence for the purpose of the guarding of the other accessores of the Prayaniya and other munor sacrifices, the Vigil should be kept sopurately at the time of the Auparasathya -Even if the Vigil were mount to serve only an unseen purpose (and not that of guarding the sacrificial accessories), then also the Aupavasathya night would be the occasion for the keeping of the Vagd, and when the occasion is there whatever is due to be done on that occasion should be done -From all this it follows that in connection with the Prāyaniya and the rest, the Vigil should be kept separately ADHIKARANA (9): At separate Altars, the Mantras should be recited separately. SÚTRA (18). MANTRAS ALSO (SHOULD BE RECITED SEPARATELY), AS THEY HELP DIRECTLY. Bhasya At the Varunnpraghisa sacrifices, there are two separate Altars (one for the Adhvaryu and another for the Praprasthātr), in connection with these there are certain Mantras that operate upon them directly, along with the Taking up of Clarified Butler, Besprinkling and Touching The question that arises 18-Should these Mantras be recited in common’ for the two Altars or separately? This discussion bears, not upon Prasanga (the subject-matter of the present discourse), but upon Tantra and Āvāpa (the subject of the previous discourses). The Purvapaksa is that “the Mantras should be recited 17. common’, for the purpose of honouring the Declaration of Procedure” In answer to this, the Siddhanta is as follows :-The reciting of Mantras also-in connection with the Taking up of Clarified Butter, etc.-should be done separately;-why-because they help directly; the Mantras in question are all such as help directly, as they signify the action that is present at the time, as a matter of fact, the Adhvaryu and the Pratiprasthātr (who are in charge of the two Altars severally) come up in connection with separate actions, hence the Mantras should be recited separately. Further, it is going to be explained under Su 12. 3 24, that all the agencies operating upon actions end with the Mantra, and that being so, a Mantra must be regarded as subservient to the purposes of that Act upon which it operates; and by virtue of this differentiating condition, there should be repetition of Mantras. ADHIKARANA (10): There shall be no Agnyanvādhāna ’ ’ at the Dikṣaniya and other sacrifices. [The next few Adhikaranas up to Adhi. 18 deal with those Isfis that form part of the Soma-sacrifice, but which have the Daraka-Pūrnamāsa for their Archetype.] SUTRA (19) AT THE SUMA-SACRIFICE, THERE IS NO ÁGNYANVÄDHÄNA’, AS IT IS FOR 6 THE PURPOSE OF MAINTENANCE Bhāsya. In course of the Soma-sacrifice there are certain Istis, like the Dikṣaniyā ; at hese the rite of Agnyanvādhāna’ (Reinstallation of Fire) becomes ad- missible under the General Law The question is- Should this Rite be performed or not? The Purvapakça is that” it should be performed, because only by so doing would the General Law be obeyed ’ In answer to thus, we have the following Siddhanta -The Agnyunvādhāna should not be performed at the Diksaniyä, etc.—why –because it is for the purpose of maintenance, the Agnyanıīdhāna is meant to be done for the purpose of maintaining (keeping up) the Fire that has been brought up, that rite has been already performed in connection with the Fire brought out for the performance of the Soma-sacrifice,—and the Fire has been main- tamed by that means; there can be no maintaining of what has been maintained already.-“But that is done without Mantras “-True, it is done without Mantras, but it has been doue ull the same; and what has been done once need not be done again, only for the purpose of reciting the Mantras -From all this it follows that the Aqryanvūdhāna should not be done at the Dikṣaniya and other Istia ADHIKARANA (11): At the Dikṣaniya and other Istis there 4 is to be no Taking of the Vow’. L SÚTRA (20). So ALSO THE Vow’, BECAUSE IT HAS BEEN ALREADY TAKEN Bhasya. At the said Diksaniyā and the rest, there is admissible, under the General Law, the taking of the vow’ which has been enjoined in connection with the Darsha-Purnamāsa [The question being as to whether or not tlus vow should be taken at the Dikṣaniya, etc] the Siddhanta is that, like the Agnyanıādhāna, this vow should not be taken,—because it has bren already taken, that which has been taken and not yet finishod cannot be taken up again, the act of taking up’ consists in obtaining what has not been obtained, and hence it cannot be done to what has been already obtained L SUTRA (21) ALSO BECAUSE OF INCOMPATIBILITY. Bhāsya. L . The words pronounced by the person taking up the vow aro- -Ayne vratapati aratañcharışyāmı’ which contains the verb in the Future tense, and thus would be incompatible with the row if it were already present SUTRA (22) “IT MAY BE LIKE TRUTH-TELLING —1 THIS IS URGED [then the answer is as below] Bhāsya 4. Say the Opponent—‘Why can it not be like Truth-telling* *–Just as the vow of Truth-telling, being a man’s duty, continues throughout life, and yet it is taken at the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa " SÚTRA (23). THAT CANNOT BE, BECAUSE OF THE CONNECTIONS BEING DISTINCT. Bhāṣya. The case of the row m question is not analogous to that of telling’, because of the connections being distinct; in the case of Truth. C Truth- F ADHYAYA XII, PĀDA I, ADHIKARAṆA (11) 2275 telling’, there are two distinct connections that of the Man, and that of the sacrifice, so that having been previously taken up as pertaming to the Man (as hus general duty), it becomes taken up again in connection with the sacrifice.—“ In the case in question also, there is distinctness of connection; having been taken up previously in connection with the Soma-offering, it may be taken up again in connection with the Tsti”.–In the case in question, there is no need for ’taking up the vow’ aguu,–as that which has been done already in connection with the Soma-sacfice will accomplish its purpose at the other sacrifico also, through Extended Application ‘.-“In the other case (of Truth-telling) also, the purpose could be accomplished in the same manner -It might accomplish it if it were previously known that it is for the purpose of accomplishing a certain desi 2, 84 a matter of fact however, this fact 19 recogni? d onl in connection with the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa itself (not before that). w’uk in the case in question, thus fact has been already recognized in connection with the Archetypal sacrifice. Henco the citing of the case of ‘Truth tlling’ cannot sorve as an instance in point. " The necessity of the recognition of the accessory (of Truth telling, e.g.) serving the purposes of the Mam action los in the fact of that being the determining factor m the deciding of the Exact Expiation;-as explamed undo Sutra 3 4 12-13ADHIKARANA (12): At the ‘Istis’, there is to be no ‘Agnyan– vādhāna’, even for purposes adopting the Deity. SUTRA (24). THE PREVIOUSLY MENTIONED AOT, EVEN FOR PURPOSES OF ADOPTING (THE DEITY), [SHALL NOT BE DONE], AS THE IȘTI ITSELF SERVES THAT PURPOSE. Bhasya. It has been explained (under Adhikarana 10 above) that the ‘Agnyanvā- dhana’ already done in connection with the Sorra-sacrifice, accomplishes the same purpose, through Extended Application’, at the Istis also. This is now objected to-“The Extended application spoken of in the previous Adhikarana has been in reference to that Agnyanvādhāna which is done for the purpose of maintaining the Fire; as a matter of fact, however, the Agnyanvādhāna is done, not only for the purpose of maintaining the Fire, but for that purpose of maintaining the Fire, as also for the purpose of adopting the Deity; we read in connection with the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa— ‘Mamagnē varcho vihavēşvastu iti pūrvamagnum gṛhņāti, dēvatā ēva tatpūrvēd- yurgrhitvā shvobhūtē yajatë ’ ;—though the Agnyanvādhāna for the purpose of maintaining the Fire may come in, through Extended Application’, from that performed in connection with the Soma-sacrifice, yet that which is done at the Darsha-Purnumasa for the purpose of adopting the Derty should have to be done at the Iştır” 1 of In answer to this, we have the following Siddhanta :-The view set forth above is not right; as a matter of fact, that Agnyanvädhana which is done for the purpose of adopting the Deity also would be secured through ‘Extended Application (and hence should not have to be done again).-Why ?- Because the Igh itself serves that purpose; in connection with the Soma- sacrifice also, the Dīkṣaṇīyā Iştı is found mentioned as serving the purpose adopting the desty-Agnavarenavamēkādashakapālam nirvapēt dikṣṣya- mānaḥ, agnıḥ prathamo dēvatānām viṣnuh paramah, yadagnāvarṣṇavamēkā, dashakapālam nirvapatı dēvatā yajñañcha tadubhayataḥ parryrhya dikṣate’.- This same Işti, thus serving the purpose of adopting the deity at the Soma- sacrifice, will serve the same purpose for the Ists also, by ’extended application’. SUTRA (25) “IT WOULD BE LIKE THE ACCESSORIES 22 IF THIS IS URGED [then the answer is as in the next Sūtra]. Bhāṣya. Says the Opponent-” The purposes of the Istis would not be served in the manner suggested; the Dikṣaṇiyd-Işți subserves the purposes of the ADHYAYA XII, PĀDA I, ADHIKARAṆA (12), 2277 Main sacrifice, and as such it operates towards the adopting of the deity of the Main sacrifice;-the deities of the subsidiaries however, which are more accessories, are not included under that adoption ;-hence for the purposes of adopting these deities, the Agnyanwadhāna related to the Darsha- Pūrnamāsa should be performed in connection with the Istis.” SUTRA (26). NOT SO, BECAUSE THERE IS THE VAISHADEVA’ (RELATED TO AFL DEITIES’). C Bhāṣya. The said Aryanvidhāna should n be performed; the purpose of adopting the deity will be accor aplished by the Dıkşaniya Iştı itself, through ‘Extended Application’ -“But it has been pointed out that the Diksaniyā serves the purpose of adopting the deity of the Main sacrifice only “-By subserving the purpose of the deity of the Main sacrifice, it would also take in the deities of the subsidiaries” How so !"-Because there is the varshva- dēra, in connection with the Soma-sacrifice, there is the Grahayaga, which is ‘varshvadēva ‘, in the sense that all deities (vishvē dēvāḥ) are sacrificed to in this sacrifice, and the deities of the subsidiaries also are included among theni ; so that these also become adopted. Hence there is no need for the performance of the Agnyanvudhāna in connection with the Ights, for the purpose of adopting those deities. SUTRA (27). [Objection]” THERE SHOULD BE NEED FOR IT, AS THEY HAVE BEEN NAMED. “5 Bhāṣya. There should need for the Agryanvādhāna, as it is necessary to adopt the deities of the subsidiaries through the Agnyanvādhāna in connection with the Ighe; because as a matter of fact, those deities cannot be taken as ‘adopted’ on the ground that sacrifices are offered to all deities’, because un reality, at the said Graha-yaga, sacrifices are not offered to all dentes, the term ‘Vishvë- dēvaḥ’ stands, not for all (vishvē) derties (dēvāḥ), but for a definite group of derties, consisting of the Sadhyas, the Rudras and the Vasus.-How do you know that ?-Because they have been named; the deities meant have been actually named in the text-Agnar varubhiḥ, somo raudraiḥ, indro marud- bhiḥ, varuna adityarh, brhaspatervishvedevath; where it appears that the · Vishvēdēvas’ are entities different from the Vasus and other well-known deities. If all derties had been spoken of by means of the term ‘vishvēdēva’, then those deities would not have been different from the well-known deities, Vasu and the rest. Hence we conclude that the term ‘vishvē-děva’ denotes only a well-defined group (of deities).—Such being the case, the deities of subsidiaries 2278 SHABARA-BR İŞYA: could not be included under that name; hence for the adopting of those, the performance of the Agnyanvādhāna would be necessary.” SÜTRA (28) NOT SO, BECAUSE IT SERVES THE PURPOSE OF INDICATING AN EXCELLENCE. Bhāṣya. C It cannot be as suggested-Why ?-Because it serves the purpose of indicating an excellence; 1.e. the above-quoted description (enumeration) of the Vishvēdēvas cannot be regarded as indicating a group of dertres; the description is meant to be an indication of excellence,-1.e. a praise of Brhaspati, the sense of the praise being that- Agni is accompanied by the Vasus only, Soma, by the Rudras only,-Indra, by the Maruts only, and Varuna, by the Adityas only; but Brhaspati is accompanied by all the deities, those named here as well as others’. This praise is just like the praise of the king in the words ‘The Army-commander has come in with his paid army and will fight along with his own army,–but the King is accompanied by all armies, those mentioned as well as others’.-Further, under the inter- pretation suggested, it would be necessary to assume a group of deities bearing the name ‘T’ishvēdēva’, while all deities are understood to be actually denoted by that name 6 From all thus it follows that the adopting of the subsidiary deities also 18 acomplished by means of the Dikṣaniya, through Extended Application’, and hence the Agnyanvādhāna related to the Darsha-Purnamasa should not be performed in connection with the Istis. " C ADHIKARANA (13): At the Istis, the Patnisannahana’ (Dressing up of the Lady) shall not be performed. SUTRA (J) THE DRESSING UP ALSO SHOULD NOT BE DONE], AS IT HAS BEEN DUNE ALREADY Bhāṣya. The ‘Sannahana’ (‘Dressing up’) of the sacrificer’s Lady has been laid down in connection with the Darsha-Purnamasa, in the text’ Dresses up the Lady with the Yoktra’. Under the General Law, this should be done at those Isti rites that are performed in connection with the Soma-sacrifice. [The question arising as to whether or not this Dressing up should be per- formed at these rites] the Siddhanta is that it should not be done ;-why? -because it has been done already; at the time of the Initiation, the Dressing up of the Lady for the purposes of the Soma-sacrifice has been already done, as laid down in the text’ He dresses up the Lady with the Yoktra and the Initiated Sacrificer with the Mekhala, with a view to joining the two’. This dressing up with the Yoktra is for the purpose of lending support to the Dress; and when this has been done in connection with the Soma-sacrifice itself, it will continue to serve that purpose till the completion of the sacrifice along with its subsidiaries, which latter also it will benefit by ‘Extended Application’. ADHIKARANA (14): At the Istis there need not be ‘Feeding upon wild-growing Things’. SUTRA (30). THE EATING OF WILD-GROWING THINGS’ SHOULD NOT BE DONE; AS THERE IS INJUNCTION OF ANOTHER. Bhāṣya 2 In connection with the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa, the eating of wild- -growing things’ has been laid down, in the text-Yadaranyānı ashnāts, etc., etc’. + 4 This becomes admissible into the Prayaniya and other Istis, under the General Law. [The question arising as to whether or not this eating should be done at these Iṣṭis] the Siddhänta is as follows -Even though it is indicated by the General Law as admissible, it should not be done;-why-because there is injunction of another. The Eating of wild-growing things’ that has been enjoined in connection with the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa is meant to be for the purposes of subsistence;-in connection with the Soma-sacrifice also, means of subsistence have been laid down-‘The Brahmana shall live on milk, the Kṣatirıya on gruel and the Vaishya on Curdled Milk’; this also serves a visible purpose and hence is regarded as a means of subsistence; of these two means of subsistence, that connected with the Soma-sacrifice 18 found to be directly enjoined, and it is also the more important of the two,-hence this must be done; and when the subsistence has been secured by this means, it helps the other subsidiary rites also, through ‘Extended Application’; hence the other means of subsistence becomes excluded. ADHIKARAŅA (15): At the Ists there should be ‘Eating of < Remnants’. SÚTRA (31) IF IT BE URGED THAT THE SAME SHOULD BE THE CASE WITH THE EATING OF RE INANTS THAT IS NOT SO, BECAUSE THAT IS FOR A CC DIFFERENT PURPOSE Bhāsya In connection with the Dursha-Pūrnamāsa, there is the Eating of Remnants, Ida and the rest-This is indicated by the General Law as ad- missible at the Ists performed in course of the Soma-sacrifice. It may be argued that, as the ‘Eating of wild-growing things’ has been set aside by the means of subsistence laid down in connection with the Soma-sacrifice, so this Eating of Remnants also should be set aside (as this also is only a means of subsistence) “.-The answer to this is that it is not so ;-why ?-because that is for a different purpose; the Eating of Remnants’ is not meant to be a means of subsistence; it is not for the purpose of sustaining the body; it is in fact meant to be an embellishment (of the substance), because the substance in question is only the remnant of what has been used, and because all these Eatings are spoken of by means of words with the Accusative Ending, in such texts as Yajamānapañchamā ṛtvyjaḥ iḍām bhakṣayanti’,–therefore in the case in question, the Eating of Remnants’, should be done. C 55 ADHIKARANA (16): At the Istis, there is to be no gift of the C Anvāhārya’. SUTRA (32). THE ‘PURCHASE’ ALSO (SHOULD NOT BE DONE), AS THEY ARE ALREADY ENGAGED. Bhāsya. In connection with the Darsha-Purnamasa, the Anvähärya-gift has been laid down as the ‘purchase-price’ (payment for services), the General Law indicates thus as to be done at the Istas performed in course of the Soma-sacrifice. [The question arising as to whether or not that gift should be made at these Istrs] the Siddhanta is that it should not be made ;- why ?—because they are already engaged, the Priests concerned have been already engaged and their services secured by the payment of the ‘pur- chase-price’ in connection with the Soma-sacrifice,-in accordance with the text The sacrificial Fee is 1200’-And the subsidiaries are always performed at the sarne place and time by the same performers as the Mam sacrifice; hence the subsidiary Istis in question have to be performed by those same Priests that have been engaged for the Soma-sacrifice; conse- quently there can be no separate ‘purchase-price’ to be paid in connection with the subsidiaries; hence the Anvāhārya-gift has to be omitted ADHIKARAṆA (17): At the Istis, the Eating of Remnants’ shall be done as serving the purposes of Embellishment’. " SUTRA (33). 4 [PURVAPAKSA]—“THE EATINGS OF R MNANTS ALSO SHOULD BE SIMILARI Y OMITTED -IF THIS IS URGED [then the answer is as in the next Sūtra]. Bhāṣya. It might be argued that “the Eatings of Remnants also should be omitted at the Istis, just as the Anvāhārya-gift is omitted 77 Thus question is raised on the basis of the possible notion that the Eating of Remnants is by way of ’l’urchase-price’ (for services rendered) [which alone would make it subject to the conclusion regarding the Anvāhārya]. SUTRA (34) [SIDDHANTA]-IT IS NOT SO, BECAUSE THOSE ARE CONNECTED WITH THE C ACTIONS. Bhāsya. The Eatings of Remnants should not he omitted, because they are not meant to be payment for services rendered; as a matter of fact, those Eatings of Remnants have been laid down as to be done after the completion of the functions of the priests whose services had been secured by the gift of the Anvāhārya, nor are these Eatings’ sufficient as price for securing of the servicos [Read ’na chālamānamanāya’]; hence these Eatings are not meant to be the ‘price’ of services rendered, they are meant to be embellishments of the Remnants of substances used; and for this purpose they have to be done (at the Igtis in question also). ADHIKARANA (18): At the Istis, there should be ‘appoint- ment’ of the Hotr Priest. · SUTRA (35). INASMUCH AS THERE IS APPOINTMENT’ AFTER COMMENCEMENT, THERE SHOULD BE APPOINTMENT’ OF THE HOTR-PRIEST AT EACH RITE. Bhāṣya In connection with the Darsha-Purnamasa, the ‘appointment’ of the Hotṛ-priest has been laid down, in the text’ Agnirdēvo etc.’,-the General Law indicates the admission of thus at the Işta performed as parts of the Soma-sacrifice.-But in connection with the Soma-sacrifice itself, the ’ appoint- mont of the Hotr has been laid down separately, in the text’ Agnirhotā, etc…… hotāram vṛnītē”. • In regard to this we proceed to consider the question-At the Lates in question, should or should not there be the appointment of the Hotṛ’ that has been laid down in connection with the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa ? The Purvapakea is as follows-“It should not be done;—why ?— The Appointment is made for the purpose of securing the man’s services;— the Hotr’s services for the performance of the entire Soma sacrifice along with its accessories have been already secured by the appointment’ in connection with the Soma-sacrifice itself,-there can be no need for the securing of the services of one whose services have been already secured; hence the Appointment in question should not be done.” In answer to the above, we have the following Siddhanta,—Inasmuch as there 18 Appointment after commencement, there should be appointment of the Hoty-priest at each Rite,it is not right that the Appointment made in connection with the Soma-sacrifice will serve, through Extended Applica- tion’, the purposes of that Appointment also which is related to the Darsha- Pūrnamāsa ;—as a matter of fact, there is Appointment after commencement,- 1.8. it is after the performance has commenced that the appointment related to the Darsha-Pūrṇamāsa 19 made,-hence it cannot be meant for securing the services of the Priest;-in fact it is meant to be a mere act by itself; hence if it were not done, the performance would be defective to that extent. Hence the Appointment should be done separately with each of the Rites in question. SÜTRA (36). " “THE BRAHMAN-PRIEST ALSO -IF THIS BE URGED [then the answer is as in the next Sutra]. Bhasya. The Opponent says “If it is your view that, inasmuch as the Appoint- ment is done after commencement, the Appointment of the Hoty should ADHYAYA XII, PĪDA I, ADHIKARAṆA (18). 2285 be done with each Rite, then, inasmuch as the Brahman-Priest also 18 appointed after the performance has commenced, at the time of the bringing up of the Pranītā-vessel, it follows that the appointment of this Priest also is an act by itself and as such this also should be done with each Rite; –or you should point out some difference between the two cases (of the Hotr and the Brahman).” SUTRA (37). THAT CANNOT BE; BECAUSE IN REALITY, THE APPOINTMENT COMES FIRST; AS IT IS FOR THAT Bhāṣya 4 The appointm at of the Brahman-Prut should not be done at the Rites in question.—Why ?-Because the appointment comes first; it is true that the appointment of the Brahman comes after the commencement of the Per- formance; but prior to this appointment, the character of Brahman- Priest’ is not thore at all, in fact all the functions of the Brahman come after his Appointment; hence the appointment which is for the purpose of those functions must be regarded as subserving a sacrifice, and not an act by itself; it servos in fact the purpose of securing the services of the Priest; his services however have been already secured by means of his appoint- ment’ done in connection with the Soma-sacrifice ;-hence there need be no further appointment of that Priest (in connection with the Istis) SUTRA (38). C “IT RELATES TO WHAT HAS BEEN LAID DOWN “,-IF THIS BE URGED [then the answer is as in the next Sūtra]. Bhāṣya. The following argument might be put forward-“The making of the Platform has been laid down as to be done on the Aupavasathya Day in connection with the Darsha-sacrifice, in the text-At the Darsha-sacrifice, on the previous day, he makes the Platform’,-at this the commencement of the measuring out of the Platform is done by the Brahman-priest; so that the Brahman-priest also is one whose appointment (like that of the Hotr) is made after the commencement of the Performance SUTRA (39). NOT SO; BECAUSE THERE IS NO DECLARATION. Bhāṣya What has been laid down as to be done at the Darsha-sacrifice, on the previous day, 18 the making, not the measuring out, of the Platform, as there is no declaration; the ‘adopting’ is done after the Brahman-priest has been ‘appointed’ in its own time; as the ‘Appointment’ is for the purposes of the sacrificial performance.- “But the measuring out of the Platform is done before its making, and there also the start is to be made by the Brahman. priest.“2286 L SHABARA-BHĀṢYA: 4 That is true; in that case here is another answer to the objection:- In the context of the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa, the making of the Platform has been laid down as to be done after the securing of the offering-materials ;- the Appointment of the Brahman-priest also has been laid down as to be done before the functions of that Priest begin; and as this must serve a visible purpose, it is taken as serving the purpose of securing the services of the Priest. Such being the case, at the Darsha-sacrifice, the making of the Veda is anticipated’ in obedience to the direct declaration to that effect; and when this ‘making’ has been anticipated’, the ‘measuring out’ 18 also ‘anticipated’,-so also its commencement, as also the appointment of the Brahman-priest; because accessories follow the time and place of their Primaries. Under the circumstances, at the Paurnamasa sarrifice, the appointment of the Brahman-priest is done at the time of the bringing up of the Pranita, while at the Darsha-sacrifice, it is done on the previous day; in both cases, before the functions of the Priest have commenced. Hence It follows that in both cases the Appointment serves the purpose of securing the services Consequently this appointment of the Brahman-priest need cut be done at each Rite, the services of the Brahman-priest having been already secured by the Appointment done at the Soma-sacrifice SUTRA (40). 33 “SO SHOULD IT BE IN THE CASE OF THE HOTR ALSO -IF THIS IS URGED [then the answer is as given in the next Sutra]. Bhāṣya. Says the Opponent-“If it is your view that-if the Appointment of the Brahman comes before the commencement of the Performance,–and before his Appointment there is nothing to be done by that priest,-hence the Brahman-priest cannot be one whose appointment has been already made’, then the same should be the case with the Hotr also, for the Hotr also there is nothing to do before his appointment; and his appointment also is not an act by itself.” L SÚTRA (41) NOT SO BECAUSE OF CONNECTION WITH ACTION. Bhāsya. As a matter of fact, even before his Appointment, the Hoir is connected with the definite action of Reciting the Samidhēni verses, -as laid down in the text Before being appointed, he recites the Samidhēnis ‘.-From this it is clear that the Appointment of the Hotr is for an unseen purpose; hence it should be done at the Dikṣaniya and other Istis in question. As for the Appointment of the Brahman-priest however, it is for a visible purpose; and as this purpose has been served by the Appointment at the Soma-sacrifice, the Appointment should not be done at the Istre in question. € ADHIKARANA (19): At the Atithya-Isti, the Besprinkling” etc. of the Grass are not to be done in connection with each Rite. [See in this connection Sutras 4 2. 29-30.] SUTRA (42). [PURVAPAKŞA—“IN CONNECTION WIT THE INJUNCTION RELATING TO THE SACRIFICE, AS THE ACT DONE TO THE ESTABLISHED ENTITIES ARE DISTINT, THEY SHOUL BE PERFORMED IN CON- NECTION WITH FACH RITE Bhāṣya In connection with the Soma-sacrifice, we read- The grass used at the Aluthyā is also that of the Upasads and of the Agnisomiya’,-at this there are certain acts done to the entity in the shape of the Chopped Grass,- such as Washing, Removal of Tips, Sprinkling of the Roots In regard to these there arises the question-At the Atthya and other Iştis, where the performances are distinct, are these acts to be performed separately with each performance? Or the other performances are helped, through Extended Application’, by the act that has been performed in connection with the Atthga itself? C The Purvapaksa is as follows -“In connection with the Injunction relating to the Sacrifice,- -e. the injunction relating to the Atthya,-in the form ‘The grass used at the Atthya is also that of the Upasads’–the act that is done to the established entity should vary with each performance, as the rites of the Atthya and the rest have distinct performances of their own; and in regard to this we perceive the peculiarity that the Washing and other acts done at the performance of one Rite are subservient to that Rite; con- sequently, with every other performance, they should be repeated In this way there is to be repetition of each of the acts. There can be no Extended Application in this case, because neither the Upasads nor the Agnizomiya are included in the Procedure of the Anthya.” SUTRA (43) [SIDDHANTA]-AS A MATTER OF FACT, IT IS NOT SO, BECAUSE IT HAS BEEN ALREADY DONE, SPECIALLY AS THERE IS DECLARATION OF THAT. Bhāsya As a matter of fact, the acts of Washing, etc should not be done with each rite, why t-because it has been already done, 1.0. these acts have been 2288 CE SHABARA-BHAṢYA: already done to the Grass at the Atthya; and as the Grass has become duly embellished by that, there can be no need for the performance of these acts again.- But Embellishments subserve the purposes of Rites, and in this case the Rites are different, so that the Embellishments must appertain to that Rite alone in connection with which they are performed."-The answer to this is that though the Embellishments are subservient to the Rites, they do not become related to any one Rite directly, like the Askandapähkä (7); in fact, they become so related only indirectly through the Grass; 1.8. they become related to that Rite to which the Grass belongs. Now in the case in question, the Grass is common to the Atithya, the Upasada and the Agnişomiya - “How do you know that?"-There is declaration of that; 1.8. what the declaration the Grass at the Atithya is also that of the Upasads and the Agnişomiya’ lays down is the fact of the Grass being common to the three Rites, and not the transference of any accessory details.
